title.zh: 卷510 列傳二百九十七 列女三
title.raw: 卷510 列傳二百九十七 列女三

sentences.zh: 韋守官妻梁，長清人。

translations.literal: Liang, the wife of Wei Shouguan, was a native of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was the wife of Wei Shouguan, from Changqing.

sentences.zh: 明季飢，女未行，從父流轉河南，婢於富室。

translations.literal: In the famine at the end of the Ming, the girl had not yet married; she followed her father and drifted to Henan, where she served as a maid in a wealthy household.
translations.idiomatic: During the famine at the close of the Ming, before she had married, she followed her father to Henan and was indentured as a servant in a rich family.

sentences.zh: 及笄，主為擇婿，梁泣言幼嘗受韋氏聘，死，不敢別嫁。

translations.literal: When she came of age, her master chose a husband for her; Liang wept and said that in childhood she had received betrothal from the Wei family, and that if he died she would not dare marry another.
translations.idiomatic: When she reached marriageable age, her master sought a match for her, but Liang tearfully declared that she had been betrothed to the Wei clan as a child and that, even if her betrothed died, she could not marry anyone else.

sentences.zh: 主使求得守官，守官迎以歸。

translations.literal: The master had someone seek out Shouguan; Shouguan welcomed her and took her home.
translations.idiomatic: The master sent men to find Wei Shouguan, who came and brought her home as his bride.

sentences.zh: 已而守官卒，家人欲使別嫁，樑自沉大清河，救，不死。

translations.literal: Before long Shouguan died; the family wished her to remarry, and Liang threw herself into the Daqing River; she was rescued and did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shouguan died. When the family tried to marry her off again, Liang drowned herself in the Daqing River but was rescued and survived.

sentences.zh: 乃自治棺，曰：「有欲娶我，以此畀之！

translations.literal: She then made her own coffin, saying, "Whoever wishes to marry me, let him take this!"
translations.idiomatic: She then had a coffin made for herself, saying, "Whoever wants to marry me may have this!"

sentences.zh: 」家人不復言。

translations.literal: The family spoke no more of it.
translations.idiomatic: Her family never raised the matter again.

sentences.zh: 寇亂，匿棺以免。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of bandits, she hid the coffin to preserve it.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits ravaged the region, she hid the coffin so it would not be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，師南行，過其村，梁懼，積薪於戶下，舉火，乃入棺，自焚死。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, the army marched south and passed her village; Liang was afraid, piled firewood beneath her door, set fire, then entered the coffin and burned herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi, as the Qing army marched south through her village, Liang piled firewood at her doorway, set it ablaze, climbed into her coffin, and burned herself to death.

sentences.zh: 歸昭妻陸，弟繼登妻張，昭，崑山人；

translations.literal: Gui Zhao's wife Lu, and his younger brother Jideng's wife Zhang—Zhao was from Kunshan;
translations.idiomatic: Gui Zhao's wife Lu and his younger brother Jideng's wife Zhang were involved; Zhao was a native of Kunshan;

sentences.zh: 陸、張皆太倉人。

translations.literal: Lu and Zhang were both from Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu and Zhang were both from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 昭仕明為監紀，順治二年，死揚州；

translations.literal: Zhao served the Ming as supervisor of discipline; in the second year of Shunzhi he died at Yangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had served the Ming as an inspector of discipline and died at Yangzhou in the second year of Shunzhi;

sentences.zh: 繼登為教諭，長興民亂，戕焉。

translations.literal: Jideng was an instructor; when the people of Changxing rose in disorder, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jideng was a district instructor; when the people of Changxing rebelled, he was slain.

sentences.zh: 二婦未得問。

translations.literal: The two women could not obtain news of them.
translations.idiomatic: The two widows could learn nothing of their husbands' fate.

sentences.zh: 崑山兵起，舅姑避於鄉，舟迎二婦，二婦不果行。

translations.literal: When troops rose in Kunshan, the parents-in-law fled to the countryside and sent a boat to fetch the two women, but they did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting broke out in Kunshan, their parents-in-law fled to the countryside and sent a boat for the two daughters-in-law, but they refused to leave.

sentences.zh: 師至，城閉，城西砲如雷。

translations.literal: The army arrived; the city gates were shut, and cannon west of the city thundered like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing army arrived and sealed the city; west of the walls the cannon fire rolled like thunder.

sentences.zh: 二婦夜登樓，環坐諸兒女酌酒，戒積薪樓下，城破則縱火。

translations.literal: At night the two women went up to the tower, sat in a circle with the children pouring wine, and ordered firewood piled below, saying that when the city fell they would set fire.
translations.idiomatic: That night the two women went up to a tower, gathered the children around them, poured wine, and instructed that firewood be stacked below so that when the city fell they could set it ablaze.

sentences.zh: 一老僕進，謂城破當兵衝，慮不及死，城北比丘尼故與主母善，菴後有池，倉卒可得死，從之。

translations.literal: An old servant came forward and said that when the city fell the military thoroughfare would leave no time to die; a Buddhist nun north of the city had been on good terms with the mistress, and behind her convent was a pool where one could die in haste—they followed her.
translations.idiomatic: An old servant urged that once the walls were breached the main streets would be overrun and death might come too late; he knew a nun north of the city who had been close to their mother-in-law, and behind her convent was a pond where they could die quickly, and they went with him.

sentences.zh: 城破，兵掠菴，張入池，陸視其女，一卒前犯，陸力拒，被二矛，僕，又亂箠之，乃絕。

translations.literal: The city fell; soldiers plundered the convent; Zhang entered the pool; Lu watched her daughter; a soldier came forward to violate her; Lu resisted with all her strength, was struck by two spears and fell, and the soldiers beat her with clubs until she died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, soldiers looted the convent. Zhang entered the pond. Lu was watching her daughter when a soldier advanced to assault her; she fought him off fiercely, was pierced by two spears and knocked down, then beaten to death with clubs.

sentences.zh: 張以水淺，不即死。

translations.literal: Zhang, because the water was shallow, did not die immediately.
translations.idiomatic: The water was too shallow for Zhang to drown at once.

sentences.zh: 兵去，潛視陸，陸亦蘇，乃與尼共掖起之。

translations.literal: When the soldiers left, they secretly looked at Lu; Lu also revived, and together with the nun they helped her up.
translations.idiomatic: After the soldiers withdrew, Zhang found that Lu too had revived, and together with the nun they helped her to her feet.

sentences.zh: 兵復至，張輒避諸池，一卒索得張，欲執以去，張力拒，見殺。

translations.literal: The soldiers returned; Zhang repeatedly hid in the pool; a soldier found Zhang and wished to seize her and take her away; Zhang resisted with all her strength and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers came back. Zhang kept diving into the pond, but a soldier found her and tried to drag her away; she fought him with all her might and was killed.

sentences.zh: 陸創重卒。

translations.literal: Lu's wounds were severe, and she died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, grievously wounded, died as well.

sentences.zh: 羅仁美妻李，仁美，揚州人，失其縣；

translations.literal: Luo Renmei's wife Li—Renmei was a native of Yangzhou, his county of origin being unknown;
translations.idiomatic: Luo Renmei's wife Li: Renmei was from Yangzhou, though his native district is not recorded;

sentences.zh: 李，龍遊人。

translations.literal: Li was from Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Li was from Longyou.

sentences.zh: 家揚州廣儲門。

translations.literal: Their home was at Guangchu Gate in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They lived at Guangchu Gate in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 師下揚州，李方娠，積薪所居樓下，呼諸婦曰：「原死者共死，毋辱！

translations.literal: When the army descended on Yangzhou, Li was pregnant; she piled firewood beneath the building where they lived and called to the women, "Let those who wish to die die together—do not suffer disgrace!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing army entered Yangzhou, Li was pregnant. She stacked firewood under their house and called to the women, "Whoever is willing to die, let us die together—let us not be shamed!"

sentences.zh: 」於是姒劉、仁美妾梅、李，前室女宦姑及諸婦，從李登樓，凡十二人。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sister-in-law Liu, Renmei's concubine Mei, Li, the former wife's daughter Guangu, and the other women followed Li upstairs—twelve persons in all.
translations.idiomatic: Then Sister-in-law Liu, Renmei's concubine Mei, Li herself, the former wife's daughter Guangu, and the other women followed Li upstairs—twelve in all.

sentences.zh: 呼婢菊花舉火，前室子哭，從李俱上，李顧見，啟牖呼仁美，擲兒下。

translations.literal: She called the maid Juhua to set fire; the son of the former wife wept and followed Li up; Li looked back, opened the window, called to Renmei, and threw the child down.
translations.idiomatic: She told the maid Juhua to light the fire. The former wife's son wept and tried to follow Li upstairs; she looked back, opened the window, called to Renmei, and cast the boy down to him.

sentences.zh: 仁美負母手挈兒，哭出巷，回首，見黑煙出瓦隙，火合樓摧，聞屧聲沸火中。

translations.literal: Renmei carried his mother on his back and led the child by the hand, weeping as he fled the lane; looking back, he saw black smoke issuing from between the tiles, fire engulfed the building and it collapsed, and he heard the sound of sandals boiling in the flames.
translations.idiomatic: Renmei bore his mother on his back, took the child by the hand, and fled down the lane in tears. Looking back, he saw black smoke pouring through the roof tiles; the fire merged and the building collapsed, and he heard what sounded like pattering footsteps churning in the blaze.

sentences.zh: 仁美行，遇兵，僅得脫。

translations.literal: As Renmei went on his way, he met soldiers and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Renmei met soldiers and barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 兵去，發樓燼，拾殘骼，惟菊花遺肢衣可辨。

translations.literal: When the soldiers left, they opened the ashes of the building and gathered the charred bones; only fragments of Juhua's clothing could be identified.
translations.idiomatic: After the soldiers withdrew, they sifted the ruins and collected the charred remains; only scraps of Juhua's clothing could be recognized.

sentences.zh: 乃叢葬十三人西華門外。

translations.literal: They then buried the thirteen together outside Xihua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteen victims were buried together in a common grave outside Xihua Gate.

sentences.zh: 同時錢應式女淑賢，丹徒人。

translations.literal: At the same time Qian Yingshi's daughter Shuxian was from Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time, Qian Yingshi's daughter Shuxian, of Dantu,

sentences.zh: 聞城破，數自殺，未絕。

translations.literal: Hearing that the city had fallen, she tried several times to kill herself but did not die.
translations.idiomatic: hearing that the city had fallen, attempted suicide several times without success.

sentences.zh: 雨甚，門外萬馬聲，比屋殺人，火四起。

translations.literal: The rain fell heavily; outside the gate the sound of ten thousand horses; house after house people were killed, and fires rose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Rain poured down. Outside the gate came the thunder of countless hooves; neighbors were slaughtered house by house, and fires broke out everywhere.

sentences.zh: 淑賢以紙漬水塞口鼻，持父手壅其氣，父手悸不能舉，又解衣帶，強母使縊。

translations.literal: Shuxian stuffed her nose and mouth with wet paper, held her father's hand to block his breath, but his hand trembled and could not be raised; she then untied her sash and forced her mother to hang herself.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxian stuffed wet paper into her nose and mouth, seized her father's hand to smother him, but his hand shook and would not stay put; she then loosened her belt and forced her mother to hang herself.

sentences.zh: 母哭走，出，聞足擊床閣閣，入視，已絕。

translations.literal: Her mother wept and ran out; going out, she heard feet striking the bed with a steady thud; entering to look, Shuxian was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother wept and fled. When she went out she heard feet drumming on the bedstead; she went back in and found Shuxian already dead.

sentences.zh: 王氏三女，金壇人。

translations.literal: The three daughters of the Wang family were from Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang family's three daughters were from Jintan.

sentences.zh: 其二為同產，其一為群從姊妹，年皆十六七，以王師下江南，諸州縣盜群起，王氏避長蕩湖。

translations.literal: Two were sisters by the same mother, and one was a cousin; all were sixteen or seventeen years old. Because the imperial army descended on Jiangnan and bandits rose in every district and county, the Wangs took refuge at Lake Changdang.
translations.idiomatic: Two were full sisters and one a cousin; all were sixteen or seventeen. When the Qing armies entered Jiangnan and bandits rose throughout the region, the family fled to Lake Changdang.

sentences.zh: 晝延緣葦間，夜復其居。

translations.literal: By day they crept along among the reeds; by night they returned to their dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: By day they hid among the reeds; by night they returned to their shelter.

sentences.zh: 一日，盜至，劫三女子，縛置筏上。

translations.literal: One day bandits came, seized the three girls, bound them, and placed them on a raft.
translations.idiomatic: One day robbers came, seized the three girls, bound them, and put them on a raft.

sentences.zh: 三女子號泣跌蕩，筏覆，三女子死焉，賊十數輩亦溺。

translations.literal: The three girls wept and struggled until the raft overturned; the three girls died, and more than ten of the bandits were drowned as well.
translations.idiomatic: The girls wept and thrashed until the raft capsized; all three drowned, and more than ten of the bandits went down with them.

sentences.zh: 明日，屍浮水上，縛盡弛，三女子攜手，發相縻。

translations.literal: The next day their corpses floated on the water; the bonds had all come loose, and the three girls held hands, their hair tangled together.
translations.idiomatic: The next day their bodies floated to the surface. Their bonds had come undone, and the three lay hand in hand, their hair intertwined.

sentences.zh: 亂中無棺，得故篋三重以斂，墓於湖濱，墓木枝蘗皆三，相樛。

translations.literal: In the turmoil there were no coffins; they found three old chests and used them for burial, interring them by the lakeshore; every shoot and branch on the grave trees came in threes, intertwined.
translations.idiomatic: With no coffins to be had in the chaos, they buried the girls in three old chests by the lakeshore; every sprig on the grave mounds grew in threes, twined together.

sentences.zh: 沈華區妻潘，海寧人，居硤石。

translations.literal: Shen Huaqu's wife Pan was from Haining and lived at Xiashi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaqu's wife Pan was from Haining and lived at Xiashi.

sentences.zh: 順治二年六月，舉人周宗彝起兵硤石。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Shunzhi, the licentiate Zhou Zongyi raised troops at Xiashi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Shunzhi, the licentiate Zhou Zongyi raised a force at Xiashi.

sentences.zh: 八月望，師宵乘北關破之，華區與潘皆被俘。

translations.literal: On the night of the mid-autumn full moon in the eighth month, the army made a night attack through Beiguan and broke them; Huaqu and Pan were both taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth night of the eighth month the Qing army stormed Beiguan by night and broke the rebels; Huaqu and Pan were both captured.

sentences.zh: 過南市橋，潘睨水欲自沉，華區密止之，曰：「汝死，兵且殺我！

translations.literal: Crossing South Market Bridge, Pan glanced at the water and wished to drown herself; Huaqu secretly stopped her, saying, "If you die, the soldiers will kill me!"
translations.idiomatic: As they crossed South Market Bridge, Pan looked at the water and tried to throw herself in. Huaqu quietly restrained her, saying, "If you die, the soldiers will kill me!"

sentences.zh: 」潘乃語兵：「我從汝去，原得釋我夫。

translations.literal: Pan then said to the soldiers, "I will go with you, provided you release my husband."
translations.idiomatic: Pan then told the soldiers, "I will go with you if you release my husband."

sentences.zh: 」兵釋華區，驅潘入舟，舟行十八里，至王店。

translations.literal: The soldiers released Huaqu, drove Pan into a boat, and after the boat had traveled eighteen li they reached Wangdian.
translations.idiomatic: They released Huaqu, forced Pan into a boat, and after eighteen li reached Wangdian.

sentences.zh: 水次，觀者方集，潘忽躍起，曰：「我硤石沈華區妻，義不任受辱！

translations.literal: At the water's edge a crowd had gathered; Pan suddenly leapt up and cried, "I am Shen Huaqu's wife of Xiashi—I will not endure disgrace!"
translations.idiomatic: A crowd had gathered at the landing. Pan suddenly sprang up and cried, "I am Shen Huaqu's wife of Xiashi—I will not live in dishonor!"

sentences.zh: 」奮入水。

translations.literal: She plunged into the water.
translations.idiomatic: She flung herself into the water.

sentences.zh: 兵驚，捽其發出水，潘力自沉，發斷，係以纟墨，益力自沉，纆絕，如是三，兵以刃舂其喉，遂死。

translations.literal: The soldiers were startled, seized her hair and pulled her out; Pan struggled to drown herself with all her might; her hair broke; they tied her with silk cord and she struggled all the harder to sink; the cord snapped—three times this happened—and the soldiers ran a blade into her throat, and she died.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers seized her by the hair and hauled her out. She fought to sink with all her strength; her hair tore away. They bound her with silk cord, and she fought harder still; the cord broke. Three times this happened before a soldier drove a blade into her throat and killed her.

sentences.zh: 師中有裨將歎其烈，出千錢為斂。

translations.literal: A lieutenant in the army admired her valor and contributed a thousand cash for her burial.
translations.idiomatic: A lieutenant in the army, moved by her fortitude, donated a thousand cash for her burial.

sentences.zh: 陳某妻伍，華亭人。

translations.literal: The wife Wu of a certain Chen was from Huating.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, wife of a man surnamed Chen, was from Huating.

sentences.zh: 師下松江，陳家璜溪，兵至，斧陳首，伍奔救，兵捨其夫而縶之。

translations.literal: When the army entered Songjiang, Chen's family was at Huangxi; soldiers came, struck off Chen's head with an axe; Wu ran to save him, and the soldiers left her husband and seized her.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing army reached Songjiang, the Chens were at Huangxi. Soldiers came and struck off Chen's head with an axe. Wu rushed to save him; the soldiers abandoned her husband's body and seized her instead.

sentences.zh: 伍曰：「毋縛我，我從汝去！

translations.literal: Wu said, "Do not bind me—I will go with you!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu said, "Do not tie me up—I will go with you!"

sentences.zh: 」將登舟，躍入溪，死。

translations.literal: As she was about to board the boat, she leapt into the stream and died.
translations.idiomatic: As she was about to board the boat, she leapt into the creek and drowned.

sentences.zh: 當時死於溪者，諸生孫諤妻顧、徽州商孫氏之媼。

translations.literal: Those who died in the stream at that time included Gu, wife of the student Sun E, and an old woman of the Sun merchant family of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Others who died in the creek at that time included Gu, wife of the student Sun E, and an old woman of the Sun merchant family from Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 洪志達妻葉，歙人。

translations.literal: Hong Zhida's wife Ye was from She county.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zhida's wife Ye was from She county.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，徽州初定，盜賊所在多有，志達偕葉避兵淳安鄭家村。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, Huizhou had just been pacified, but bandits were everywhere; Zhida and Ye together fled the fighting to Zhengjia Village in Chun'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi, Huizhou had only just been pacified, yet bandits were still rampant; Zhida and Ye fled together to Zhengjia Village in Chun'an.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，村人譁言兵至，志達與葉倉皇走，匿草中，遊騎過，自草中曳葉出。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year the villagers clamored that soldiers were coming; Zhida and Ye fled in panic and hid in the grass; passing horsemen dragged Ye out of the grass.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the second month, villagers shouted that troops were approaching. Zhida and Ye fled in panic and hid in the tall grass, but passing horsemen dragged Ye out.

sentences.zh: 志達習拳勇有力，踴自草中，奮擊一騎，僕，眾騎拔刀赴志達。

translations.literal: Zhida had studied boxing and was strong; he leapt from the grass and struck one horseman with all his might; the man fell, and the horsemen drew their swords and rushed at Zhida.
translations.idiomatic: Zhida had trained in boxing and was powerful. He sprang from the grass and struck down one rider, but the others drew their swords and closed on him.

sentences.zh: 志達徒手與鬥，眾騎且僕且起，環射之，矢中志達目，貫腦死。

translations.literal: Zhida fought them bare-handed; the horsemen knocked him down and he rose again; they surrounded him and shot; an arrow struck Zhida in the eye and pierced through his brain, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought them empty-handed as they knocked him down again and again. They ringed him and shot; an arrow struck him in the eye and pierced through to his brain, and he died.

sentences.zh: 葉抱屍慟，眾騎挾之行，葉輟哭。

translations.literal: Ye embraced the corpse and wailed; the horsemen seized her and marched her away; Ye ceased her weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Ye embraced his body and wailed. The horsemen seized her and rode off; she stopped crying.

sentences.zh: 馬行漸緩，度懸崖，葉曰：「勿持我急，我自能乘。

translations.literal: The horse went more and more slowly; crossing a cliff, Ye said, "Do not hold me so tight—I can ride by myself."
translations.idiomatic: As the horse slowed on a cliff path, Ye said, "Do not grip me so tightly—I can ride on my own."

sentences.zh: 」賊信之，遂​​縱馬向崖，眾騎自後從之，葉自馬上擲崖下，死。

translations.literal: The bandits believed her, and so they let the horse run toward the cliff; the horsemen followed from behind; Ye threw herself from the horse over the cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: They believed her and slackened their hold. She spurred the horse toward the precipice; when the riders followed from behind, she threw herself from the saddle over the cliff and died.

sentences.zh: 淳安人言其死且為神，為之祠焉。

translations.literal: The people of Chun'an said that after her death she became a spirit, and they built a shrine to her.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chun'an said that in death she became a spirit, and they erected a shrine in her honor.

sentences.zh: 羅章袞妻杜，群聘妻田，淳化人。

translations.literal: Luo Zhanggun's wife Du and Qunpin's wife Tian were from Chunhua.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zhanggun's wife Du and Qunpin's wife Tian were from Chunhua.

sentences.zh: 群聘，章袞從子也，皆早卒。

translations.literal: Qunpin was Zhanggun's nephew; both men had died young.
translations.idiomatic: Qunpin was Zhanggun's nephew; both husbands had died young.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，寇至，城破，杜指牆間井，語養女淑明、淑儀曰：「此吾曹死所也！

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi bandits came and the city fell; Du pointed to the well between the walls and said to her adopted daughters Shuming and Shuyi, "This is where we shall die!"
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi, raiders came and the city fell. Du pointed to a well in the courtyard and told her adopted daughters Shuming and Shuyi, "This is where we die!"

sentences.zh: 」遂入井。

translations.literal: She then entered the well.
translations.idiomatic: She went into the well.

sentences.zh: 淑明、淑儀相向哭，從之下。

translations.literal: Shuming and Shuyi wept facing each other and followed her down.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming and Shuyi wept face to face and followed her in.

sentences.zh: 田與杜連牆居，聞哭，呼其女優姐，亦趨井死。

translations.literal: Tian lived next door to Du; hearing the cries, she called her daughter Youjie, and she too rushed to the well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tian lived next door to Du. Hearing the cries, she called her daughter Youjie, who also ran to the well and died.

sentences.zh: 先一年，縣兵譟變，章袞侄女竇芳墮樓死，竇芳有從姊雁珠，明崇禎間死寇，竇芳方在娠，其母夢雁珠偕一女至，謂唐奉天竇烈女也，故命曰竇芳。

translations.literal: A year earlier, when the county troops mutinied, Zhanggun's niece Dou Fang fell from a tower and died; Dou Fang had a cousin Yanzhen who had died fighting bandits in the Chongzhen era; while Dou Fang was still in the womb, her mother dreamed that Yanzhen came with a girl and said she was the Dou Lienü who gave her life for Tang under Emperor Fengtian, and therefore named her Dou Fang.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, when county troops mutinied, Zhanggun's niece Dou Fang fell from a tower to her death. Dou Fang had a cousin Yanzhen who had died fighting bandits in the Chongzhen reign. While Dou Fang was still in the womb, her mother dreamed that Yanzhen came with a girl and said she was the Dou Lienü who sacrificed herself for the Tang at Fengtian, and so the child was named Dou Fang.

sentences.zh: 既長，嫁三原房大猷。

translations.literal: When she grew up, she married Fang Dayou of Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When she grew up, she married Fang Dayou of Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 其死後雁珠十七年，俱以正月十五日死，死時年俱十八，鄉人合前後稱「七烈」。

translations.literal: Seventeen years after Yanzhen's death, both died on the fifteenth day of the first month, both at the age of eighteen; the villagers collectively called them the "Seven Martyrs."
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen years after Yanzhen's death, both died on the fifteenth day of the first month, each at eighteen; the villagers collectively honored the seven as the "Seven Martyrs."

sentences.zh: 王磐千妻顏，江西安福人。

translations.literal: Wang Panqian's wife Yan was from Anfu in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Panqian's wife Yan was from Anfu in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，遇寇，紾其臂索賄，顏詫曰：「此手乃為賊執耶？

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi they met bandits, who twisted her arm demanding a bribe; Yan exclaimed in astonishment, "Is this hand to be seized by bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi they encountered bandits who twisted her arm demanding money. Yan cried in outrage, "Is this hand to be held by robbers?"

sentences.zh: 」投水死。

translations.literal: She threw herself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 何大封妻阮，無為人，早寡。

translations.literal: He Dafeng's wife Ruan was from Wuwei and had been widowed early.
translations.idiomatic: He Dafeng's wife Ruan was from Wuwei and had been widowed young.

sentences.zh: 有授物誤觸其手者，引刀斷指，血濺尺許。

translations.literal: When someone handing her something accidentally touched her hand, she drew a knife and cut off her finger; blood splashed more than a foot.
translations.idiomatic: When someone handing her an object accidentally brushed her hand, she took a knife and severed her finger; blood spattered more than a foot away.

sentences.zh: 方希文妻項，名淑美，淳安人。

translations.literal: Fang Xiwen's wife Xiang, named Shumei, was from Chun'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xiwen's wife Xiang, called Shumei, was from Chun'an.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，明潰師掠縣，希文攜家避兵西坑。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, defeated Ming troops plundered the county; Xiwen took his family to flee the fighting to Xikeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi, routed Ming soldiers plundered the county. Xiwen led his family to Xikeng to escape the fighting.

sentences.zh: 以妾子病，謁醫。

translations.literal: Because the concubine's child was ill, he went to see a doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Because his concubine's child was ill, he went to fetch a physician.

sentences.zh: 兵驟至，縱火。

translations.literal: Soldiers suddenly arrived and set fires.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers suddenly appeared and set fires.

sentences.zh: 火將及，婢請項出避，項曰：「出，死於兵；

translations.literal: As the fire was about to reach them, a maid begged Xiang to flee; Xiang said, "If we go out, we die at the hands of soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: As the flames drew near, a maid urged Xiang to flee. Xiang said, "If we leave, we die at the soldiers' hands;

sentences.zh: 不出，死於火。

translations.literal: if we do not go out, we die in the fire.
translations.idiomatic: if we stay, we die in the fire.

sentences.zh: 死同，死火不辱。

translations.literal: Death is the same, but to die by fire is not disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Death is the same either way, but to die by fire is not shameful.

sentences.zh: 若能死，則從；

translations.literal: If you are able to die, then follow me;
translations.idiomatic: If you are ready to die, then stay with me;

sentences.zh: 不能，亟出！

translations.literal: if not, go out at once!"
translations.idiomatic: if not, leave at once!"

sentences.zh: 」希文故有藏書，項積書左右，坐其中，火及，書燼，項殉焉。

translations.literal: Xiwen had a collection of books; Xiang piled books around her and sat among them; when the fire reached them the books were consumed to ash, and Xiang perished with them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiwen kept a library of books. Xiang heaped books around her and sat in their midst. When the fire reached her, the books burned to ash and Xiang perished with them.

sentences.zh: 廖愈達妻李，妾汪、張，泰宁人。

translations.literal: Liao Yuda's wife Li and concubines Wang and Zhang were from Taining.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yuda's wife Li and his concubines Wang and Zhang were from Taining.

sentences.zh: 李讀書通大義，教二妾章句。

translations.literal: Li read books and understood great principles; she taught the two concubines passages and lines.
translations.idiomatic: Li was well read and understood the larger moral principles; she taught both concubines to read classical passages.

sentences.zh: 愈達從外歸，聞李疏「仁」字，教二妾，語諄諄。

translations.literal: When Yuda returned from outside, he heard Li explaining the character ren (benevolence) and instructing the two concubines, speaking earnestly and at length.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuda came home from abroad, he heard Li lecturing the two concubines on the character ren, "benevolence," her words earnest and unhurried.

sentences.zh: 愈達入而笑，李正色曰：「志士仁人，有殺身以成仁，毋求生以害仁！

translations.literal: Yuda entered and laughed; Li said with a stern face, "The noble person of resolve gives up his life to fulfill benevolence—he does not preserve his life at the cost of benevolence!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuda came in and laughed. Li said gravely, "The man of noble resolve gives his life to fulfill benevolence—he does not save his life at the cost of benevolence!"

sentences.zh: 」順治三年，愈達將妻妾避兵，或傳崇禎十七年京師破時，檢討汪偉與其妻耿殉國事，李以告二妾，相持而哭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, Yuda was about to take his wife and concubines to flee the fighting; someone reported that when the capital fell in the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, the reviser Wang Wei and his wife Geng died for the state; Li told the two concubines, and they embraced and wept.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi, as Yuda prepared to flee with his wife and concubines, word came that when Beijing fell in the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, the reviser Wang Wei and his wife Geng had died for the dynasty. Li told the two concubines, and they clung to one another weeping.

sentences.zh: 師漸逼，愈達與妻妾夜走南石砦，師至，攻砦，愈達率妻妾避砦口。

translations.literal: As the army drew nearer, Yuda and his wife and concubines fled by night to South Stone Fort; the army arrived and attacked the fort; Yuda led his wife and concubines to avoid them at the fort entrance.
translations.idiomatic: As the Qing army closed in, Yuda fled with his wife and concubines by night to South Stone Fort. When the army came and assaulted the fort, he led them toward the entrance.

sentences.zh: 或呼師自砦後入，李即從砦口展手投崖下。

translations.literal: Someone shouted that the army was entering from behind the fort; Li immediately stretched out her hands at the fort entrance and threw herself off the cliff.
translations.idiomatic: Someone cried that troops were entering from the rear. Li at once spread her arms at the fort mouth and cast herself from the cliff.

sentences.zh: 愈達挈二妾匿岩石中，搜山兵至，張亦投崖死。

translations.literal: Yuda took the two concubines and hid in the rocks; soldiers searching the mountain came, and Zhang also threw herself off the cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuda led the two concubines into hiding among the rocks. When search parties came, Zhang too cast herself from the cliff and died.

sentences.zh: 愈達出金遣兵去，汪堅持愈達衣，伏其後，頃之，遙見師中出裨將，硃纓窄袖，指揮從卒巡山。

translations.literal: Yuda produced gold to send the soldiers away; Wang clung to Yuda's garment and crouched behind him; before long, from afar they saw a lieutenant emerge from the army, with vermilion tassel and narrow sleeves, directing followers to patrol the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yuda paid the soldiers to leave. Wang gripped his robe and hid behind him. Soon they saw a lieutenant in vermilion tassel and narrow sleeves emerge from the camp, directing men to search the hills.

sentences.zh: 汪大哭曰：「君善自保！

translations.literal: Wang wept loudly and said, "My lord, take good care of yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang burst into tears and cried, "My lord, preserve yourself!"

sentences.zh: 」亦投崖，激於石，身裂若支解。

translations.literal: She too threw herself off the cliff; striking the rocks, her body was torn as if dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: She too threw herself from the cliff. She struck the rocks and her body was shattered as if cut apart.

sentences.zh: 師退，愈達及諸同避砦中者皆得脫。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, Yuda and all who had taken refuge in the fort escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, Yuda and everyone who had sheltered in the fort escaped.

sentences.zh: 葉芊妻謝，寧都人。

translations.literal: Ye Qian's wife Xie was from Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Qian's wife Xie was from Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 六年冬十月，明將揭重熙等以師赴南昌，駐寧都兵掠得謝，部曲將悅其色，問家世，謝從容具以對，因乞得沐浴，部曲將許之，遂入室，以鬀鬢刀自揕其喉，死。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth winter year, Ming generals Jie Chongxi and others led troops to Nanchang and were stationed at Ningdu; soldiers plundering seized Xie; a subordinate officer was pleased with her beauty and asked about her family; Xie calmly told him in full, and therefore begged to be allowed to bathe; the officer permitted it; she then entered the room and stabbed her own throat with a barber's knife and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the sixth year, Ming generals including Jie Chongxi marched on Nanchang and encamped at Ningdu. Plundering soldiers seized Xie. An officer, taken with her beauty, asked her lineage; she answered calmly and begged leave to bathe. When he granted it, she went inside and stabbed her throat with a razor knife and died.

sentences.zh: 姚文璚妻劉，名滿，福清人。

translations.literal: Yao Wenjing's wife Liu, named Man, was from Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Wenjing's wife Liu, called Man, was from Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 文璚鬻香於市，順治三年，海寇至，索錢無所得，截文璚首去。

translations.literal: Wenjing sold incense in the market; in the third year of Shunzhi sea bandits came; demanding money and obtaining none, they cut off Wenjing's head and took it away.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing sold incense in the marketplace. In the third year of Shunzhi, sea bandits came; when he had no money to give them, they struck off his head and carried it away.

sentences.zh: 滿舁屍還，舐血縛布綴於頸，斂畢，乃言曰：「我恨不能手刃賊，獨以死報君。

translations.literal: Man carried the corpse back, licked the blood, bound cloth with strips to the neck, and when the burial was complete she said, "I regret that I could not with my own hand slay the bandits; I can only repay my lord with death."
translations.idiomatic: Man bore the body home, licked the blood from the wound, and bound cloth around his neck for burial. When it was done she said, "I regret that I could not kill those bandits myself—I can only repay my husband with my life."

sentences.zh: 」首觸棺，僕，久之，甦，請以兄公子為後，盡鬻衣珥營葬。

translations.literal: She struck her head against the coffin and fell; after a long time she revived, asked that her elder brother's son be made heir, and sold all her clothing and ornaments to arrange the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: She dashed her head against the coffin and collapsed. After a long while she revived, arranged for her brother's son to be heir, and sold every piece of jewelry and clothing to pay for the burial.

sentences.zh: 越三年，清明上塚，歸，屑金咽之，死。

translations.literal: Three years later, on Clear and Bright she visited the tomb; returning home, she swallowed gold dust and died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, on the grave-sweeping festival she visited his tomb. Returning home, she swallowed powdered gold and died.

sentences.zh: 毛翼順妻陳，亦福清人。

translations.literal: Mao Yishun's wife Chen was also from Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yishun's wife Chen was also from Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，翼順死於寇，舁屍還，血溢於鼻，陳舐血，斂畢，不食七日，自經。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi Yishun died at the hands of bandits; they carried the corpse back; blood overflowed from the nose; Chen licked the blood; when the burial was complete she ate nothing for seven days and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, Yishun was killed by bandits. When his body was brought home, blood still flowed from his nose; Chen licked it. After the burial she fasted seven days and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 王三接妻黃，曹縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Sanjie's wife Huang was from Caoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sanjie's wife Huang was from Caoxian.

sentences.zh: 三接官汾西知縣，黃侍姑田家居。

translations.literal: Sanjie was magistrate of Fenxi; Huang attended her mother-in-law Tian at home.
translations.idiomatic: Sanjie served as magistrate of Fenxi while Huang stayed home caring for her mother-in-law Tian.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，李化鯨亂，破城，姑、婦皆被執。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi Li Huajing rebelled, broke the city, and both mother-in-law and daughter-in-law were seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shunzhi, Li Huajing rebelled and stormed the city. Mother-in-law and daughter-in-law were both taken.

sentences.zh: 黃語賊曰：「釋我姑，我與金帛，惟爾欲！

translations.literal: Huang said to the bandits, "Release my mother-in-law, and I will give you gold and silk—take whatever you wish!"
translations.idiomatic: Huang told the bandits, "Let my mother-in-law go, and I will give you gold and silk—take whatever you want!"

sentences.zh: 」賊釋其姑，黃度姑行遠，乃罵曰：「吾家清白吏，安有厚藏？

translations.literal: The bandits released her mother-in-law; Huang, judging that her mother-in-law had gone far, then cursed, saying, "Our family are honest officials—how could we have great hoards?"
translations.idiomatic: The bandits released the older woman. When Huang judged her mother-in-law was far enough away, she cursed them: "Our family has always been upright officials—what hoards do you imagine we have?"

sentences.zh: 吾名家女，命婦，豈肯從賊？

translations.literal: I am the daughter of an eminent family, a wife of official rank—how could I follow bandits?
translations.idiomatic: I am a daughter of a distinguished house, a wife of rank—how could I submit to bandits?

sentences.zh: 有死而已！

translations.literal: I have only death!
translations.idiomatic: I have nothing but death!

sentences.zh: 」賊磔之。

translations.literal: The bandits dismembered her.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits tore her limb from limb.

sentences.zh: 當時為賊殺者，劉琰妻邢等九人；

translations.literal: Those killed by bandits at that time included Xing, wife of Liu Yan, and eight others;
translations.idiomatic: Among those slain by the bandits were Xing, wife of Liu Yan, and eight others;

sentences.zh: 投水死者，王躋聖妻韓等七人。

translations.literal: those who drowned themselves included Han, wife of Wang Jisheng, and six others.
translations.idiomatic: those who drowned themselves included Han, wife of Wang Jisheng, and six others.

sentences.zh: 程顯妻硃，新建人，明宗室女也。

translations.literal: Cheng Xian's wife Zhu was from Xinjian and was a daughter of the Ming imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xian's wife Zhu was from Xinjian and a daughter of the Ming imperial house.

sentences.zh: 以其侄為子婦。

translations.literal: She took her nephew as daughter-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: She had taken her nephew's wife as her own daughter-in-law.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，金聲桓為亂，顯自南昌將家人入山，道遇兵相失。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi Jin Shengwan rebelled; Xian led his family from Nanchang into the mountains; on the road they met soldiers and were separated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shunzhi, Jin Shengwan rose in rebellion. Xian led his family from Nanchang into the hills and was separated from them on the road.

sentences.zh: 或傳顯已死，硃謂子婦：「翁死，吾不獨生，汝奈何？

translations.literal: Word came that Xian was already dead; Zhu said to her daughter-in-law, "Your father-in-law is dead—I will not live alone; what will you do?"
translations.idiomatic: Rumor spread that Xian was dead. Zhu said to her daughter-in-law, "Your father-in-law is dead—I will not live alone. What of you?"

sentences.zh: 」婦曰：「死耳！

translations.literal: The daughter-in-law said, "Death, of course!"
translations.idiomatic: The younger woman said, "Death, of course!"

sentences.zh: 」硃縊樹上，已絕，兵救之，甦，复觸樹死。

translations.literal: Zhu hanged herself on a tree and was already dead; soldiers rescued her and she revived, then struck the tree again and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu hanged herself on a tree. Soldiers cut her down and revived her; she struck the tree again and died.

sentences.zh: 婦亦起觸樹，兵前持婦，婦齧其指，奪刀自剄死。

translations.literal: The daughter-in-law also rose and struck the tree; soldiers came forward and seized her; she bit their fingers, seized a knife, and cut her own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter-in-law too rose to dash herself against the tree. Soldiers seized her; she bit their fingers, snatched a blade, and cut her own throat.

sentences.zh: 劉元鏜妻吳，妾硃，南昌人。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanyong's wife Wu and concubine Zhu were from Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanyong's wife Wu and concubine Zhu were from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 元鏜亦將家人避兵，兵及，棄抱中兒道旁《廣則》而走，吳伏溝草。

translations.literal: Yuanyong also led his family to flee the fighting; when soldiers came he abandoned the child in his arms by the roadside at Guangze and fled; Wu hid in ditch grass.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyong too fled with his family. When soldiers came he set down the child he was carrying at Guangze and ran; Wu hid in grass along a ditch.

sentences.zh: 硃為兵得，縶以行，經溪，躍，縶絕，兵斫其頰，死。

translations.literal: Zhu was seized by soldiers, bound, and marched away; crossing a stream she leapt; the bonds broke; the soldiers cut her cheek, and she died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was captured and led away. At a stream she leapt in; her bonds snapped, but the soldiers slashed her cheek and killed her.

sentences.zh: 吳出草，行數十武，遇鄰媼，脫簪求扶持。

translations.literal: Wu came out of the grass, walked several tens of paces, met a neighbor woman, removed her hairpin and begged support.
translations.idiomatic: Wu emerged and had gone only a few dozen paces when she met a neighbor. She took out her hairpin and begged to be helped along.

sentences.zh: 兵復至，吳握發仰天號曰：「夫邪子邪！

translations.literal: Soldiers came again; Wu seized her hair and cried to heaven, "Husband! Child!"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers returned. Wu clutched her hair and wailed to heaven, "My husband! My child!"

sentences.zh: 吾其死邪！

translations.literal: Must I die as well!"
translations.idiomatic: Am I to die as well?"

sentences.zh: 」兵挾刃逐之，行赴陂死。

translations.literal: Soldiers with blades pursued her; she went to a pond and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers with blades chased her. She ran to a pond and drowned.

sentences.zh: 是役諸女婦死者至眾，靖安舒調熙妻硃，救夫；

translations.literal: In this campaign the women who died were very numerous; Zhu, wife of Shu Tiaoxi of Jing'an, saved her husband;
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign countless women perished. Zhu, wife of Shu Tiaoxi of Jing'an, died saving her husband;

sentences.zh: 豐城熊嗣蕃妻胡，及從子有恆妻沈，從夫救舅：皆死。

translations.literal: Hu, wife of Xiong Sifan of Fengcheng, and Shen, wife of his nephew Youheng, followed their husbands to save the father-in-law—all died.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, wife of Xiong Sifan of Fengcheng, and Shen, wife of his nephew Youheng, followed their husbands to rescue a father-in-law—all died.

sentences.zh: 而新建徐文璠妻硃，割乳斷首；

translations.literal: And Zhu, wife of Xu Wenlin of Xinjian, cut off her breast and severed her head;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, wife of Xu Wenlin of Xinjian, cut off her own breast and severed her head;

sentences.zh: 進賢胡永益妻胡，刃出背：死尤烈。

translations.literal: Hu, wife of Hu Yongyi of Jinxian, was stabbed through the back: their deaths were especially fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, wife of Hu Yongyi of Jinxian, was run through from behind—their deaths were especially terrible.

sentences.zh: 應氏婦，鄞人。

translations.literal: A woman of the Ying family was from Yin county.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the Ying clan was from Yin.

sentences.zh: 貧行乞。

translations.literal: Poor, she went begging.
translations.idiomatic: She was poor and lived by begging.

sentences.zh: 順治六年，海寇至，匿郭東廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shunzhi sea bandits came; she hid in Guodong Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shunzhi, sea bandits came and she hid in Guodong Temple.

sentences.zh: 寇欲汙之，堅不從。

translations.literal: The bandits wished to violate her; she firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to violate her; she steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 既仍偽諾，出廟，將入井，寇复牽以入，終號泣不就，死亂刃。

translations.literal: She then pretended to consent, left the temple, and was about to enter a well when the bandits again dragged her back inside; to the end she wept and cried and would not submit, and died by random blades.
translations.idiomatic: She feigned consent, left the temple, and was about to throw herself into a well when they dragged her back. She wept and resisted to the end and was hacked to death.

sentences.zh: 平陽婦，不知其姓氏。

translations.literal: A woman of Pingyang—her surname is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of Pingyang—her surname is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 順治七年，姜瓖亂，為其徒所掠，過定州唐城村，刺血題詩於壁，並為序自述，略言：「明月在天，清水在旁。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shunzhi, when Jiang Xiang rebelled, she was seized by his followers; passing Tangcheng Village in Dingzhou, she pricked blood and inscribed a poem on the wall, with a preface recounting herself, saying in brief, "The bright moon is in heaven, clear water is at hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Shunzhi, during Jiang Xiang's rebellion, she was seized by his men. At Tangcheng Village in Dingzhou she wrote a poem in blood on a wall, with a preface that read in part: "The bright moon hangs in heaven; clear water lies beside me.

sentences.zh: 得自盡於此，上不媿父母，次不慚婿，庶幾與水同清，與月同明。

translations.literal: To be able to end my life here—I am not ashamed before my parents above, nor before my husband below; I may perhaps be as clear as the water and as bright as the moon."
translations.idiomatic: To die here—I am not ashamed before my parents above nor before my husband below; may I be as pure as the water and as bright as the moon."

sentences.zh: 」遂自經死。

translations.literal: She then hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: She then hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 殷壯猷妻李，豐潤人。

translations.literal: Yin Zhuangyou's wife Li was from Fengrun.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhuangyou's wife Li was from Fengrun.

sentences.zh: 順治中，壯猷為臨藍參將。

translations.literal: During Shunzhi, Zhuangyou was deputy commander at Linlan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shunzhi reign Zhuangyou served as deputy commander at Linlan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，孫可望攻臨藍，壯猷築城以守，圍久不解，出戰，死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Sun Kewang attacked Linlan; Zhuangyou built walls to defend; the siege was long unresolved; he went out to fight and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Sun Kewang besieged Linlan. Zhuangyou fortified the city and held out until, sallying forth, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 李以印畀次子質，揮使出避，而與長子文自剄死。

translations.literal: Li gave the seal to her second son Zhi, sent the steward away to escape, and with her eldest son Wen cut her own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Li handed the official seal to her second son Zhi, sent the steward away to safety, and with her eldest son Wen cut her own throat.

sentences.zh: 楊昌文妻袁，安義人，或曰建昌人。

translations.literal: Yang Changwen's wife Yuan was from Anyi, or some say Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Changwen's wife Yuan was from Anyi, though some say Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 順治間兵亂，父母迎袁歸，袁不可，曰：「棄姑避兵，不義。

translations.literal: During the military disorders of Shunzhi her parents came to take Yuan home; Yuan would not go, saying, "To abandon my mother-in-law and flee the fighting is unrighteous."
translations.idiomatic: During the disorders of Shunzhi her parents came to fetch her home. Yuan refused, saying, "To abandon my mother-in-law and flee would be wrong."

sentences.zh: 」兵至，伏地請死，斫數刃去。

translations.literal: When soldiers came she prostrated herself and begged for death; they hacked her with many blades and left.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers came she threw herself to the ground and begged them to kill her. They hacked her many times and left.

sentences.zh: 家人歸，努目問：「姑無恙乎？

translations.literal: When the family returned, she glared and asked, "Is Mother-in-law unharmed?"
translations.idiomatic: When her family returned, she fixed them with a stare and asked, "Is my mother-in-law unharmed?"

sentences.zh: 」曰「無恙」，乃瞑。

translations.literal: They said "Unharmed," and she closed her eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Told she was safe, she closed her eyes and died.

sentences.zh: 諶日昇妻陳，高安人。

translations.literal: Chen Risheng's wife Chen was from Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Risheng's wife Chen was from Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 順治間，金聲桓亂，為兵掠挾上馬，力拒，中八刃，剖心斷脰刳孕死。

translations.literal: During Shunzhi, in Jin Shengwan's rebellion, she was seized by soldiers and forced onto a horse; she resisted with all her strength, was struck by eight blades, her heart cut out, her neck severed, and her womb opened—she died pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: During Jin Shengwan's rebellion in Shunzhi, soldiers seized her and forced her onto a horse. She fought them off, took eight blade wounds, had her heart cut out, her neck severed, and her pregnant belly opened—she died.

sentences.zh: 陳某妻萬，萬縣人。

translations.literal: The wife Wan of a certain Chen was from Wan county.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, wife of a man surnamed Chen, was from Wan county.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，譚弘亂，被執，殺其懷中子。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi era Tan Hong rebelled; she was seized and they killed the child in her arms.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi reign Tan Hong rebelled. She was captured and they killed the child in her arms.

sentences.zh: 萬詭言家有藏鏹，賊使其徒從以往，過懸崖，奮起，擠賊墮，亦自投死。

translations.literal: Wan falsely said there was hidden treasure at home; the bandits sent followers to go with her; passing a cliff she suddenly rose, pushed the bandits over, and threw herself down as well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wan claimed there was buried treasure at home and led bandits to a cliff, then suddenly shoved them over the edge and threw herself after them.

sentences.zh: 林應雒妻莫，梁學謙女，吳師讓妻某，黃某妻李，皆新會人。

translations.literal: Mo, wife of Lin Yingluo; a daughter of the Liang family, wife of Wu Shirang; Li, wife of a certain Huang—all were from Xinhui.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, wife of Lin Yingluo; a daughter of the Liang family; the wife of Wu Shirang; Li, wife of a certain Huang—all were from Xinhui.

sentences.zh: 應雒、學謙、師讓皆諸生。

translations.literal: Yingluo, Xueqian, and Shirang were all students.
translations.idiomatic: Yingluo, Liang Xueqian, and Shirang were all licentiates.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年，明將李定國攻新會，城守閱八月，食盡，殺人馬為食。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi the Ming general Li Dingguo attacked Xinhui; the city defended itself for eight months; food was exhausted and they killed men and horses for food.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi the Ming general Li Dingguo besieged Xinhui. The city held eight months until food ran out and they ate horse and human flesh.

sentences.zh: 莫代姑，梁女年十一代父，黃、李代夫，皆死。

translations.literal: Mo took her mother-in-law's place; Liang's daughter, eleven years old, took her father's place; Huang's wife and Li took their husbands' places—all died.
translations.idiomatic: Mo died in her mother-in-law's stead; Liang's eleven-year-old daughter died in her father's place; Huang's wife and Li died in their husbands' places.

sentences.zh: 李之死，兵持首還其夫，使葬焉。

translations.literal: When Li died, the soldiers held out her head to her husband and made him bury it.
translations.idiomatic: When Li died the soldiers brought her head to her husband and ordered him to bury it.

sentences.zh: 文秉世妻梁，鬱林人。

translations.literal: Wen Bingshi's wife Liang was from Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Bingshi's wife Liang was from Yulin.

sentences.zh: 李定國掠州，梁為兵掠，迫上馬。

translations.literal: Li Dingguo plundered the prefecture; Liang was seized by soldiers and forced onto a horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Dingguo ravaged the region, soldiers seized Liang and forced her onto a horse.

sentences.zh: 梁哭，據地罵，兵殺之。

translations.literal: Liang wept, clung to the ground and cursed; the soldiers killed her.
translations.idiomatic: She wept, clung to the ground, and cursed them until they killed her.

sentences.zh: 越二日，秉世得其屍，目未瞑也。

translations.literal: Two days later Bingshi recovered her corpse; her eyes had not closed.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Bingshi recovered her body; her eyes were still open.

sentences.zh: 文氏女兆祥，文樞妻陸，灌陽人。

translations.literal: The daughter Zhaoxiang of the Wen family, and Lu, wife of Wen Shu, were from Guanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhaoxiang, daughter of the Wen family, and Lu, wife of Wen Shu, were from Guanyang.

sentences.zh: 定國兵至，姑嫂避火星山箐中，兵入，自殺。

translations.literal: When Dingguo's army came, mother-in-law and daughter-in-law fled to Huoxing Mountain ravine; when soldiers entered, they killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingguo's army came, the two women fled to a ravine on Huoxing Mountain. When soldiers entered, they killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 何氏女，昭平人。

translations.literal: A daughter of the He family was from Zhaoping.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter of the He family was from Zhaoping.

sentences.zh: 是歲師逐定國，避兵思庇衝。

translations.literal: That year the army pursued Dingguo; fleeing the fighting she took refuge at Sibichong.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as the Qing army pursued Dingguo, she fled to Sibichong.

sentences.zh: 或迫之，死。

translations.literal: When some pressed her, she died.
translations.idiomatic: When men threatened her, she died.

sentences.zh: 王氏三女：長亥娘，次竹姑，次酉娘，博白農家女。

translations.literal: The three daughters of the Wang family: the eldest Hai'niang, the second Zhugu, the third You'niang—peasant girls of Bobai.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang family's three daughters—the eldest Hai'niang, the second Zhugu, the third You'niang—were peasant girls of Bobai.

sentences.zh: 康熙十九年，避寇宴石岩，寇攻岩，姊妹皆投崖死。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi they fled bandits to Yanshi Rock; when bandits attacked the rock, the sisters all threw themselves from the cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi they fled bandits to Yanshi Rock. When bandits stormed the cliff, all three sisters leapt to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 陳心俊妻馬，伏羌人。

translations.literal: Chen Xinjun's wife Ma was from Fuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xinjun's wife Ma was from Fuxiang.

sentences.zh: 年十九，寡。

translations.literal: At nineteen she was widowed.
translations.idiomatic: She was widowed at nineteen.

sentences.zh: 順治初，流寇據城，其渠聞馬有色，遣人強致之。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi roaming bandits held the city; their chief, hearing Ma was beautiful, sent men to seize her by force.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, bandits held the city. Their chief, hearing Ma was beautiful, sent men to take her by force.

sentences.zh: 馬居樓上，揮雜器物擲樓下，厲聲叱其人曰：「白若渠，欲強污我，惟有頭可斷耳！

translations.literal: Ma stayed on the upper floor, hurled miscellaneous objects down, and shouted fiercely at the men, "Tell your chief—if he wishes to violate me by force, he may have only my head!"
translations.idiomatic: Ma barricaded herself upstairs, hurled whatever she could find at them, and shouted, "Tell your chief—if he wants me by force, he may have only my head!"

sentences.zh: 」渠聞，亦愕曰：「烈婦！

translations.literal: The chief heard and also exclaimed in astonishment, "A martyr!
translations.idiomatic: The chief heard and exclaimed in wonder, "A woman of iron!

sentences.zh: 烈婦！

translations.literal: A martyr!
translations.idiomatic: A martyr!

sentences.zh: 」卒得免。

translations.literal: In the end she was spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the end she was left unharmed.

sentences.zh: 郭俊清女蓮姑，巴州人。

translations.literal: Lian'gu, daughter of Guo Junqing, was from Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lian'gu, daughter of Guo Junqing, was from Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年九月，教匪破城，掠以去，女罵不絕。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Jiaqing, sect rebels broke the city and carried her off; the girl cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Jiaqing, religious rebels stormed the city and carried her off. She cursed them without pause.

sentences.zh: 賊褫其衣，罵愈厲，殺之，書其背曰「烈女屍」。

translations.literal: The bandits stripped her clothing; she cursed all the more fiercely and was killed; they wrote on her back "Corpse of a martyr woman."
translations.idiomatic: They stripped her; she cursed all the more fiercely and was killed. On her back they wrote, "Corpse of a martyr."

sentences.zh: 張問行妻楊，秦州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenxing's wife Yang was from Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenxing's wife Yang was from Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 同治間回亂，破其堡。

translations.literal: During the Tongzhi Muslim rebellion her fort was broken.
translations.idiomatic: During the Muslim rebellion of Tongzhi her fortified village fell.

sentences.zh: 楊遣三子行，持廚刀倚扉罵賊，賊剺其口至耳際，罵猶不已，遂死。

translations.literal: Yang sent her three sons away, took a kitchen knife, leaned against the door and cursed the bandits; they slashed her mouth to her ears; she still cursed without cease and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang sent her three sons away, took up a kitchen knife, and leaning in the doorway cursed the rebels. They slashed her mouth to her ears; she still cursed until they killed her.

sentences.zh: 賊舉扉掩其屍，書其上曰：「此張監生妻楊烈婦，毋損其屍。

translations.literal: The bandits raised the door to cover her corpse and wrote upon it, "This is the corpse of Yang, martyr wife of Student Zhang—do not harm her body.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels lifted the door to cover her body and wrote on it, "This is Yang, martyr wife of Student Zhang—do not harm this corpse.

sentences.zh: 張聯標妾傅，泰順人。

translations.literal: Fu, concubine of Zhang Lianbiao, was from Taishun.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, concubine of Zhang Lianbiao, was from Taishun.

sentences.zh: 聯標為羅陽知縣，傅從，年方笄。

translations.literal: Lianbiao was magistrate of Luoyang; Fu accompanied him, not yet having come of age.
translations.idiomatic: Lianbiao was magistrate of Luoyang; Fu went with him, still a young girl.

sentences.zh: 山寇破縣，被執。

translations.literal: Mountain bandits broke the county; she was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain bandits stormed the county and seized her.

sentences.zh: 賊渠令其徒百方誘之，不從。

translations.literal: The bandit chief ordered his followers to tempt her in every way; she would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Their chief had his men try every means to seduce her; she would not yield.

sentences.zh: 一夕，擁至渠所，諸賊執刀夾左右，怵以死，終不屈，乃縊殺之。

translations.literal: One evening they brought her to the chief's place; the bandits held knives on both sides, threatened her with death, but to the end she would not yield, and they strangled her.
translations.idiomatic: One night they brought her to the chief. Bandits flanked her with blades and threatened death, but she would not yield, and they strangled her.

sentences.zh: 林乾妻程，漳浦人。

translations.literal: Lin Qian's wife Cheng was from Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Qian's wife Cheng was from Zhangpu.

sentences.zh: 有殊色。

translations.literal: She had exceptional beauty.
translations.idiomatic: She was exceptionally beautiful.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，縣有劉暢者，為盜馬婆山。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, one Liu Chang of the county became a bandit at Maposhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi a man of the county named Liu Chang turned bandit at Mapo Mountain.

sentences.zh: 掠程至，將★之，不從。

translations.literal: They seized Cheng and were about to violate her; she would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Cheng and meant to violate her; she refused.

sentences.zh: 使他婦惎之曰：「我曹已至此，即完節，誰復能信？

translations.literal: They had another woman provoke her, saying, "We have already come to this—even if you preserve your chastity complete, who will believe it?"
translations.idiomatic: Another captive woman taunted her: "We are already here—even if you keep your virtue intact, who will believe you?"

sentences.zh: 」程曰：「吾自行吾志，非求人信，豈能效汝曹無恥耶！

translations.literal: Cheng said, "I follow my own will—not to win others' belief. How could I imitate you shameless ones!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "I act on my own conscience, not for others' approval. Would I imitate your shamelessness?"

sentences.zh: 」暢殺之。

translations.literal: Chang killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Chang killed her.

sentences.zh: 楊應鶚妾佟，奉天人。

translations.literal: Yang Yinghe's concubine Tong was from Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yinghe's concubine Tong was from Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 應鶚官貴陽同知，吳三桂叛，檄署官，應鶚力拒，乃置諸順寧。

translations.literal: Yinghe was subprefect of Guiyang; Wu Sangui rebelled and summoned him to an acting post; Yinghe firmly refused and was placed at Shunning.
translations.idiomatic: Yinghe served as Guiyang subprefect. When Wu Sangui rebelled and offered him office, he refused and was confined at Shunning.

sentences.zh: 師將入滇，郭壯圖使殺之。

translations.literal: When the army was about to enter Yunnan, Guo Zhuangtu had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: As the Qing army prepared to enter Yunnan, Guo Zhuangtu had him executed.

sentences.zh: 應鶚罵使者。

translations.literal: Yinghe cursed the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Yinghe cursed the messenger.

sentences.zh: 佟曰：「大丈夫當毅然引決，無戀戀如兒女子！

translations.literal: Tong said, "A great man should resolve himself without hesitation—do not linger like a child or a woman!"
translations.idiomatic: Tong said, "A true man should die decisively—do not cling to life like a child!"

sentences.zh: 我請為公先，不使公遺憾。

translations.literal: I ask to go before you, so that you leave no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Let me go first, so you have no regret."

sentences.zh: 」遂縊，應鶚亦縊。

translations.literal: She then hanged herself, and Yinghe hanged himself as well.
translations.idiomatic: She hanged herself, and Yinghe hanged himself too.

sentences.zh: 黃居中妻吳，居中失其里貫；

translations.literal: Huang Juzhong's wife Wu—Juzhong's native place is unknown;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Juzhong's wife Wu: Juzhong's birthplace is not recorded;

sentences.zh: 吳豐順人，廣東饒平鎮總兵六奇女也。

translations.literal: Wu was from Fengshun and was the daughter of Wu Liuqi, regional commander of Raoping in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was from Fengshun, daughter of Wu Liuqi, regional commander of Raoping in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，居中為蒼梧教諭。

translations.literal: During Kangxi, Juzhong was instructor at Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: During Kangxi, Juzhong was district instructor at Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 十三年，孫延齡叛，梧州戍兵應之，入其室，吳曰：「封疆之事，固知非若曹所能，若曹其俘我乎？

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Sun Yanling rebelled; Wuzhou garrison troops joined him and entered their room; Wu said, "Matters of the frontier—I know well that such as you cannot manage them. Will you take me captive?"
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Sun Yanling rebelled. Wuzhou garrison troops mutinied and entered their quarters. Wu said, "Frontier affairs are beyond the likes of you. Do you mean to take me prisoner?"

sentences.zh: 我將待之！

translations.literal: I shall wait for you!"
translations.idiomatic: I shall wait!"

sentences.zh: 」奮擊，殺二人，自伏劍死。

translations.literal: She struck fiercely, killed two men, and fell on her own sword and died.
translations.idiomatic: She fought fiercely, killed two men, then fell on her sword and died.

sentences.zh: 胡守謙妻黃，閩人。

translations.literal: Hu Shouqian's wife Huang was from Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shouqian's wife Huang was a Fujian native.

sentences.zh: 守謙武舉。

translations.literal: Shouqian was a military licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian held a military licentiate degree.

sentences.zh: 當耿精忠叛，守謙投書城外，言賊必敗，狀為守者所收，送郊外殺之。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Shouqian sent a letter outside the city saying the rebels would surely be defeated; the letter was seized by the defenders and he was taken outside the city and killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Shouqian sent a letter beyond the walls predicting rebel defeat. Guards seized it and had him killed outside the city.

sentences.zh: 黃請代，不許。

translations.literal: Huang asked to take his place; they did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Huang begged to die in his stead; they refused.

sentences.zh: 乃求得守謙首，綴於屍。

translations.literal: She then obtained Shouqian's head and joined it to the body.
translations.idiomatic: She recovered his head and joined it to the corpse.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，自具棺衾，飲藥死。

translations.literal: When the burial was complete, she prepared her own coffin and shroud, took poison, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After burial she prepared her own coffin and shroud, took poison, and died.

sentences.zh: 沈棠妻俞，莆田人。

translations.literal: Shen Tang's wife Yu was from Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tang's wife Yu was from Putian.

sentences.zh: 年十八，美。

translations.literal: At eighteen she was beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen she was beautiful.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠兵至，執俞，並及棠。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong's troops came, they seized Yu and also seized Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong's soldiers came they seized both Yu and Tang.

sentences.zh: 俞計脫棠，乃抗賊。

translations.literal: Yu planned to free Tang and therefore resisted the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yu schemed to free Tang and defied the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊威以刃，就刃；

translations.literal: The bandits threatened her with blades; she went to the blade;
translations.idiomatic: They threatened her with blades; she pressed herself to the blade;

sentences.zh: 迫以火，赴火；

translations.literal: they forced her with fire; she went to the fire;
translations.idiomatic: they threatened fire; she threw herself into the fire;

sentences.zh: 幽之，遂自縊，賊磔其屍。

translations.literal: they confined her, and she hanged herself; the bandits dismembered her corpse.
translations.idiomatic: they imprisoned her, and she hanged herself; the rebels dismembered her body.

sentences.zh: 同時福清陳得棟妻蔣，陳雲元妻週，皆為賊磔。

translations.literal: At the same time in Fuqing, Jiang, wife of Chen Dedong, and Zhou, wife of Chen Yun'yuan, were both dismembered by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time in Fuqing, Jiang wife of Chen Dedong and Zhou wife of Chen Yun'yuan were also dismembered by rebels.

sentences.zh: 莆田林振先妻鄭支解，永安黃尾四妻鄭刳孕，貴溪傅護妻薛剖腹，臟腑盡出。

translations.literal: In Putian, Zheng, wife of Lin Zhenxian, was cut limb from limb; in Yong'an, Zheng, wife of Huang Weisi, was disemboweled while pregnant; in Guixi, Xue, wife of Fu Hu, was cut open and her entrails entirely removed.
translations.idiomatic: In Putian, Zheng wife of Lin Zhenxian was hacked apart; in Yong'an, Zheng wife of Huang Weisi was disemboweled while pregnant; in Guixi, Xue wife of Fu Hu was cut open and her bowels removed.

sentences.zh: 汪二蛟母徐，妻戴，開化人。

translations.literal: Xu, mother of Wang Erjiao, and Dai, his wife, were from Kaihua.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, mother of Wang Erjiao, and Dai his wife, were from Kaihua.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，耿精忠兵入浙江境，開化陷，二蛟及母、妻行避賊。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, Geng Jingzhong's troops entered Zhejiang; Kaihua fell; Erjiao and his mother and wife fled to escape the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13, Geng Jingzhong's army entered Zhejiang and Kaihua fell. Erjiao fled with his mother and wife.

sentences.zh: 賊至，縛二蛟，驅其母、妻以行。

translations.literal: When bandits came they bound Erjiao and drove his mother and wife along.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits bound Erjiao and drove his mother and wife before them.

sentences.zh: 行過大澤，戴厲聲曰：「得死所矣！

translations.literal: Passing a great marsh, Dai cried loudly, "Here is where we may die!"
translations.idiomatic: Crossing a great marsh, Dai cried, "Here is our place to die!"

sentences.zh: 」徐應曰：「待我！

translations.literal: Xu answered, "Wait for me!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu called, "Wait for me!"

sentences.zh: 」賊持戴袖，戴絕袖，抱子自投澤中，徐與俱下。

translations.literal: A bandit seized Dai's sleeve; Dai tore the sleeve, embraced her child, and threw herself into the marsh; Xu went in with her.
translations.idiomatic: A bandit gripped Dai's sleeve; she tore free, clasped her child, and plunged into the marsh; Xu followed.

sentences.zh: 二蛟大呼，縛盡絕，亦赴水死。

translations.literal: Erjiao cried out loudly; his bonds all broke, and he too went into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Erjiao shouted; his bonds snapped and he too drowned.

sentences.zh: 後二年，開化复陷，劉章壽妻徐，為賊渠所得，置樓上，令兩卒為守。

translations.literal: Two years later Kaihua fell again; Xu, wife of Liu Zhangshou, was seized by a bandit chief and placed upstairs with two soldiers to guard her.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Kaihua fell again. Xu, wife of Liu Zhangshou, was taken by a rebel chief and locked upstairs under guard.

sentences.zh: 婦陽謂守者：「事已至此，幸語若主，欲婚我，當具禮。

translations.literal: The woman pretended to tell the guards, "Matters have come to this—please tell your master that if he wishes to marry me, he must observe the rites."
translations.idiomatic: She feigned compliance: "Tell your chief that if he wants me as wife, he must observe proper rites."

sentences.zh: 」卒告渠，渠盛服佩刀上，婦迎坐，解刀置案上。

translations.literal: The soldiers told the chief; the chief came up in full dress with a sword at his belt; the woman welcomed him to sit and removed the sword and placed it on the table.
translations.idiomatic: They told the chief, who came up richly dressed with a sword. She seated him and laid the sword aside.

sentences.zh: 复陽言：「奈何不為我具衣飾？

translations.literal: She again pretended to say, "Why do you not prepare clothing and ornaments for me?"
translations.idiomatic: She pretended again, "Why have you not brought me proper dress and ornaments?"

sentences.zh: 」渠諾而下，婦取刀弄之，拔出鞘，忽引自刺。

translations.literal: The chief assented and went down; the woman took the sword and played with it, drew it from the sheath, and suddenly stabbed herself.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed and descended. She drew the sword and suddenly stabbed herself.

sentences.zh: 守者前奪刀，婦揮刀斷其臂，遂自剄，渠裂其屍。

translations.literal: The guards rushed forward to seize the sword; the woman swung the blade and severed an arm, then cut her own throat; the chief tore her corpse apart.
translations.idiomatic: Guards seized at the blade; she hacked off one's arm, then cut her throat; the chief dismembered her body.

sentences.zh: 黃嘉文妻蔡，名慧奴，黃岩人。

translations.literal: Huang Jiawen's wife Cai, named Huinu, was from Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jiawen's wife Cai, called Huinu, was from Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，耿精忠之徒陷黃岩，明年，師复黃岩，以黃岩民嘗麗賊，俘焉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, followers of Geng Jingzhong seized Huangyan; the next year the army recovered Huangyan; because the people of Huangyan had once sided with the rebels, they were taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13, Geng Jingzhong's men took Huangyan. The next year the Qing recovered it and took the townspeople captive for having sided with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 蔡及其子女屬杭州駐防將，將艷蔡，欲以為子婦。

translations.literal: Cai and her children fell to the Hangzhou garrison general; the general was taken with Cai's beauty and wished to make her his daughter-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Cai and her children were assigned to the Hangzhou garrison general, who coveted her beauty and wished her for his son.

sentences.zh: 九月壬申，將召蔡喻指，蔡取壁間刀自剄死，將投其屍於江。

translations.literal: On the day renshen of the ninth month the general was about to summon Cai and explain his intent; Cai took a knife from the wall and cut her throat; the general threw her corpse into the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth month's renshen day he summoned her; she took a wall-knife and cut her throat. The general threw her body in the river.

sentences.zh: 時軍中得俘輒責金贖，嘉文方求金杭州，至，則蔡已死，乃贖子女還。

translations.literal: At that time captives were ransomed for gold; Jiawen was seeking gold in Hangzhou; when he arrived Cai was already dead, and he ransomed the children and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Captives were ransomed for gold. Jiawen was in Hangzhou raising money when she died; he redeemed the children and returned.

sentences.zh: 蔡父行求蔡屍，十二月丙子，風作，江潮湧，蔡屍乃出，距蔡死九十有九日。

translations.literal: Cai's father went seeking her corpse; on the day bingzi of the twelfth month the wind rose and the river tide surged, and Cai's corpse came forth—ninety-nine days after her death.
translations.idiomatic: Her father searched for her body. On the twelfth month's bingzi day a wind rose, the tide surged, and her corpse appeared—ninety-nine days after her death.

sentences.zh: 嘉文還，言子女得贖正同日。

translations.literal: When Jiawen returned, he said the children's ransom had been completed that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Jiawen returned saying the children's ransom had been completed that very day.

sentences.zh: 徐明英妻吳，名宗愛，字絳雪，永康人。

translations.literal: Xu Mingying's wife Wu, named Zong'ai, style Jiangxue, was from Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mingying's wife Wu, called Zong'ai, style Jiangxue, was from Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 宗愛幼慧，九歲通音律，十餘歲即能詩，善寫生，間作設色山水。

translations.literal: Zong'ai was clever from childhood; at nine she understood music; in her teens she could compose poetry, was skilled at sketching from life, and occasionally painted landscapes in color.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood, at nine she mastered music; in her teens she wrote poetry, painted from life, and sometimes landscapes in color.

sentences.zh: 明英卒。

translations.literal: Mingying died.
translations.idiomatic: Mingying died.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，耿精忠將徐尚朝攻處州，略金華。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, Geng Jingzhong's general Xu Shangchao attacked Chuzhou and overran Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13, Geng Jingzhong's general Xu Shangchao attacked Chuzhou and overran Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 六月，遊兵至永康。

translations.literal: In the sixth month roaming soldiers reached Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month raiders reached Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 尚朝嘗官浙東，聞宗愛才色，乃使脅宗愛族人，求宗愛，勢洶洶。

translations.literal: Shangchao had once served in eastern Zhejiang; hearing of Zong'ai's talent and beauty, he sent men to coerce her clansmen to deliver her; the momentum was fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Shangchao had once served in eastern Zhejiang. Hearing of Zong'ai's beauty and talent, he threatened her kin to hand her over.

sentences.zh: 宗愛乃曰：「未亡人終一死耳，行矣，復何言！

translations.literal: Zong'ai then said, "A woman not yet dead has only one death in the end—go on, what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Zong'ai said, "A widow has only death ahead—go on, what is left to say!"

sentences.zh: 」賊遣迎宗愛，以兩騎翼宗愛行。

translations.literal: The bandits sent men to welcome Zong'ai; two horsemen flanked her as she went.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels sent escorts; two horsemen rode on either side of her.

sentences.zh: 至三十里坑，宗愛紿騎取飲，投崖死。

translations.literal: At Thirty-Li Pit Zong'ai deceived the horsemen into fetching drink and threw herself from the cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Thirty-Li Pit she tricked them into fetching water and leapt from the cliff.

sentences.zh: 宗愛二女兄皆能詩，而宗愛尤工，所著詩二卷。

translations.literal: Zong'ai's two elder sisters could both compose poetry, but Zong'ai was especially accomplished; her collected poems filled two scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Both elder sisters wrote poetry, but Zong'ai excelled; her poems filled two scrolls.

sentences.zh: 長清嶺烈婦，不知其氏，諸暨人。

translations.literal: The martyr woman of Changqing Ridge—her clan is unknown; she was from Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: The martyr of Changqing Ridge—her surname unknown—was from Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，盜硃德甫佔縣紫閬山為亂，吏發兵討之，婦見掠，與其並縶。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi the bandit Zhu Defu occupied Zijlang Mountain in the county and rebelled; officials sent troops to suppress him; the woman was seized and bound with others.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 the bandit Zhu Defu seized Purple Canopy Mountain and rebelled. Troops were sent; she was seized with others.

sentences.zh: 婦好謂兵：「吾既被獲，復何言？

translations.literal: The woman spoke kindly to the soldiers, "I am already captured—what more is there to say?"
translations.idiomatic: She said calmly to the soldiers, "I am already taken—what more need be said?"

sentences.zh: 吾夫祗此子，請俟其追至，以子歸之，吾從汝去耳。

translations.literal: My husband has only this child—please wait until he catches up, give the child back to him, and I will go with you."
translations.idiomatic: My husband has only this child—wait until he comes, let me give the boy to him, then I will go with you."

sentences.zh: 」行至長清嶺，其夫奔而至，婦復請以子授其夫。

translations.literal: When they reached Changqing Ridge her husband came running; the woman again asked to hand the child to her husband.
translations.idiomatic: At Changqing Ridge her husband caught up; she handed him the child.

sentences.zh: 度父子行已遠，自擲崖下死。

translations.literal: Judging that father and son had gone far, she threw herself from the cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: When father and son were far enough away, she leapt from the cliff.

sentences.zh: 韓昌有妻李，秦州人。

translations.literal: Han Changyou's wife Li was from Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Changyou's wife Li was from Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年六月，遇寇，李負幼子，行遲，為賊及。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year of Kangxi they met bandits; Li carried a young child and walked slowly and was overtaken by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Kangxi 14 they met bandits. Li carried an infant, fell behind, and was caught.

sentences.zh: 李批賊頰罵，賊刃之七創，項未殊。

translations.literal: Li slapped a bandit's cheek and cursed; the bandits blade-wounded her seven times, but her neck was not severed.
translations.idiomatic: She struck a bandit's face and cursed; they cut her seven times but failed to sever her neck.

sentences.zh: 昌有舁之歸，夜而蘇，謂昌有曰：「必葬我松下！

translations.literal: Changyou carried her home; at night she revived and said to Changyou, "You must bury me beneath the pine!"
translations.idiomatic: Changyou bore her home. That night she revived and said, "Bury me under the pine!"

sentences.zh: 」又七日乃絕，昌有葬之松下。

translations.literal: Seven days more and she died; Changyou buried her beneath the pine.
