translations.idiomatic: Seven days later she died; he buried her there.

sentences.zh: 馬雄鎮妻李，雄鎮自有傳，李不知其里貫。

translations.literal: Ma Xiongzhen's wife Li—Xiongzhen has his own biography; Li's native place is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiongzhen's wife Li: Xiongzhen has a separate biography; Li's birthplace is unknown.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮為廣西巡撫，孫延齡反，遣子世濟如京師告變，旋見執，幽四歲。

translations.literal: Xiongzhen was governor of Guangxi; Sun Yanling rebelled and sent his son Shiji to the capital to report the mutiny, but was soon seized and confined four years.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongzhen was Guangxi governor. Sun Yanling rebelled; Xiongzhen sent his son Shiji to report it, but was seized and held four years.

sentences.zh: 康熙十六年，吳世琮攻殺延齡，遂戕雄鎮及其二子。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kangxi Wu Shijiong attacked and killed Yanling, then killed Xiongzhen and his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 Wu Shijiong killed Yanling, then slew Xiongzhen and his two sons.

sentences.zh: 李及妾顧、劉，女子子二，世濟妻董，妾苗，同日死。

translations.literal: Li and concubines Gu and Liu, two daughters, Shiji's wife Dong, concubine Miao—all died the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Li, concubines Gu and Liu, two daughters, Shiji's wife Dong, and concubine Miao all died that day.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮初見執，置其孥別室，妾趙及世濟子一、女三皆以飢寒死。

translations.literal: When Xiongzhen was first seized, his family was placed in a separate room; concubine Zhao and Shiji's one son and three daughters all died of hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first seized his family was confined apart; concubine Zhao and Shiji's son and three daughters died of cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 於是雄鎮二女相要同死，妾顧亦原從。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiongzhen's two daughters agreed to die together, and concubine Gu also wished to follow.
translations.idiomatic: His two daughters resolved to die together; concubine Gu wished to join them.

sentences.zh: 及雄鎮見執，守者梯垣以告，二女謂顧：「今日當踐約。

translations.literal: When Xiongzhen was seized, guards climbed the wall to tell them; the two daughters said to Gu, "Today we keep our pledge."
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Xiongzhen was taken, the daughters told Gu, "Today we fulfill our vow."

sentences.zh: 」為繯於梁，語顧曰：「夫人諸母行，宜位於中，雖顛沛，不可失序。

translations.literal: They made nooses on a beam and said to Gu, "You, madam, are of the mothers' generation and should stand in the center—even in turmoil, order must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: They fixed nooses and told Gu, "You are senior to us—take the center place; even in chaos, order must hold."

sentences.zh: 」顧曰：「我妾也，又無出，何敢與諸母齒？

translations.literal: Gu said, "I am a concubine and childless—how dare I rank with the mothers?"
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "I am a childless concubine—how dare I stand with the mistresses?"

sentences.zh: 」再讓，乃先縊，幼女年十五，弱，手不勝綆，久之，環不就，呼曰：「姊助我！

translations.literal: After yielding twice she hanged first; the younger daughter, fifteen and frail, could not manage the cord; long she tried and the loop would not close; she cried, "Sister, help me!"
translations.idiomatic: After twice yielding she went first. The younger, fifteen and weak, could not manage the noose and cried, "Sister, help me!"

sentences.zh: 」長女年十八，應曰：「妹怖死耶？

translations.literal: The elder daughter, eighteen, answered, "Little sister, are you afraid to die?"
translations.idiomatic: The elder, eighteen, answered, "Are you afraid, little sister?"

sentences.zh: 吾助妹！

translations.literal: I will help you!"
translations.idiomatic: I will help you!"

sentences.zh: 」已，皆縊。

translations.literal: Before long all had hanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all were dead.

sentences.zh: 董先二女縊，綆再絕，再僕地，傷額及足，三縊乃絕。

translations.literal: Dong hanged before the two daughters; the cord broke twice and she fell, wounding forehead and foot; on the third hanging she died.
translations.idiomatic: Dong went before the daughters; the rope broke twice; on the third attempt she died.

sentences.zh: 苗與劉后二女縊，李視諸人皆死，曰：「姑婦子女，皆幸不辱身，我無憾矣！

translations.literal: Miao and Liu hanged after the two daughters; Li, seeing all were dead, said, "Mother-in-law, daughters, and daughters-in-law—all have kept their honor; I have no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Miao and Liu followed. Li, seeing all dead, said, "Mother, daughters, daughters-in-law—all unstained; I am content!"

sentences.zh: 」乃亦縊。

translations.literal: She too hanged.
translations.idiomatic: She too hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 顧，名荃，字芬若，豐潤人，能詩畫。

translations.literal: Gu, named Quan, style Fenruo, was from Fengrun and could compose poetry and paint.
translations.idiomatic: Gu, named Quan, style Fenruo, from Fengrun, wrote poetry and painted.

sentences.zh: 沈瑞妻鄭，瑞附見其從祖志祥傳。

translations.literal: Zheng, wife of Shen Rui—Rui is mentioned in the biography of his grand-uncle Zhixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, wife of Shen Rui, is treated in the biography of his grand-uncle Zhixiang.

sentences.zh: 鄭父斌事鄭錦，私署禮官，蓋亦錦族。

translations.literal: Zheng's father Bin served Zheng Jing and was privately appointed ritual officer; he was also of the Zheng clan.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Bin served Zheng Jing as ritual officer and was of the Zheng clan.

sentences.zh: 瑞嗣封續順公，駐潮州。

translations.literal: Rui succeeded to the title Continued Duke of Shun and was stationed at Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rui inherited the title Continued Duke of Shun and was posted at Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 錦兵破潮州，送瑞台灣，時瑞年十五，斌蓋以此時婿瑞。

translations.literal: When Jing's troops broke Chaozhou, Rui was sent to Taiwan; Rui was then fifteen; Bin presumably gave Zheng to him in marriage at this time.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing's forces took Chaozhou, Rui was sent to Taiwan at fifteen; Bin likely gave him Zheng then.

sentences.zh: 居數年，錦部有傅為霖者謀為反間，事泄，辭連瑞，錦系瑞及其孥，而以鄭歸斌。

translations.literal: After several years, one Fu Weilin in Jing's camp plotted as a double agent; the plot was exposed; implicating Rui, Jing imprisoned Rui and his family and returned Zheng to Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Years later a double agent named Fu Weilin was exposed; Rui was implicated, imprisoned with his family, and Zheng returned to Bin.

sentences.zh: 鄭泣謂斌曰：「兒既歸沈氏，生死與共！

translations.literal: Zheng wept and said to Bin, "The child has already entered the Shen family—in life and death we share together!"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng wept and told Bin, "The child is already Shen clan property—in life and death we go together!"

sentences.zh: 請遣兒同系。

translations.literal: She asked that the child be imprisoned with him.
translations.idiomatic: She begged that the boy be confined with him.

sentences.zh: 」斌使處於別室。

translations.literal: Bin had him placed in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: Bin had the boy kept in a separate room.

sentences.zh: 及瑞將死，問：「夫人安在？

translations.literal: When Rui was about to die he asked, "Where is my wife?"
translations.idiomatic: As Rui faced execution he asked, "Where is my wife?"

sentences.zh: 」或以告，解帶使訣鄭，鄭遂自經。

translations.literal: Someone told him; they loosened his bonds so he could bid farewell to Zheng; Zheng then hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Told of it, they freed his bonds for a final parting; Zheng hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 傅璇妻黃，名棄娘，台灣人。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan's wife Huang, named Qiniang, was from Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan's wife Huang, called Qiniang, was from Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 璇，為霖子也。

translations.literal: Xuan was Weilin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was the son of Fu Weilin.

sentences.zh: 為霖事敗，錦俘其孥，棄娘有兄銓為營救得免。

translations.literal: When Weilin's affair was exposed, Jing captured his family; Qiniang had a brother Quan who secured her release.
translations.idiomatic: When Weilin's plot failed, Jing seized the family; her brother Quan ransomed her free.

sentences.zh: 為霖、璇皆被殺，棄娘矢殉，銓寬譬之。

translations.literal: Weilin and Xuan were both killed; Qiniang vowed to die with her husband; Quan comforted and urged her.
translations.idiomatic: Weilin and Xuan were executed. Qiniang vowed to follow her husband; Quan tried to dissuade her.

sentences.zh: 棄娘曰：「今日之事，子為父死，妻為夫死，復何言！

translations.literal: Qiniang said, "In today's matter, the son dies for the father, the wife dies for the husband—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Qiniang said, "A son dies for his father, a wife for her husband—what more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 」卒自經。

translations.literal: In the end she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: She hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 劉昆妻張，保寧人。

translations.literal: Liu Kun's wife Zhang was from Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun's wife Zhang was from Baoning.

sentences.zh: 昆死烏蒙之難，語在忠義傳。

translations.literal: Kun died in the Wumeng disaster; the account is in the Loyal and Righteous biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Kun died in the Wumeng catastrophe, recorded in the Loyal and Righteous biographies.

sentences.zh: 昆既死，賊遂破城，張冠帔坐中堂，呼女易璋、可璋及妾吳，戒毋辱，出昆佩刀示易璋，易璋泣而跪，張斫其肩死。

translations.literal: After Kun died the bandits broke the city; Zhang, crowned and robed, sat in the central hall, called her daughters Yizhang and Kezhang and concubine Wu, admonished them not to suffer disgrace, produced Kun's belt knife and showed Yizhang; Yizhang wept and knelt; Zhang struck her shoulder and she died.
translations.idiomatic: After Kun's death the rebels stormed the city. Zhang, crowned and robed, sat in the main hall, summoned daughters Yizhang and Kezhang and concubine Wu, forbade disgrace, and gave Yizhang Kun's dagger. Yizhang wept and knelt; Zhang struck her shoulder and killed her.

sentences.zh: 可璋亦跪，張栗，刀墮，可璋曰：「母怖耶？

translations.literal: Kezhang also knelt; Zhang trembled and the knife fell; Kezhang said, "Mother, are you afraid?"
translations.idiomatic: Kezhang knelt too. Zhang's hand shook and the knife fell. Kezhang asked, "Mother, are you afraid?"

sentences.zh: 」拾刀自鏨，亦死。

translations.literal: She picked up the knife and stabbed herself, and died as well.
translations.idiomatic: She picked up the blade and stabbed herself to death.

sentences.zh: 張語吳：「汝將三歲兒，好自匿，存張氏後。

translations.literal: Zhang said to Wu, "You have a three-year-old child—hide yourself well and preserve the Zhang line."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang told Wu, "You have a three-year-old—hide well and preserve the Zhang line."

sentences.zh: 」吳號，抱張膝，張且嘆且回刀自殊，頸且斷，危坐几上。

translations.literal: Wu wailed and embraced Zhang's knees; Zhang sighed and turned the knife on herself; her neck was nearly severed, yet she sat upright on the couch.
translations.idiomatic: Wu wailed and clung to her knees. Zhang sighed, turned the knife on herself, nearly severed her neck, yet sat upright.

sentences.zh: 吳揮乳母抱兒速去，拜張前，引刀衝喉，死幾下。

translations.literal: Wu waved the wet-nurse to flee quickly with the child, bowed before Zhang, and ran the knife into her throat; she nearly died at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent the nurse away with the child, bowed, and drove the knife into her throat.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年八月事也。

translations.literal: It was the affair of the eighth month of the eighth year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the eighth month of the eighth year of Yongzheng.

sentences.zh: 乳母逃山中，卒全張氏後。

translations.literal: The wet-nurse fled into the mountains and in the end preserved the Zhang line.
translations.idiomatic: The nurse fled to the hills and preserved the Zhang line.

sentences.zh: 師定烏蒙，錄昆死事，張、吳易璋、可璋旌贈如例。

translations.literal: When the army pacified Wumeng, Kun's death was recorded; Zhang, Wu, Yizhang, and Kezhang were honored and posthumously rewarded according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Wumeng was pacified, Kun's death was recorded and Zhang, Wu, and the daughters were honored posthumously.

sentences.zh: 楊天階妻關，開化人。

translations.literal: Yang Tianjie's wife Guan was from Kaihua.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tianjie's wife Guan was from Kaihua.

sentences.zh: 天階為烏蒙守備，城破時戰死。

translations.literal: Tianjie was Wumeng garrison commander and died fighting when the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjie was garrison commander at Wumeng and died when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 亦有女子子二，長曰鳳，次無名，關聞天階死，謂二女曰：「我當死，汝姊妹宜求自脫。

translations.literal: He also had two daughters; the elder was called Feng, the younger had no name; Guan, hearing Tianjie was dead, said to the two girls, "I must die; you sisters should seek to save yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: He had two daughters, the elder Feng, the younger unnamed. Hearing of his death, Guan told them, "I must die; you should try to save yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」二女泣曰：「父已死，兄不知存亡，何以為生？

translations.literal: The two girls wept and said, "Father is already dead and our elder brother's fate is unknown—how can we live?"
translations.idiomatic: They wept, "Father is dead and our brother's fate unknown—how can we live?"

sentences.zh: 」遂對縊。

translations.literal: They then hanged themselves facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: They hanged themselves together.

sentences.zh: 關自剄死。

translations.literal: Guan cut her own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Guan cut her own throat.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙女，不知姓氏，里居烏蒙。

translations.literal: A woman of Wumeng—her surname is unknown; she lived at Wumeng.
translations.idiomatic: A Wumeng woman, surname unknown, lived there.

sentences.zh: 倮亂，掠子女財物，女子年少者，頭人自取之。

translations.literal: When the Luo rebelled they plundered children and goods; the headman took the younger women for himself.
translations.idiomatic: During a Luo uprising they seized children and goods; the headman claimed the young women.

sentences.zh: 女與其曹二十餘輩立棚下，日暮，頭人持刀入，叱諸女去衣，不從。

translations.literal: The woman and more than twenty companions stood beneath a shed; at dusk the headman entered with a knife and ordered the women to strip; they would not.
translations.idiomatic: She and twenty others stood under a shed. At dusk the headman came with a blade and ordered them to strip; they refused.

sentences.zh: 擊以刀脊，次及女，女年十五六，有容色，堅不從。

translations.literal: He struck them with the flat of the blade; when it came to the woman, she was fifteen or sixteen and comely, and firmly would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: He beat them with the flat of the blade. She was fifteen or sixteen and beautiful, and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 頭人欲擊輒复止，小倮告有以酒食賀者，頭人擲刀出。

translations.literal: When the headman was about to strike her he repeatedly stopped; a young Luo reported that someone had come with food and drink to congratulate him, and the headman threw down the knife and went out.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the blade again and again but held back. A young Luo announced visitors with food and drink; the headman dropped the knife and left.

sentences.zh: 倮營中為坑，爇薪炭禦寒，女挾頭人所棄刀立坑後。

translations.literal: In the Luo camp they dug pits and burned charcoal for warmth; the woman seized the headman's discarded knife and stood behind the pit.
translations.idiomatic: The camp had pits burning charcoal for warmth. She took the discarded knife and stood behind the pit.

sentences.zh: 頭人醉，復入就女，張兩手將抱持，女迎刺洞其胸，僕地死。

translations.literal: The headman, drunk, entered again and approached the woman, spreading his arms to seize her; she met him with a thrust that pierced his chest, and he fell dead.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he returned and reached for her. She stabbed him through the chest and he fell dead.

sentences.zh: 眾倮驚，就視，女已自剄，群碎其屍。

translations.literal: The Luos were alarmed and came to look; the woman had already cut her own throat; the crowd hacked her corpse to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The Luos rushed over; she had already cut her throat. They hacked her body to pieces.

sentences.zh: 劉亨基女，字滿，湘潭人。

translations.literal: Liu Hengji's daughter, styled Man, was from Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hengji's daughter, styled Man, was from Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 亨基官台灣府同知，權知彰化縣。

translations.literal: Hengji was Taiwan subprefect and acting magistrate of Zhanghua.
translations.idiomatic: Hengji was Taiwan subprefect and acting Zhanghua magistrate.

sentences.zh: 林爽文之難，亨基殉焉。

translations.literal: In Lin Shuangwen's rebellion Hengji died a martyr.
translations.idiomatic: He died a martyr in Lin Shuangwen's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 滿年十六，自沉廳後池，池淺不得死，輾轉泥中。

translations.literal: Man was sixteen; she drowned herself in the pool behind the hall; the pool was shallow and she did not die, writhing in the mud.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen she threw herself into the pool behind the yamen. The water was shallow; she thrashed in the mud without dying.

sentences.zh: 賊大至，曳之上，滿罵曰：「我名家女，豈懼死乎？

translations.literal: The bandits came in force and dragged her up; Man cursed, "I am a daughter of an eminent family—do you think I fear death?"
translations.idiomatic: Rebels dragged her out. She cursed, "I am a gentleman's daughter—do you think I fear death?"

sentences.zh: 汝曹生太平，乃為逆亂，官軍至，汝曹當萬段！

translations.literal: You live in peace yet commit rebellion; when the government army comes you will be cut to ten thousand pieces!"
translations.idiomatic: You grew up in peace yet rebel—when the army comes you will die by ten thousand cuts!"

sentences.zh: 」賊劙其口，劓其鼻，罵愈厲，乃殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits slashed her mouth and cut off her nose; she cursed all the more fiercely and they killed her.
translations.idiomatic: They slashed her mouth and cut off her nose; she cursed fiercer still, and they killed her.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，得旌，台灣之民私諡曰貞烈。

translations.literal: When Taiwan was pacified she received an official commendation; the people of Taiwan privately styled her Chastity and Martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan was pacified she was honored; the people privately called her Chastity and Martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 滕士學妻滿，向宗榜妻滕，滕作賢妻楊，滕家萬妻黃，皆麻陽高村人。

translations.literal: Man, wife of Teng Shixue; Teng, wife of Xiang Zongbang; Yang, wife of Teng Zuoxian; Huang, wife of Teng Jiawan—all were from Gaocun in Mayang.
translations.idiomatic: Man wife of Teng Shixue; Teng wife of Xiang Zongbang; Yang wife of Teng Zuoxian; Huang wife of Teng Jiawan—all of Gaocun, Mayang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六十年，苗亂，掠高村，入士學家，擊滿以梃。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong the Miao rebelled, plundered Gaocun, entered Shixue's home, and struck Man with a club.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 60 the Miao rebelled, raided Gaocun, entered Shixue's house, and beat Man with a club.

sentences.zh: 滿怒罵，苗抉其目。

translations.literal: Man cursed in rage; the Miao gouged out her eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Man raged and cursed; they gouged out her eyes.

sentences.zh: 罵愈厲，遂斷舌剖腹，寸磔死。

translations.literal: She cursed all the more fiercely; they cut out her tongue, disemboweled her, and dismembered her.
translations.idiomatic: She cursed fiercer still; they cut out her tongue, disemboweled her, and hacked her limb from limb.

sentences.zh: 滕繃其兒走水次，求舟將渡。

translations.literal: Teng bound her child and fled to the water's edge, seeking a boat to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Teng bound her child on her back and fled to the river seeking a boat.

sentences.zh: 苗逐之，執其手，滕怒罵，苗殺其子，滕躍入水死。

translations.literal: The Miao pursued, seized her hand; Teng cursed in rage; the Miao killed her child; Teng leapt into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Miao seized her hand; she cursed; they killed her child; she leapt into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 作賢、家萬皆為苗殺，楊自剄殉。

translations.literal: Zuoxian and Jiawan were both killed by the Miao; Yang cut her throat and died a martyr.
translations.idiomatic: Zuoxian and Jiawan were killed by the Miao; Yang hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 黃為苗掠至八斗山，紿苗入深林，解刀揕其胸，殺之。

translations.literal: Huang was seized by the Miao and taken to Badou Mountain; she deceived them into entering deep forest, drew a knife and stabbed one in the chest, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was taken to Badou Mountain, lured a Miao into the forest, and stabbed him through the chest.

sentences.zh: 走求家萬屍岩下，亦自經殉。

translations.literal: She went seeking Jiawan's corpse beneath the cliff and hanged herself as a martyr.
translations.idiomatic: She found Jiawan's body below the cliff and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 高村又有婦，以舅方病，不忍去。

translations.literal: In Gaocun there was also a woman whose uncle-in-law was ill and whom she would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Another Gaocun woman would not leave her sick uncle-in-law.

sentences.zh: 苗至，將殺其舅，婦奪刀刺苗，殪，遂自剄。

translations.literal: When the Miao came and were about to kill her uncle, the woman seized a knife and stabbed a Miao, killing him, then cut her own throat.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao came to kill him, she seized a knife, killed one, then cut her own throat.

sentences.zh: 陳世章妻朱，義寧人。

translations.literal: Chen Shizhang's wife Zhu was from Yining.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shizhang's wife Zhu was from Yining.

sentences.zh: 世章為湖北保康知縣。

translations.literal: Shizhang was magistrate of Baokang in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhang was magistrate of Baokang in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，曾世興為亂，保康故無城，賊驟至，硃懷印坐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing Zeng Shixing rebelled; Baokang had no walls; bandits came suddenly; Zhu held the seal and sat.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1, Zeng Shixing rebelled. Baokang had no walls; rebels came suddenly; Zhu sat holding the official seal.

sentences.zh: 賊挾刃索印，硃曰：「我命婦，印在此！

translations.literal: Bandits held blades and demanded the seal; Zhu said, "I am the magistrate's wife—the seal is here!"
translations.idiomatic: They demanded the seal at blade-point. Zhu said, "I am the magistrate's wife—the seal is here!"

sentences.zh: 汝曹何敢奪？

translations.literal: How dare you seize it?"
translations.idiomatic: How dare you take it?"

sentences.zh: 」賊以矛貫其胸死。

translations.literal: The bandits ran a spear through her chest and she died.
translations.idiomatic: They ran a spear through her chest and killed her.

sentences.zh: 薛中傑女，洋縣人。

translations.literal: The daughter of Xue Zhongjie was from Yang county.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhongjie's daughter was from Yang county.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，教匪掠縣境，女年十六七，從家人行避賊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing sect rebels plundered the county borders; the girl was sixteen or seventeen and fled with her family to escape the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 2, sect rebels raided the county. She was sixteen or seventeen and fled with her family.

sentences.zh: 為賊得，置馬上，女罵，躍，僕地，賊掖之起行。

translations.literal: She was seized and placed on a horse; the girl cursed, leapt, fell to the ground; the bandits helped her up and marched her on.
translations.idiomatic: Seized and put on horseback, she cursed, leapt off, fell, and was forced onward.

sentences.zh: 經益水濱，自擲入水。

translations.literal: Passing the Yi River bank she threw herself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yi River she threw herself in.

sentences.zh: 方冬，水落，不即死。

translations.literal: It was winter and the water was low; she did not die immediately.
translations.idiomatic: It was winter; the water was shallow and she did not drown at once.

sentences.zh: 賊岸上立，好語招使上，女益匍匐求深處，賊攢矛刺之，死。

translations.literal: The bandits stood on the bank and spoke kindly, inviting her up; the girl crawled all the more seeking deeper water; the bandits gathered spears and stabbed her, and she died.
translations.idiomatic: They called kindly from the bank; she crawled deeper. They stabbed her with spears and killed her.

sentences.zh: 傅瑛妻週，寶慶人。

translations.literal: Fu Ying's wife Zhou was from Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ying's wife Zhou was from Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 道光間，教匪起，周方在母家，從母匿叢栗中。

translations.literal: During the Daoguang era sect rebels rose; Zhou was at her mother's home and hid with her mother in chestnut thickets.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daoguang era, sect rebels rose. Zhou was at her mother's and hid with her in chestnut thickets.

sentences.zh: 賊擁入，鄰婦先匿者群叩頭乞哀，週語母曰：「死生命也！

translations.literal: Bandits crowded in; neighboring women who had hidden first all kowtowed begging mercy; Zhou said to her mother, "Life and death are fate!"
translations.idiomatic: Bandits burst in. Neighbors kowtowed for mercy. Zhou told her mother, "Life and death are fate!"

sentences.zh: 奈何降志於此曹乎？

translations.literal: Why lower our will before such as these?"
translations.idiomatic: Why bow our spirits to such men?"

sentences.zh: 」乃舉袂蒙其首伏母懷。

translations.literal: She then raised her sleeve to cover her head and lay against her mother's breast.
translations.idiomatic: She covered her head with her sleeve and hid in her mother's arms.

sentences.zh: 賊迫視之，美，挾上馬，二賊挾以行。

translations.literal: The bandits forced a look; she was beautiful; they seized her onto a horse; two bandits flanked her as they went.
translations.idiomatic: They saw she was beautiful, seized her onto a horse, and two bandits rode on either side.

sentences.zh: 週罵賊，賊撫其背為好語，週以指剺面罵益急。

translations.literal: Zhou cursed the bandits; they stroked her back with kind words; Zhou scratched her face with her fingers and cursed all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: She cursed them; they spoke softly and stroked her back; she clawed her own face and cursed fiercer still.

sentences.zh: 賊刺其肋，推墜馬，死亂刃下。

translations.literal: The bandits stabbed her ribs, pushed her from the horse, and she died under random blades.
translations.idiomatic: They stabbed her side, threw her from the horse, and hacked her to death.

sentences.zh: 任寨村二十烈女，任寨村寶豐縣村也。

translations.literal: The twenty martyr women of Renzhai Village—Renzhai is a village in Baofeng county.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty martyr women of Renzhai Village in Baofeng county.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，教匪至，距村不十里，村民出禦。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing sect rebels came; they were less than ten li from the village; villagers went out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5, sect rebels approached within ten li; villagers went out to fight.

sentences.zh: 此二十人者，與同村諸婦避於樓。

translations.literal: These twenty, together with other women of the village, took refuge in a tower.
translations.idiomatic: These twenty and other village women took refuge in a tower.

sentences.zh: 教匪入村，攻樓，不能克，乃收禾黍積​​樓下，環而焚焉。

translations.literal: Sect rebels entered the village, attacked the tower but could not take it, then gathered grain and piled it below and burned it all around.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels could not storm the tower, piled grain below, and set it afire.

sentences.zh: 火熾，樓中諸婦有穴牆而跳者，或欲與二十人俱，二十人同聲曰：「教匪盈野，理難自拔，萬一求死不能得，何顏食息於人世？

translations.literal: As the fire blazed, some women in the tower broke through the wall and leapt; some wished to go with the twenty; the twenty said together, "Sect rebels fill the fields—it is hard to escape; if we cannot even find death, what face have we to live in the world?"
translations.idiomatic: As flames rose, some broke through the wall. The twenty cried together, "Rebels cover the land—if we cannot even die cleanly, how can we live?"

sentences.zh: 死於刃，死於水，死於火，死同也。

translations.literal: Death by blade, by water, by fire—death is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Death by blade, water, or fire is still death.

sentences.zh: 惟畢命於此，吾儕志決矣！

translations.literal: Only to end our lives here—our resolve is fixed!"
translations.idiomatic: We end our lives here—our minds are made up!"

sentences.zh: 」俄而風起，火益怒，樓燼，二十人熸。

translations.literal: Before long the wind rose, the fire grew fiercer, the tower was ashes, and the twenty perished.
translations.idiomatic: Wind rose, fire roared, the tower burned to ash, and all twenty perished.

sentences.zh: 二十人中已適人者，何李氏、張王氏、劉王氏、馮劉氏、傅李氏、任趙氏、任周氏、任宋氏、任邱氏、任張氏、任趙氏、趙葉氏、李張氏、張趙氏、崔郝氏；

translations.literal: Among the twenty who were already married: He the Li family, Zhang the Wang family, Liu the Wang family, Feng the Liu family, Fu the Li family, Ren the Zhao family, Ren the Zhou family, Ren the Song family, Ren the Qiu family, Ren the Zhang family, Ren the Zhao family, Zhao the Ye family, Li the Zhang family, Zhang the Zhao family, Cui the Hao family;
translations.idiomatic: The married among them were: He née Li, Zhang née Wang, Liu née Wang, Feng née Liu, Fu née Li, Ren née Zhao, Ren née Zhou, Ren née Song, Ren née Qiu, Ren née Zhang, Ren née Zhao, Zhao née Ye, Li née Zhang, Zhang née Zhao, Cui née Hao;

sentences.zh: 未字者，何氏、馮氏、傅氏、熊氏、崔氏。

translations.literal: unmarried: the He, Feng, Fu, Xiong, and Cui families.
translations.idiomatic: unmarried: He, Feng, Fu, Xiong, and Cui.

sentences.zh: 王自正妻馬，秦安人。

translations.literal: Wang Zizheng's wife Ma was from Qin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zizheng's wife Ma was from Qin'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，教匪破縣，馬被掠，罵不已，刀脅之，益厲，眥裂血，賊積薪焚殺之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing sect rebels broke the county; Ma was seized and cursed without cease; they threatened her with blades and she grew fiercer; her eyes split and bled; the bandits piled firewood and burned her to death.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 rebels took the county. Ma was seized and cursed without stop; threatened with blades she cursed fiercer; blood split from her eyes; they burned her alive.

sentences.zh: 強逢泰妻徐，韓城人。

translations.literal: Qiang Fengtai's wife Xu was from Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Fengtai's wife Xu was from Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 逢泰父克捷，嘉慶間官滑縣知縣。

translations.literal: Fengtai's father Kejie was magistrate of Hua county in the Jiaqing era.
translations.idiomatic: Fengtai's father Kejie was Hua county magistrate under Jiaqing.

sentences.zh: 十八年九月庚午，李文成之徒為亂，克捷及其妻殉焉。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu of the ninth month of the eighteenth year, Li Wencheng's followers rebelled; Kejie and his wife died martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth month's gengwu day in the eighteenth year, Li Wencheng's rebels rose; Kejie and his wife died as martyrs.

sentences.zh: 前一月，逢泰將其弟望泰歸取婦。

translations.literal: One month earlier Fengtai was bringing his younger brother Wangtai home to fetch his bride.
translations.idiomatic: A month earlier Fengtai was bringing his brother Wangtai home to marry.

sentences.zh: 亂作，徐罵賊不為屈，賊縶徐釘著廳事柱上，臠割之，棄其骨。

translations.literal: When the disorder broke out Xu cursed the bandits and would not yield; the bandits bound Xu and nailed her to a hall pillar, cut her flesh piece by piece, and cast away her bones.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out Xu cursed the rebels and would not yield. They nailed her to a hall pillar, flayed her piece by piece, and cast away her bones.

sentences.zh: 事聞，仁宗以徐死事烈，命諡節烈，贈恭人，附祀克捷祠。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Emperor Renzong, because Xu's death was fiercely loyal, ordered her styled Chastity and Martyrdom, granted the title of Lady, and enshrined her in Kejie's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong honored her death, styled her Chastity and Martyrdom, granted Lady, and enshrined her with Kejie.

sentences.zh: 方振聲妻張，大興人；

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of Fang Zhensheng, was from Daxing;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, wife of Fang Zhensheng, was from Daxing;

sentences.zh: 陳玉威妻唐，台灣人。

translations.literal: Tang, wife of Chen Yuwei, was from Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang, wife of Chen Yuwei, was from Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 振聲官嘉義縣鬥六門縣丞，玉威官台灣北路協把總。

translations.literal: Zhensheng was assistant magistrate at Douliumen in Jiayi county; Yuwei was company commander of the Taiwan north route.
translations.idiomatic: Zhensheng was assistant magistrate at Douliumen, Jiayi; Yuwei was company commander on Taiwan's north route.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年十一月，盜張炳為亂，遣其徒黃城攻鬥六門，振聲、玉威與千總唐步衢拒戰，皆死之，張、唐殉焉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year of Daoguang the bandit Zhang Bing rebelled and sent his follower Huang Cheng to attack Douliumen; Zhensheng, Yuwei, and battalion commander Tang Buqu resisted and all died; Zhang and Tang died martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 12's eleventh month Zhang Bing rebelled and sent Huang Cheng against Douliumen. Zhensheng, Yuwei, and Tang Buqu resisted and died; Zhang and Tang were martyrs.

sentences.zh: 張罵賊，劓鼻剜舌死尤慘。

translations.literal: Zhang cursed the bandits; they cut off her nose and gouged out her tongue—her death was especially cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang cursed the rebels; they cut off her nose and gouged out her tongue—her death was especially cruel.

sentences.zh: 其幼女亦從死。

translations.literal: Her young daughter died with her.
translations.idiomatic: Her young daughter died with her.

sentences.zh: 宣宗命張、唐並諡節烈，附祀振聲、玉威祠。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered Zhang and Tang both styled Chastity and Martyrdom and enshrined in the temples of Zhensheng and Yuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong styled both Zhang and Tang Chastity and Martyrdom and enshrined them with their husbands.

sentences.zh: 終清世，婦人得諡者凡三人。

translations.literal: Throughout the Qing, women who received posthumous styles numbered only three.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Qing dynasty only three women received posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 克捷、振聲、玉威語在忠義傳。

translations.literal: The accounts of Kejie, Zhensheng, and Yuwei are in the Loyal and Righteous biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Accounts of Kejie, Zhensheng, and Yuwei appear in the Loyal and Righteous biographies.

sentences.zh: 寶豐二婦，不知其氏，縣察河寨人。

translations.literal: Two women of Baofeng—their surnames are unknown; they were from Chahe Stockade in the county.
translations.idiomatic: Two women of Baofeng, surnames unknown, from Chahe Stockade.

sentences.zh: 道光中，教匪為亂，官軍逐捕，以車載火藥留置寨中，為教匪所诇，將攘而有之。

translations.literal: During Daoguang, sect rebels made disorder; government troops pursued them; gunpowder was carried by cart and left in the stockade; sect rebels spied it out and were about to seize it.
translations.idiomatic: During Daoguang, sect rebels rose and troops pursued them. Gunpowder was stored in the stockade; rebels learned of it and meant to seize it.

sentences.zh: 攻寨急，墮其一隅為陂陀，肉薄以登。

translations.literal: The attack on the stockade was fierce; one corner fell into rubble and they pressed close to scale it.
translations.idiomatic: The assault was fierce; one corner collapsed and they climbed the rubble.

sentences.zh: 二婦見賊入，大呼曰：「寨破矣！

translations.literal: When the two women saw bandits enter, they cried loudly, "The stockade is broken!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing rebels enter, the two women shouted, "The stockade has fallen!"

sentences.zh: 火藥且資賊，奈何？

translations.literal: The gunpowder will supply the bandits—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The powder will arm the rebels—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 」寨中人皆潛避，無應者。

translations.literal: Everyone in the stockade had hidden and fled; none answered.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the stockade had fled; no one answered.

sentences.zh: 二婦從風而火，藥盡焚，煙湧塵起，蓬勃雺晦如夜，賊自相鬥殺，二婦燔焉。

translations.literal: The two women set fire with the wind; the powder was all burned; smoke surged and dust rose, dense and dark as night; the bandits fought and killed one another; the two women were burned.
translations.idiomatic: They set the powder alight. Smoke and dust blotted out the day; rebels fought each other in the blast; the two women burned with it.

sentences.zh: 戴鈞衡妻李、妾劉，桐城人。

translations.literal: Dai Junheng's wife Li and concubine Liu were from Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Junheng's wife Li and concubine Liu were from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 鈞衡，文苑有傳。

translations.literal: Junheng has a biography in the Literary Grove.
translations.idiomatic: Junheng has a biography in the Literary Grove section.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，洪秀全之徒攻縣，鈞衡避舒城，李、劉及二女居。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng, Hong Xiuquan's followers attacked the county; Junheng fled to Shucheng; Li, Liu, and the two daughters remained.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng, Taiping forces attacked the county. Junheng fled to Shucheng; Li, Liu, and two daughters stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 寇至，仲女年十六，抗刃死，李、劉皆被掠。

translations.literal: When bandits came, the second daughter, sixteen, resisted with a blade and died; Li and Liu were both seized.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels came the second daughter, sixteen, fought with a blade and died. Li and Liu were seized.

sentences.zh: 寇使他所掠婦與李處，李陽與諸婦語，納手入袖。

translations.literal: The bandits placed other seized women with Li; Li pretended to converse with the women and slipped her hand into her sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels quartered other captives with Li. She feigned conversation and slipped her hand into her sleeve.

sentences.zh: 忽口噴血僕地，視之，刃刺喉死。

translations.literal: Suddenly blood spurted from her mouth and she fell; looking closely, a blade had pierced her throat and she was dead.
translations.idiomatic: Blood burst from her mouth and she fell—a blade had pierced her throat.

sentences.zh: 寇欲褫其衣，其侶呼曰：「此烈婦！

translations.literal: The bandits wished to strip her clothing; her companion cried, "This is a martyr!
translations.idiomatic: They meant to strip her; a companion cried, "She is a martyr!

sentences.zh: 汝褫其衣，吾斬汝！

translations.literal: If you strip her clothing I will cut you down!"
translations.idiomatic: Strip her and I will kill you!"

sentences.zh: 」諸婦防劉益嚴，劉受李誡，以間脫其幼女囚。

translations.literal: The women guarded Liu all the more strictly; Liu followed Li's instruction and in an interval freed her young daughter from confinement.
translations.idiomatic: The women guarded Liu more closely. Following Li's counsel, Liu freed her young daughter.

sentences.zh: 兩月餘，不言，不櫛發。

translations.literal: For more than two months she did not speak and did not comb her hair.
translations.idiomatic: For two months she neither spoke nor combed her hair.

sentences.zh: 一日，寇欲污之，乃大罵。

translations.literal: One day when bandits wished to violate her, she cursed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: One day when rebels meant to violate her, she cursed them.

sentences.zh: 寇怒，殺諸東郊外，罵不絕。

translations.literal: The bandits in rage killed her east of the suburb; she cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they killed her east of the city; she cursed to the end.

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾今可以報女君矣！

translations.literal: She said, "Now I can repay Lady Li!"
translations.idiomatic: She cried, "Now I repay my lady Li!"

sentences.zh: 」遂死。

translations.literal: And died.
translations.idiomatic: And died.

sentences.zh: 陳吉麟妻周，臨川人。

translations.literal: Chen Jilin's wife Zhou was from Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jilin's wife Zhou was from Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐間，洪秀全之徒破縣，週與女仙英走銅嶺，賊及之，加劍於項，逼之，不肯從。

translations.literal: During Xianfeng, Hong Xiuquan's followers broke the county; Zhou and her daughter Xianying fled to Tongling; bandits overtook them, put a sword to her neck and pressed her; she would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping forces took the county, Zhou and daughter Xianying fled to Tongling. Rebels caught them, held a blade to her neck, and pressed her; she refused.

sentences.zh: 殺仙英，愈怒，批​​賊頰，賊殺之，屍提其首而立，賊為之驚走。

translations.literal: They killed Xianying; growing angrier, she slapped the bandit's cheek; the bandit killed her; they raised the corpse by the head; the bandits were startled and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Xianying. She slapped a rebel's face; he killed her and held up her severed head; his comrades fled in shock.

sentences.zh: 同時凌傳經妻楊，彭澤人。

translations.literal: At the same time Yang, wife of Ling Chuanjing, was from Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time Yang, wife of Ling Chuanjing, was from Pengze.

sentences.zh: 與姑匿山中，賊搜得姑，楊持刀奔赴。

translations.literal: She hid with her mother-in-law in the mountains; bandits found the mother-in-law; Yang seized a knife and rushed forward.
translations.idiomatic: She hid with her mother-in-law in the hills. When rebels found the older woman, Yang ran forward with a knife.

sentences.zh: 賊舍姑與鬥，力盡，為賊支解。

translations.literal: The bandits left the mother-in-law and fought her; her strength gave out and the bandits cut her limb from limb.
translations.idiomatic: They abandoned the mother-in-law and fought Yang until, exhausted, they hacked her apart.

sentences.zh: 楊同縣又有賈蓮品妻韓，摑賊，為所磔。

translations.literal: In the same county Han, wife of Jia Lianpin, struck bandits and was dismembered by them.
translations.idiomatic: In the same county Han, wife of Jia Lianpin, struck rebels and was dismembered.

sentences.zh: 秦耀曾妻畢，耀曾，江寧人；

translations.literal: Bi, wife of Qin Yaoceng—Yaoceng was from Jiangning;
translations.idiomatic: Bi, wife of Qin Yaoceng: Yaoceng was from Jiangning;

sentences.zh: 畢，鎮洋人，湖廣總督沅女也。

translations.literal: Bi was from Zhenjiang and was the daughter of Yuan, governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was from Zhenjiang, daughter of Governor-General Yuan of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 耀曾以舉人官郎中。

translations.literal: Yaoceng, a licentiate, served as director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoceng, a licentiate, served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年二月，洪秀全攻江寧。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Xianfeng Hong Xiuquan attacked Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xianfeng 3, Hong Xiuquan attacked Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 畢年將八十，城破，集家人告曰：「吾家人受朝廷恩，於義當死。

translations.literal: Bi was nearly eighty; when the city fell she gathered the family and said, "Our family has received the court's grace; in righteousness we should die."
translations.idiomatic: Nearly eighty, when the city fell she gathered her kin: "Our family owes the court a debt of honor—we should die."

sentences.zh: 爾曹皆朝廷百姓，平日受承平之福，今寇亂，可愛死乎？

translations.literal: You are all subjects of the court; in ordinary times you enjoyed the blessings of peace; now in bandit turmoil, can you cherish life?"
translations.idiomatic: You are the emperor's people, long at peace—now in rebellion, can you cling to life?"

sentences.zh: 且為賊得，必有求死不得者，悔何及！

translations.literal: Moreover, if seized by bandits, there will be those who cannot find death when they wish—what regret will be left!"
translations.idiomatic: If captured, some will beg for death in vain—what regret then?"

sentences.zh: 」乃服命服，扶杖赴水死。

translations.literal: She then donned her formal robes, took her staff, and went into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: She donned formal robes, took her staff, and walked into the water.

sentences.zh: 從者數十人。

translations.literal: Several tens followed her.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen followed.

sentences.zh: 曹士鶴妻管，名懷珠，字藏真，亦江寧人。

translations.literal: Guan, wife of Cao Shihe, named Huaizhu, style Cangzhen, was also from Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Guan, wife of Cao Shihe, called Huaizhu, style Cangzhen, was also from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 士鶴官陝西清澗知縣。

translations.literal: Shihe was magistrate of Qingjian in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shihe was magistrate of Qingjian in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 城將破，與士鶴兄妻李縊硃氏祠樹上，自書衣襟曰：「陝西清澗縣知縣曹士鶴妻管氏為國死於此。

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall, she and Shihe's elder brother's wife Li hanged themselves on a tree at the Zhu clan shrine, writing on her collar, "Guan, wife of Cao Shihe, magistrate of Qingjian in Shaanxi, died for the state here."
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall, she and Shihe's sister-in-law Li hanged themselves at the Zhu shrine. She wrote on her collar: "Guan, wife of Qingjian magistrate Cao Shihe, died for the state here."

translations.literal: " (closing quotation mark of the collar inscription).
translations.idiomatic: "—the closing mark of her collar inscription.

sentences.zh: 謝石全妻廖，曾石泰妻黃，葉金題母胡，繆勝雲妻黃，皆定南人。

translations.literal: Liao, wife of Xie Shiquan; Huang, wife of Zeng Shitai; Hu, mother of Ye Jinti; Huang, wife of Miao Shengyun—all were from Dingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Liao wife of Xie Shiquan; Huang wife of Zeng Shitai; Hu mother of Ye Jinti; Huang wife of Miao Shengyun—all from Dingnan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，粵賊攻城，廖、黃皆助城守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng Guangdong bandits attacked the city; Liao and Huang both helped defend the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 6, Guangdong rebels besieged the city. Liao and Huang helped defend.

sentences.zh: 廖執刃登陴，歷數十晝夜。

translations.literal: Liao took a blade and mounted the battlements, standing watch for dozens of days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Liao took a blade to the walls and stood watch day and night for weeks.

sentences.zh: 一夕，依堞視賊，為飛砲所中，遂卒。

translations.literal: One night, leaning on the parapet to watch the bandits, she was struck by a flying cannonball and died.
translations.idiomatic: One night, leaning on the parapet, she was struck by a cannonball and died.

sentences.zh: 黃佐石泰殺賊，賊攻城東南隅，黃赴救，中火槍，猶大呼殺賊，死城上。

translations.literal: Huang assisted Shitai in killing bandits; when bandits attacked the southeast corner of the city Huang went to the rescue, was struck by a musket, and still cried loudly to kill bandits, dying on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Huang fought beside Shitai. When rebels attacked the southeast corner she rushed to help, took a musket ball, still shouted to kill rebels, and died on the wall.

sentences.zh: 八年，賊復至，攻胡所居村，金題從鄉兵禦賊，胡握析薪斧，踣賊十餘。

translations.literal: In the eighth year bandits came again and attacked the village where Hu lived; Jinti followed village soldiers to resist; Hu wielded a firewood axe and struck down more than ten bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year rebels attacked Hu's village. Jinti joined village militia; Hu wielded a firewood axe and felled more than ten.

sentences.zh: 力鬥，被重創，與金題俱死。

translations.literal: Fighting fiercely she received grave wounds and died together with Jinti.
translations.idiomatic: She fought until gravely wounded and died with Jinti.

sentences.zh: 勝雲所居曰繆家莊，土寇作，黃與妯娌發火箭殪賊。

translations.literal: Shengyun lived at Miao Family Village; local bandits rose; Huang and her sisters-in-law shot rockets and killed bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shengyun lived at Miao Family Village. Local bandits rose; Huang and her sisters-in-law shot rockets and killed some.

sentences.zh: 賊逾屋入，勝雲與其父皆死。

translations.literal: Bandits climbed over the roof and entered; Shengyun and his father both died.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels came over the roof; Shengyun and his father were killed.

sentences.zh: 黃揮刀巷戰，久之，賊大至，自剄死。

translations.literal: Huang fought with a blade in the lane; after a long while bandits came in force; she cut her own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Huang fought in the alley with a blade until rebels swarmed in; she cut her own throat.

sentences.zh: 石時稔聘妻劉，名敏和，吳縣人，家洞庭山。

translations.literal: Liu, betrothed wife of Shi Shineng, named Minhe, was from Wu county and lived at Dongting Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, betrothed to Shi Shineng, called Minhe, was from Wu county, family at Dongting Mountain.

sentences.zh: 時稔卒，劉得請於父母，奔喪，奉姑居。

translations.literal: Shineng died; Liu obtained her parents' permission, went to mourn, and attended her mother-in-law at home.
translations.idiomatic: Shineng died. Liu obtained leave to mourn and kept house for her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年夏，洪秀全之徒破蘇州，洞庭山民拒守。

translations.literal: In the summer of the tenth year of Xianfeng Hong Xiuquan's followers broke Suzhou; the people of Dongting Mountain resisted.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Xianfeng 10, Taiping forces took Suzhou. Dongting Mountain villagers resisted.

sentences.zh: 閱歲餘，力盡。

translations.literal: After more than a year their strength was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year their strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 賊自山前入，劉盛服待水次，誓死。

translations.literal: Bandits entered from before the mountain; Liu dressed splendidly and waited at the water's edge, vowing death.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels entered from the mountain front. Liu dressed in full mourning and waited by the water, resolved to die.

sentences.zh: 居三日，賊不至，姑挽令入室，劉問：「何以得免？

translations.literal: After three days bandits did not come; her mother-in-law urged her indoors; Liu asked, "How have we been spared?"
translations.idiomatic: Three days passed without rebels. Her mother-in-law urged her inside. Liu asked how they had been spared.

sentences.zh: 」則曰：「率錢輸賊兵。

translations.literal: They said, "We collected money and paid the rebel troops."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "We paid the rebels money."

sentences.zh: 」劉躍起，哭曰：「是乃降也！

translations.literal: Liu leapt up and wept, "That is surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu sprang up weeping, "That is surrender!"

sentences.zh: 降則此賊土，吾賊人矣。

translations.literal: If we surrender then these are bandit lands and I am a bandit woman.
translations.idiomatic: If we surrender this is rebel land and I am a rebel's wife.

sentences.zh: 吾以為三日中，若輩與賊決死戰耳。

translations.literal: I thought that in these three days you would fight the bandits to the death.
translations.idiomatic: I thought these three days you would fight them to the death.

sentences.zh: 今若此，何用生為？

translations.literal: Now that it is like this, what use is living?"
translations.idiomatic: Now—what is life for?"

sentences.zh: 」姑與家人輩力勸毋死，劉好謂曰：「我三日不入戶，憊矣！

translations.literal: Mother-in-law and family urged her not to die; Liu spoke gently, "I have not entered the house for three days and am weary!
translations.idiomatic: They begged her to live. She said gently, "Three days without rest—I am spent!

sentences.zh: 且少休。

translations.literal: Let me rest a little."
translations.idiomatic: Let me rest awhile."

sentences.zh: 」入室，即夜自經死。

translations.literal: Entering the room, that very night she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: She went inside and hanged herself that night.

sentences.zh: 留一紙，自書生死年月日。

translations.literal: She left a paper on which she wrote the year, month, and day of her birth and death.
translations.idiomatic: She left a note with the dates of her birth and death.

sentences.zh: 章瑤圃女亥姑，餘杭人。

translations.literal: Haigu, daughter of Zhang Yaopu, was from Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Haigu, daughter of Zhang Yaopu, was from Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，年十五。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng she was fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 10 she was fifteen.

sentences.zh: 六月庚午，賊至，亥姑抱柱堅不釋，賊擊之，十指皆創，抱柱如故。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu of the sixth month bandits came; Haigu embraced a pillar and would not let go; bandits struck her; all ten fingers were wounded; she still held the pillar.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth month's gengwu day rebels came. Haigu clung to a pillar; they struck her until all ten fingers bled; she still held on.

sentences.zh: 賊斫其肩背，亥姑罵曰：「恨不為男子殺爾輩盡！

translations.literal: Bandits hacked her shoulders and back; Haigu cursed, "I regret I am not a man to kill the lot of you!"
translations.idiomatic: They hacked her shoulders and back. She cursed, "I regret I am not a man to kill you all!"

sentences.zh: 」賊勒其頸死。

translations.literal: The bandits strangled her neck and she died.
translations.idiomatic: They strangled her to death.

sentences.zh: 戴可恆妻朱，可恆，仁和人；

translations.literal: Zhu, wife of Dai Keheng—Keheng was from Renhe;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, wife of Dai Keheng: Keheng was from Renhe;

sentences.zh: 硃，長興人。

translations.literal: Zhu was from Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was from Changxing.

sentences.zh: 可恆父熙自有傳。

translations.literal: Keheng's father Xi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Keheng's father Xi has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，杭州破，熙殉。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng Hangzhou fell; Xi died a martyr.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 10 Hangzhou fell; Xi died a martyr.

sentences.zh: 硃具衣衾，視斂如禮，從可恆轉徙。

translations.literal: Zhu prepared clothing and shroud, oversaw the encoffining according to ritual, and followed Keheng in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu prepared shrouds, oversaw the burial rites, and fled with Keheng.

sentences.zh: 明年，復還，賊復至。

translations.literal: The next year they returned; bandits came again.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they returned; rebels came again.

sentences.zh: 圍急，硃方為詩詞自若，曰：​​「我自為計久矣，何懼！

translations.literal: The siege was fierce; Zhu was composing poetry as if at ease, saying, "I have long made my plans—what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: As the siege tightened she composed poetry calmly: "I planned long ago—why fear?"

sentences.zh: 」城破，硃語可恆速將子出避，賦詩矢死。

translations.literal: When the city fell Zhu told Keheng to take the child quickly and flee, composed a poem vowing death.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell she sent Keheng away with their son, wrote a death poem, and vowed to die.

sentences.zh: 不食兩日，未絕；

translations.literal: She ate nothing for two days and did not die;
translations.idiomatic: She fasted two days without dying;

sentences.zh: 自經，絙斷，又未絕；

translations.literal: she hanged herself; the cord broke and still she did not die;
translations.idiomatic: she hanged herself; the rope broke;

sentences.zh: 夜入池死，即熙死節處。

translations.literal: at night she entered the pool and died, at the very place where Xi had died for his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: at night she drowned in the pool where Xi had died.

sentences.zh: 熙死時，少子穗孫妻孫，方歸省，聞即仰藥殉。

translations.literal: When Xi died, his younger son Suizhang's wife Sun was visiting home; hearing of it she immediately took poison and died a martyr.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi died, his younger son's wife Sun was visiting home; she took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 其祖母姚、母閔，及諸弟、妹皆死，凡七人。

translations.literal: Her grandmother Yao, mother Min, and younger brothers and sisters all died—seven persons in all.
translations.idiomatic: Grandmother Yao, mother Min, brothers and sisters—all seven died.

sentences.zh: 金福曾妻李，福曾，秀水人，有傳；

translations.literal: Li, wife of Jin Fuzeng—Fuzeng was from Xiushui and has a biography;
translations.idiomatic: Li, wife of Jin Fuzeng: Fuzeng of Xiushui has a biography;

sentences.zh: 李，餘杭人。

translations.literal: Li was from Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Li was from Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 福曾父鼎燮，官臨安訓導，寄孥杭州。

translations.literal: Fuzeng's father Dingshe was district instructor at Lin'an and had lodged his family in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzeng's father Dingshe was Lin'an instructor with family in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪秀全之徒再攻杭州，圍久食盡，雜啖草木，甚至煠雨屐緣革為食。

translations.literal: Hong Xiuquan's followers attacked Hangzhou again; the siege was long and food was exhausted; they ate grass and trees mixed together, even frying the leather edges of rain shoes for food.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping forces besieged Hangzhou again. Food ran out; they ate weeds and even boiled shoe leather.

sentences.zh: 城將破，李與福曾矢必死。

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall Li and Fuzeng vowed they must die.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall Li and Fuzeng vowed to die.

sentences.zh: 尚餘銀餅一，為福曾縫置複絮中，謂窮途得此，猶可旦夕活也。

translations.literal: One silver ingot remained; Li sewed it into Fuzeng's padded coat, saying that in extremity with this they might still live day to day.
translations.idiomatic: One silver ingot remained; Li sewed it into his padded coat, saying it might keep them alive a little longer.

sentences.zh: 俄，賊大至，投姻家洪氏屋後池死。

translations.literal: Before long bandits came in force; they threw themselves into the Hong family's pool behind the house and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebels swarmed in; they drowned themselves in the Hong family's pool.

sentences.zh: 同時鼎燮殉臨安，鼎燮弟鴻僖妻胡，避臨安村間，為賊所迫，矛舂其喉死。

translations.literal: At the same time Dingshe died a martyr at Lin'an; Dingshe's younger brother Hongxi's wife Hu, fleeing to a Lin'an village, was pressed by bandits; a spear was driven into her throat and she died.
translations.idiomatic: Dingshe died at Lin'an. His brother Hongxi's wife Hu, fleeing to a village, was speared through the throat.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，賊破嘉興，福曾之族諸婦女死者，衍芹妻倪、衍科妻鍾、鴻鑑妻徐、鴻墀妻許、鴻勛妻潘、鴻勚妻胡、鴻綬妻顧、鴻紱妻屈。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng when bandits broke Jiaxing, among Fuzeng's clan the women who died were Ni, wife of Yanqin; Zhong, wife of Yanke; Xu, wife of Hongjian; Xu, wife of Hongchi; Pan, wife of Hongxun; Hu, wife of Hongyu; Gu, wife of Hongshou; Qu, wife of Hongfu.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels took Jiaxing in Xianfeng 10, women of Fuzeng's clan who died included Ni, Zhong, Xu, Xu, Pan, Hu, Gu, and Qu.

sentences.zh: 徐、許皆有女從死。

translations.literal: Xu and Xu both had daughters who died with them.
translations.idiomatic: Two of the Xu wives had daughters who died with them.

sentences.zh: 振聲妻張，賊將至時先自經殉。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of Zhensheng, hanged herself as a martyr before the bandits arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, wife of Zhensheng, hanged herself before rebels arrived.

sentences.zh: 張福海妻姚，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Yao, wife of Zhang Fuhai, was from Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, wife of Zhang Fuhai, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 福海官廣東曲江知縣。

translations.literal: Fuhai was magistrate of Qujiang in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhai was magistrate of Qujiang in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 姚家居，寇至，城圍合，米盡食麥，麥盡食糠粃，糠粃盡食馬料豆。

translations.literal: Yao remained at home; when bandits came the city was surrounded; rice was exhausted and they ate wheat; wheat was exhausted and they ate chaff and bran; chaff and bran were exhausted and they ate horse fodder beans.
translations.idiomatic: Yao stayed home. When rebels came the city was besieged. They ate wheat, then chaff, then horse beans.

sentences.zh: 城破，賊脅姚行，姚奮起擊賊，被殺。

translations.literal: When the city fell bandits forced Yao to go; Yao rose fiercely and struck bandits and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell rebels forced her along; she struck at them fiercely and was killed.

sentences.zh: 同死者娣、姒孫、王，女杏珠，侄女滿、文、月。

translations.literal: Those who died with her were a younger sister-in-law, her elder sister-in-law's grandson Wang, her daughter Xingzhu, and her nieces Man, Wen, and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died with her were a younger sister-in-law, her elder sister-in-law's grandson Wang, her daughter Xingzhu, and her nieces Man, Wen, and Yue.

sentences.zh: 邵順年妻伊，仁和人。

translations.literal: Yi, the wife of Shao Shunnian, was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was the wife of Shao Shunnian, from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 順年，懿辰子，懿辰自有傳。

translations.literal: Shunnian was the son of Yichen; Yichen has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shunnian was Yichen's son; Yichen has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 杭州被圍，伊炊粥奉舅姑，輒忍飢不食。

translations.literal: When Hangzhou was besieged, Yi cooked gruel for her parents-in-law and always endured hunger without eating herself.
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou was besieged, Yi cooked gruel for her parents-in-law and went hungry herself.

sentences.zh: 城破，俟其姑既出，入井死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, she waited until her mother-in-law had gotten out, then entered a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell she waited until her mother-in-law was safe, then drowned herself in a well.

sentences.zh: 巡撫馬新貽上懿辰死事狀，附陳伊「生則以孝事親，臨難不求苟活，深明大義」，得旌。

translations.literal: Governor-General Ma Xinyi submitted a memorial on Yichen's death in service, adding that Yi "in life served her kin with filial piety; facing peril she sought no shameful survival, and deeply understood the greater duty," and she received an official commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Ma Xinyi reported Yichen's death and noted that Yi "served her kin with filial piety in life, refused a shameful escape in peril, and understood the greater duty"; she was officially commended.

sentences.zh: 順年弟順國妻劉，亦仁和人。

translations.literal: Liu, the wife of Shao Shunguo, Shunnian's younger brother, was also from Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, wife of Shao Shunguo (Shunnian's younger brother), was also from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 順國為六合知縣，卒。

translations.literal: Shunguo was magistrate of Liuhe and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shunguo served as magistrate of Liuhe and died in office.

sentences.zh: 劉父堃方為漢中知府，令以二子往。

translations.literal: Liu's father Kun was then prefect of Hanzhong and ordered her to send her two sons to him.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Kun was prefect of Hanzhong and summoned her two sons.

sentences.zh: 劉謂異鄉非可久居，以順國喪還葬。

translations.literal: Liu said a distant place was no fit home for long, and returned with Shunguo's coffin for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Liu said they could not stay abroad long and brought Shunguo's body home for burial.

sentences.zh: 蒐先世藏​​書授二子，督就學甚嚴，二子皆成立。

translations.literal: She gathered the family's heirloom books and gave them to her two sons, supervised their studies very strictly, and both sons came of age successfully.
translations.idiomatic: She gathered the family library for her sons, drilled them in their studies, and both grew to maturity.

sentences.zh: 陳某聘妻酆，海寧長安鎮人。

translations.literal: Feng, betrothed to a man of the Chen clan, was from Chang'an Town in Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, betrothed to a Chen, was from Chang'an in Haining.

sentences.zh: 未行而夫死，誓不嫁，奉父；

translations.literal: Before the marriage was completed her fiancé died; she vowed never to remarry and supported her father;
translations.idiomatic: Her fiancé died before the wedding; she vowed never to remarry and cared for her father;

sentences.zh: 父卒，為立後。

translations.literal: when her father died she established an heir for the line.
translations.idiomatic: when her father died she secured an heir for the family.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，賊至，焚其村，酆自沈水甕中。

translations.literal: In her forties bandits came, burned her village, and Feng drowned herself in a water jar.
translations.idiomatic: In her forties rebels burned her village; Feng drowned herself in a water jar.

sentences.zh: 賊去，戚族往視之，其廬燼，甕水沸，屍為糜矣。

translations.literal: When the bandits left, kin went to look: her hut was ashes, the jar's water boiled, and her body was pulp.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels left, kin found only ashes; the jar's water still boiled and her body was pulp.

sentences.zh: 胡金題妻俞，金題，烏程人；

translations.literal: Yu, the wife of Hu Jinti—Jinti was from Wucheng;
translations.idiomatic: Yu, wife of Hu Jinti: Jinti was from Wucheng;

sentences.zh: 俞，歸安人：家雙林。

translations.literal: Yu was from Gui'an: the family lived at Shuanglin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was from Gui'an; the family lived at Shuanglin.

sentences.zh: 賊以有色，驅使行，不從，持刃哧之，張目以頸就刃。

translations.literal: Because she was fair of face the bandits drove her to walk and she would not; they held a blade and hissed at her, and she opened her eyes and offered her neck to the edge.
translations.idiomatic: Taking her for her beauty, rebels forced her along; she refused, and when they threatened her with a blade she fixed her eyes on them and offered her neck.

sentences.zh: 賊笑曰：「痴女子！

translations.literal: The bandits laughed and said, "Silly girl!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels laughed: "Foolish girl!

sentences.zh: 」乃縶以行。

translations.literal: " They then bound her and marched her off.
translations.idiomatic: " Then they bound her and led her away.

sentences.zh: 行數十步，有橋橫水，俞好語賊曰：「雨後泥濘，縶不可以行，乞舍我，我自從汝去。

translations.literal: After several dozen paces there was a bridge across the water; Yu spoke pleasantly to the bandits, saying, "After the rain the mud is deep; bound like this one cannot walk—please release me and I will follow you myself."
translations.idiomatic: After a few dozen steps they came to a bridge; Yu said gently, "The mud is deep after the rain—I cannot walk bound. Unbind me and I will follow willingly."

sentences.zh: 」復請以兩矛夾持以上，示無死意。

translations.literal: " She again asked that two spears be held on either side to help her up, showing she had no intent to die.
translations.idiomatic: " She asked them to steady her with spears on either side, as if she meant to live.

sentences.zh: 至橋半，奮躍入水，賊怒其紿，矛刺之，死。

translations.literal: At mid-bridge she leaped fiercely into the water; the bandits, angry at being deceived, stabbed her with spears and she died.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway across she sprang into the water; enraged at the trick, they speared her to death.

sentences.zh: 王氏女婉容，亦家雙林。

translations.literal: Wanrong, a daughter of the Wang clan, also lived at Shuanglin.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong, a Wang-clan daughter, also lived at Shuanglin.

sentences.zh: 賊掠其父母，婉容請於賊：「釋父母，我從汝去。

translations.literal: The bandits seized her parents; Wanrong pleaded with the bandits, "Release my parents and I will go with you."
translations.idiomatic: When rebels seized her parents, Wanrong said, "Let them go and I will follow you."

sentences.zh: 」賊釋其父母。

translations.literal: " The bandits released her parents.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels released her parents.

sentences.zh: 已入舟，婉容出戶呼曰：「我猶有語，請少待！

translations.literal: Once she was in the boat Wanrong stepped out and called, "I still have something to say—please wait a moment!
translations.idiomatic: Once aboard she stepped out and called, "I have one more word—wait!

sentences.zh: 」且呼且行，近水，疾躍自沉。

translations.literal: " Calling as she walked, she neared the water and leaped swiftly to drown herself.
translations.idiomatic: " She called as she walked to the water and threw herself in.

sentences.zh: 賊操矛拯之，不上，遂死。

translations.literal: A bandit took a spear to pull her up but could not; she died.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel tried to fish her out with a spear but failed; she died.

sentences.zh: 鄭德高妻與方其蓮妻，皆阮氏兄弟也，蘭谿人。

translations.literal: The wives of Zheng Degao and Fang Qilian were sisters-in-law of the Ruan clan, brothers from Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The wives of Zheng Degao and Fang Qilian were sisters-in-law of the Ruan brothers, from Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 賊破縣，德高、其蓮將其孥避北山。

translations.literal: When bandits stormed the county, Degao and Qilian took their families to shelter on North Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels took the county, Degao and Qilian fled with their families to North Mountain.

sentences.zh: 久之，德高、其蓮偕入縣，為賊殺。

translations.literal: After a long while Degao and Qilian together entered the county and were killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually both men went back into the county together and were killed by rebels.

sentences.zh: 二婦慟，誓死。

translations.literal: The two women grieved and vowed to die.
translations.idiomatic: The two women mourned and vowed to die.

sentences.zh: 一日賊奄至，二婦堅坐不為動。

translations.literal: One day bandits came suddenly; the two women sat firmly and did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: One day rebels appeared without warning; the two women sat unmoving.

sentences.zh: 一賊持矛入，倚矛於壁，呼二婦具茗，二婦不應。

translations.literal: One bandit entered with a spear, leaned the spear against the wall, and called for the two women to prepare tea; the two women did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: One rebel came in with a spear, propped it against the wall, and ordered tea; they did not answer.

sentences.zh: 賊解佩刀擲地，曰：「不應且死！

translations.literal: The bandit unfastened his waist-knife and threw it to the ground, saying, "If you do not answer you will die!
translations.idiomatic: He drew his knife and flung it down: "Answer or die!

sentences.zh: 」二婦厲聲答曰：「我曹畏死，尚坐待汝耶？

translations.literal: " The two women answered in harsh voices, "If we feared death, would we still be sitting here waiting for you?
translations.idiomatic: " They answered sharply: "If we feared death, would we sit here waiting for you?

sentences.zh: 吾夫死於賊，今當殺汝！

translations.literal: Our husbands died at the hands of bandits—now we shall kill you!
translations.idiomatic: Our husbands died to your kind—now we kill you!

sentences.zh: 」遂躍起，即取刀矛擊賊，賊徒手，被數創，大呼，群賊皆至，二婦力鬥死。

translations.literal: " They then leaped up, seized the knife and spear, and struck the bandit; he was unarmed, suffered several wounds, and cried out loudly; the whole band came, and the two women fought until they died.
translations.idiomatic: " They sprang up, seized knife and spear, and attacked; unarmed, he took several wounds and shouted; more rebels came and the two women fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 周小梅妻湯，名碩人，常熟人。

translations.literal: Tang, the wife of Zhou Xiaomei, named Shuoren, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shuoren, wife of Zhou Xiaomei, was from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，洪秀全之徒陷常熟，小梅方赴鄉，湯率子漣香、女淑貞及幼子、女入井死。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng the followers of Hong Xiuquan took Changshu; Xiaomei had gone to the countryside, and Tang led her son Lianxiang, daughter Shuzhen, and her younger son and daughter into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 10 Hong Xiuquan's forces took Changshu. Xiaomei was away in the countryside; Tang led her son Lianxiang, daughter Shuzhen, and her younger children into a well.

sentences.zh: 將入井，囑長子於鄰翁；

translations.literal: Before entering the well she entrusted her eldest son to a neighbor;
translations.idiomatic: Before the well she left her eldest son with a neighbor;

sentences.zh: 脫戒指付老僕，囑持書報小梅，書曰：

translations.literal: she removed her ring and gave it to an old servant, instructing him to carry a letter to Xiaomei; the letter read:
translations.idiomatic: she gave her ring to an old servant with a letter for Xiaomei, which read:

sentences.zh: 「昨君出門，飯後即失常熟，一夜未眠。

translations.literal: "Yesterday after you went out, right after the meal I grew restless and did not sleep all night.
translations.idiomatic: "Yesterday after you left I could not settle after our meal and lay awake all night.

sentences.zh: 今水窮山盡，當死義，恨不能一言為別。

translations.literal: Now water and mountains are exhausted—we must die for righteousness; I regret that we cannot part with a single word.
translations.idiomatic: We are at the end of our road; I must die with honor and regret we cannot speak farewell.

sentences.zh: 原君平安，勿以妾母子為念。

translations.literal: May you be safe; do not think of me and our children.
translations.idiomatic: May you be safe; do not grieve for me and the children.

sentences.zh: 寄戒指一枚，見此如見妾！

translations.literal: I send one ring—seeing it is like seeing me!
translations.idiomatic: I send this ring; let it stand for me.

translations.literal: " (closing quotation mark of her letter).
translations.idiomatic: "—the closing mark of her letter.

sentences.zh: 楊某妻沈，名彩霞，金華人。

translations.literal: Shen, the wife of a man surnamed Yang, named Caixia, was a native of Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Caixia, wife of a Yang, was from Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 生農家，有力，能舞大刀，重百斤。

translations.literal: Born to a farming family, she was strong and could wield a great blade weighing a hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: She came from farming stock, was powerfully built, and could dance a hundred-jin broadsword.

sentences.zh: 俗斗牛，牛奔，彩霞手挽之，牛不得動。

translations.literal: It was the custom to hold bullfights; when a bull charged, Caixia seized it by hand and the bull could not move.
translations.idiomatic: At village bullfights, when a bull charged Caixia could seize it by the horns and hold it still.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，賊將至，鄉人集團練得數百人，推彩霞主之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng, as bandits were about to arrive, the villagers gathered a militia of several hundred men and chose Caixia to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 11, as rebels approached, villagers raised a militia of several hundred and made Caixia their leader.

sentences.zh: 時蘭溪諸葛燾團練過萬人，與相犄角，賊至則互救。

translations.literal: At the time Zhuge Tao's militia in Lanxi exceeded ten thousand men; the two forces supported each other in pincer fashion and rescued one another when bandits came.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Tao's Lanxi militia numbered over ten thousand; the two corps backed each other and came to each other's aid when attacked.

sentences.zh: 洪秀全將李世賢自龍游至，彩霞乘其未定擊之，敗走。

translations.literal: Hong Xiuquan's general Li Shixian came from Longyou; Caixia struck while his force was not yet settled and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Xiuquan's general Li Shixian marched from Longyou, Caixia attacked before he could settle in and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 總督張玉良至蘭溪，暴於民，燾惎之。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhang Yuliang came to Lanxi and preyed on the people; Tao resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhang Yuliang came to Lanxi and abused the populace; Tao bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 兵有自賊降者，偽為諸葛氏之幟過金華索犒，彩霞察其詐，擊殺數百人。

translations.literal: Some soldiers who had defected from the bandits passed through Jinhua under false colors as Zhuge's militia to demand rewards; Caixia detected the fraud and killed several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Defectors from the rebels marched through Jinhua flying Zhuge's banners to demand pay; Caixia saw through the ruse and killed hundreds.

sentences.zh: 玉良告巡撫，謂團練殺官軍，互訐不已。

translations.literal: Yuliang reported to the governor that the militia had killed government troops, and mutual accusations did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang complained to the governor that the militia had slaughtered imperial troops, and the quarrel dragged on.

sentences.zh: 賊又至，偽為官軍裝，吏不復察，金華破，彩霞自剄死。

translations.literal: Bandits came again, disguised in government uniforms; the officials no longer inspected them; Jinhua fell, and Caixia cut her own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels returned in government dress; officials no longer checked; Jinhua fell and Caixia killed herself.

sentences.zh: 楊某亦死亂軍中。

translations.literal: The man Yang also died in the turmoil of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband Yang also died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 周世棣妻胡，鎮海人。

translations.literal: Hu, the wife of Zhou Shidi, was a native of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, wife of Zhou Shidi, was from Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，賊掠世棣去，使市馬，以三賊監之行。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng bandits seized Shidi and made him buy horses, with three bandits supervising him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 11 rebels seized Shidi to buy horses, with three guards escorting him.

sentences.zh: 世棣曰：「吾鄉故多馬，四人乃不足。

translations.literal: Shidi said, "Our district has always had many horses; four men are not enough."
translations.idiomatic: Shidi said, "Our country has always had many horses—four men are too few."

sentences.zh: 」賊令募壯夫偕，世棣得鄉人同陷賊者六，導之至鄞東鄉。

translations.literal: " The bandits ordered him to recruit stout fellows to go along; Shidi found six fellow villagers also trapped among the bandits and led them to the eastern countryside of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels told him to recruit strong men; Shidi gathered six countrymen also held by the rebels and led them to eastern Yin.

sentences.zh: 地僻，遂手刃三賊，其一實陽死，世棣未察也。

translations.literal: The place was remote; he then killed three bandits with his own hand—one had only feigned death, which Shidi did not detect.
translations.idiomatic: In a remote spot he killed three rebels by hand; one had only feigned death, which he did not notice.

sentences.zh: 遣鄉人自歸，矯賊令入寧波，出被掠男婦數十輩。

translations.literal: He sent the villagers home and, forging a bandit order, entered Ningbo and released several dozen men and women who had been seized.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the villagers home, forged rebel orders, entered Ningbo, and freed dozens of captives.

sentences.zh: 夜半，陽死賊歸告其渠，將群賊捕世棣，世棣逃走。

translations.literal: At midnight the man who had feigned death returned and told their chief; they were about to seize Shidi in a body when Shidi fled.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the feigned corpse reported to their chief; rebels moved to capture Shidi, but he escaped.

sentences.zh: 賊執世棣母及胡，胡語賊曰：「吾家有藏鏹，請以吾質，遣吾姑發藏鏹，饋諸公。

translations.literal: The bandits seized Shidi's mother and Hu; Hu said to the bandits, "Our house has hidden treasure—take me as pledge and send my mother-in-law to dig out the hoard and feed you all."
translations.idiomatic: Rebels seized his mother and Hu; Hu said, "We have buried treasure—hold me and let my mother-in-law fetch it to reward you."

sentences.zh: 」姑已去，胡仰藥死，世棣母子皆得免。

translations.literal: " Her mother-in-law had already gone; Hu took poison and died, and both Shidi and his mother were spared.
translations.idiomatic: " Once her mother-in-law was gone, Hu took poison; Shidi and his mother were spared.

sentences.zh: 蔡以瑩妻曹、妾馬，蕭山人。

translations.literal: Cao and Ma, the wife and concubine of Cai Yiying, were from Xiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao and Ma, wife and concubine of Cai Yiying, were from Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，賊自嚴州循江薄蕭山，以瑩將妻妾子女避兵王家橋。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng bandits came down the river from Yanzhou toward Xiaoshan; Yiying led his wife, concubine, children, and daughters to flee the fighting to Wang Family Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 11 rebels advanced along the river from Yanzhou on Xiaoshan; Yiying fled with wife, concubine, and children to Wang Family Bridge.

sentences.zh: 遇賊，劫曹，將犯之，且罵且入水死。

translations.literal: They met bandits, who seized Cao and were about to violate her; she cursed as she entered the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: They met rebels who seized Cao; cursing, she drowned herself before they could touch her.

sentences.zh: 子景軾、女景良奔赴，與俱死。

translations.literal: The son Jingzhi and daughter Jingliang rushed forward and died together with her.
translations.idiomatic: Son Jingzhi and daughter Jingliang rushed in and died with her.

sentences.zh: 女景李為賊掠，語賊：「勿相強，我固原從汝。

translations.literal: The daughter Jingli was seized by bandits; she told the bandits, "Do not force me—I am willing to follow you after all."
translations.idiomatic: Daughter Jingli was taken; she said, "Do not force me—I will go with you willingly."

sentences.zh: 」賊稍寬之。

translations.literal: " The bandits relaxed their guard somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels eased off.

sentences.zh: 行近水，亦疾躍自沉。

translations.literal: When they neared the water she too leaped swiftly and drowned herself.
translations.idiomatic: Near the water she sprang in and drowned.

sentences.zh: 馬抱三歲子匿葦間，以瑩還，求得馬。

translations.literal: Ma hid in the reeds with her three-year-old son; when Yiying returned he found Ma.
translations.idiomatic: Ma hid in the reeds with her three-year-old; when Yiying came back he found her.

sentences.zh: 賊復至，馬視道旁舍有採菱者所遺木罌，折枯木授以瑩使乘以渡。

translations.literal: When bandits came again Ma saw beside the road a wooden tub left by lotus-gatherers in a hut; she broke dry wood and gave it to Yiying to ride across.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels returned, Ma spotted a lotus-gatherer's wooden tub by the road, broke off dry wood, and gave it to Yiying to float across.

sentences.zh: 以瑩要馬偕，馬曰：「此非舟，不能勝二人。

translations.literal: Yiying wanted Ma to go with him; Ma said, "This is no boat—it cannot bear two people."
translations.idiomatic: Yiying begged Ma to come; she said, "This is no boat—it cannot hold two."

sentences.zh: 」出懷中兒投以瑩，曰：「以此子隨君去。

translations.literal: " She took the child from her bosom and handed him to Yiying, saying, "Let this child go with you."
translations.idiomatic: " She handed him the child from her breast: "Take our son with you."

sentences.zh: 」以瑩渡未半，回望賊垂及，馬呼：「君勿念我，今與君永別！

translations.literal: " Yiying had not yet crossed halfway when he looked back and saw bandits almost upon them; Ma called, "Do not think of me—today I part from you forever!
translations.idiomatic: " Halfway across he saw rebels closing in; Ma cried, "Do not think of me—we part forever!

sentences.zh: 」赴水死，以瑩得免。

translations.literal: " She entered the water and died, and Yiying escaped.
translations.idiomatic: " She drowned; Yiying escaped.

sentences.zh: 王永喜妻盧，永喜，開州人；
