translations.literal: Lu, the wife of Wang Yongxi—Yongxi was from Kaizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Lu, wife of Wang Yongxi: Yongxi was from Kaizhou;

sentences.zh: 盧，清豐人。

translations.literal: Lu was from Qingfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was from Qingfeng.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年四月乙巳，盜李古考圍州城，永喜將出助守，語盧曰：「若聞砲，即城破，吾家世清白，慎勿為賊汙！

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the fourth month of the eleventh year of Xianfeng the bandit Li Gukao besieged the prefectural city; Yongxi was about to go out to help defend and said to Lu, "If you hear cannon fire, the city has fallen; our family has been pure for generations—take care you are not defiled by bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the fourth month of Xianfeng 11 the bandit Li Gukao besieged the city; Yongxi went to help defend and told Lu, "When you hear cannon fire the city has fallen; our house has been honorable for generations—do not let rebels defile you!"

sentences.zh: 」盧曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " Lu said, "I promise."
translations.idiomatic: " Lu answered, "I will."

sentences.zh: 」賊至，舉砲相擊，城得全。

translations.literal: " When bandits came, cannon were fired on both sides and the city was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: " Cannon answered cannon; the city held.

sentences.zh: 永喜歸，則盧率二女自經死矣。

translations.literal: When Yongxi returned, Lu had already led her two daughters to hang themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi returned to find Lu and their two daughters already hanged.

sentences.zh: 二女：長曰印，次曰改。

translations.literal: The two daughters: the elder was named Yin, the younger Gai.
translations.idiomatic: The daughters were named Yin and Gai.

sentences.zh: 又有張氏婦，村居，賊執以去。

translations.literal: There was also a woman of the Zhang clan in a village; bandits seized her and took her away.
translations.idiomatic: Another Zhang woman in a village was seized by rebels.

sentences.zh: 見井，紿曰：「我渴甚，乞解縛飲我！

translations.literal: Seeing a well, she deceived them, saying, "I am desperately thirsty—please unbind me so I can drink!"
translations.idiomatic: She saw a well and lied, "I am parched—unbind me so I can drink!"

sentences.zh: 」賊解縛，入井死。

translations.literal: " The bandits unbound her; she entered the well and died.
translations.idiomatic: " They unbound her; she threw herself into the well.

sentences.zh: 劉崇鼎母張，都昌人。

translations.literal: Zhang, the mother of Liu Chongding, was a native of Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, mother of Liu Chongding, was from Duchang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐間，洪秀全之徒攻縣，縣人治鄉兵，推崇鼎主其事，崇鼎謝母在。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng years the followers of Hong Xiuquan attacked the county; the people organized local militia and wanted to make Chongding head the affair, but Chongding declined because his mother was still living.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianfeng era Hong Xiuquan's forces attacked the county; locals raised a militia and urged Chongding to lead, but he declined while his mother lived.

sentences.zh: 張曰：「人誰無母，皆以母謝，誰當殺賊者？

translations.literal: Zhang said, "Who has no mother? If everyone pleads a mother, who will kill the bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said, "Who lacks a mother? If all use that excuse, who will fight the rebels?"

sentences.zh: 」崇鼎受命主鄉兵，張出家財佐餉。

translations.literal: " Chongding accepted the command and led the local militia; Zhang contributed family wealth to help pay the troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongding took command of the militia; Zhang gave family funds for rations.

sentences.zh: 賊至，崇鼎請母避賊，張泫然曰：「未戰而先策敗，人心散矣！

translations.literal: When bandits came Chongding asked his mother to flee; Zhang said with tears, "To plan defeat before battle is fought—the people's hearts will scatter!
translations.idiomatic: When rebels came he asked her to flee; tearful, she said, "Planning defeat before we fight will break morale!

sentences.zh: 有進尺，無退寸，此外復何顧？

translations.literal: There is advance by the foot, no retreat by the inch—what else is there to consider?"
translations.idiomatic: We advance by the foot and never retreat by the inch—what else matters?"

sentences.zh: 」崇鼎雪涕出戰，敗死。

translations.literal: " Chongding wiped away tears and went out to fight; he was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongding wiped his tears, went out, was defeated, and died.

sentences.zh: 張聞敗，曰：「崇鼎死矣！

translations.literal: When Zhang heard of the defeat she said, "Chongding is dead!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of defeat, Zhang cried, "Chongding is dead!

sentences.zh: 」遂自經，未絕；

translations.literal: " She then hanged herself but did not die;
translations.idiomatic: She tried to hang herself but survived;

sentences.zh: 賊已入，張出，坐堂上，罵賊，死之。

translations.literal: the bandits had already entered; Zhang came out, sat in the main hall, cursed the bandits, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were inside she came out, took her seat in the hall, cursed them, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 武昌女子，不知其姓氏，在賊中號為硃九妹。

translations.literal: A woman of Wuchang whose surname is unknown was known among the bandits as Zhu Jiumei.
translations.idiomatic: A Wuchang woman, surname unknown, was called Zhu Jiumei in the rebel camps.

sentences.zh: 咸豐間，洪秀全破武昌，驅以東，至江寧，楊秀清欲納之。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng years Hong Xiuquan took Wuchang, drove her eastward to Jiangning, and Yang Xiuqing wished to take her into his household.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianfeng era Hong Xiuquan seized Wuchang and marched her east to Nanjing, where Yang Xiuqing meant to make her his concubine.

sentences.zh: 女侍飲驩甚，潛置毒酒食中進秀清，持之急，秀清察有異，磔死。

translations.literal: The girl served drink with great merriment, secretly placed poisoned wine in the food she presented to Xiuqing, seized him urgently; Xiuqing detected something amiss and had her dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: She waited on him cheerfully at table, slipped poison into his meal, then seized him; Yang Xiuqing sensed the trick and had her torn apart.

sentences.zh: 滄州女子，亦不知其姓氏，同治七年，張總愚北攻滄州，其黨得此女，獻總愚，總愚使執役。

translations.literal: A woman of Cangzhou, also of unknown surname: in the seventh year of Tongzhi Zhang Zongyu attacked Cangzhou from the north; his followers seized this woman and presented her to Zongyu, who made her perform menial service.
translations.idiomatic: Another Cangzhou woman, surname unknown: in Tongzhi 7 Zhang Zongyu struck Cangzhou from the north; his men captured her, gave her to Zongyu, and he put her to servile labor.

sentences.zh: 女袖出剪刺總愚，傷其臂，群賊集，立醢之。

translations.literal: From her sleeve she drew scissors and stabbed Zongyu, wounding his arm; the bandits gathered and immediately minced her to pulp.
translations.idiomatic: She stabbed Zongyu from her sleeve with shears and wounded his arm; the rebels surrounded her and hacked her to pieces.

sentences.zh: 費某妻吳，費某，德清人；

translations.literal: Wu, the wife of a man surnamed Fei—Fei was from Deqing;
translations.idiomatic: Wu, wife of a Fei: Fei was from Deqing;

sentences.zh: 吳，處州人，失其縣。

translations.literal: Wu was from Chuzhou; the county is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was from Chuzhou; her home county is lost.

sentences.zh: 父景籓，為湖州運糧千總，因以女歸費。

translations.literal: Her father Jingfan was a grain-transport company commander at Huzhou and married the daughter to the Fei family for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Jingfan commanded a Huzhou grain-transport detachment and gave her in marriage to the Fei clan.

sentences.zh: 早寡，事祖姑甚謹。

translations.literal: She was widowed early and served her husband's grandmother with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young, she cared for her mother-in-law's mother with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 洪秀全之徒陷德清，景籓他徙，吳囑以子而留事祖姑。

translations.literal: When the followers of Hong Xiuquan took Deqing, Jingfan moved elsewhere; Wu entrusted him with her son but remained to attend the old grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xiuquan's forces took Deqing; Jingfan fled with their son while Wu stayed behind for the grandmother.

sentences.zh: 賊大至，追吳，將汙之，不從。

translations.literal: When bandits came in force they pursued Wu and were about to violate her; she would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: A great rebel host pursued her and meant to defile her; she refused.

sentences.zh: 賊抽刃出，祖姑與相向哭，吳慷慨求死。

translations.literal: A bandit drew his blade; the grandmother faced her weeping; Wu asked for death in a voice full of resolve.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel bared his blade while the old woman wept across from her; Wu boldly demanded to die.

sentences.zh: 賊系之樹上，曰：「我出汝心，觀汝心堅否？

translations.literal: The bandits bound her to a tree and said, "I will cut out your heart and see whether your heart is firm or not."
translations.idiomatic: They tied her to a tree: "I will cut your heart out and test how steadfast you are."

sentences.zh: 」刃剚胸，出心，堅如石，賊大驚。

translations.literal: " They stabbed her breast with a blade, cut out her heart—it was hard as stone—and the bandits were greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: They knifed open her chest; the heart was stone-hard, and the rebels were stunned.

sentences.zh: 就德清人求其姓氏，曰：「此婦殆有神！

translations.literal: They asked the people of Deqing for her surname and were told, "This woman surely has a spirit!"
translations.idiomatic: They asked locals her name; someone said, "This woman must have been possessed of a god!"

translations.literal: " (closing quotation mark of the townspeople's exclamation).
translations.idiomatic: "—the closing mark of what the townspeople said.

sentences.zh: 冷煜瀛妻盧，義寧人。

translations.literal: Lu, the wife of Leng Yuying, was a native of Yining.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, wife of Leng Yuying, was from Yining.

sentences.zh: 煜瀛官都昌訓導，洪秀全之徒破縣，死之。

translations.literal: Yuying was an instructor at Duchang; when the followers of Hong Xiuquan stormed the county he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuying served as county instructor at Duchang and died when Hong Xiuquan's forces took the county.

sentences.zh: 盧伏哭煜瀛側，為煜瀛理須，厲聲罵賊。

translations.literal: Lu lay weeping beside Yuying's corpse, trimmed his beard for him, and cursed the bandits in a harsh voice.
translations.idiomatic: She knelt weeping beside his body, groomed his beard, and shouted curses at the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊斷其舌，死，手猶握須弗釋也。

translations.literal: The bandits cut out her tongue and she died; her hand still gripped the beard and would not release.
translations.idiomatic: They cut out her tongue and killed her; her hand still clutched his beard.

sentences.zh: 陳兆吉妻餘，亦義寧人。

translations.literal: Yu, the wife of Chen Zhaoji, was also from Yining.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, wife of Chen Zhaoji, was also from Yining.

sentences.zh: 義寧破，賊殺兆吉。

translations.literal: When Yining fell the bandits killed Zhaoji.
translations.idiomatic: When Yining fell rebels killed Zhaoji.

sentences.zh: 餘方姙，罵賊，賊刳其腹，兒逐刃墮，呱呱泣，賊驚走。

translations.literal: Yu was pregnant and cursed the bandits; they cut open her belly and the child fell out along the blade, wailing; the bandits fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Pregnant, she cursed them; they slashed her belly and the infant tumbled out wailing, and the rebels fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 其渠聞，為之少戢。

translations.literal: When their chief heard of it he restrained them somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Their leader, hearing of it, held them back a little.

sentences.zh: 蔡法度妻簡，新淦人。

translations.literal: Jian, the wife of Cai Fadu, was from Xin'gan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, wife of Cai Fadu, was from Xin'gan.

sentences.zh: 簡早寡，美。

translations.literal: Jian was widowed early and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young, Jian was famed for her beauty.

sentences.zh: 洪秀全之徒攻縣，名索簡，言不得屠蔡氏。

translations.literal: When the followers of Hong Xiuquan attacked the county they called for Jian by name, saying that if they obtained her they would not slaughter the Cai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xiuquan's army besieged the county and demanded Jian by name, promising to spare the Cai family if she came forward.

sentences.zh: 蔡氏大忷，簡曰：「是無難。

translations.literal: The Cai clan was greatly agitated; Jian said, "That is no great difficulty."
translations.idiomatic: The Cai kin were in uproar; Jian said, "That is not hard."

sentences.zh: 」艷服乘輿出，方度谿橋，驟自輿躍出，入溪水。

translations.literal: " She put on splendid dress and went out in a sedan; just as she was crossing a stream bridge she suddenly leaped from the litter into the stream.
translations.idiomatic: She dressed in her finest and rode out in a palanquin; midway across a bridge she sprang into the river.

sentences.zh: 溪水急，求其屍，勿能得。

translations.literal: The stream ran swift; they sought her corpse but could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: The current was fierce and her body was never found.

sentences.zh: 張守一女春英，山西人，寓海城。

translations.literal: Chunying, daughter of Zhang Shouyi, was from Shanxi and lived as a guest at Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chunying, daughter of Zhang Shouyi, a Shanxi family living at Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，回亂，守一已卒，弟、妹幼，母悲泣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi the Hui rebellion broke out; Shouyi had already died; her younger brother and sister were small and her mother wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 2 the Muslim rising began; Shouyi was dead, her siblings were young, and her mother wept.

sentences.zh: 春英陽語回：「能脫我母及弟、妹，原相從。

translations.literal: Chunying spoke pleasantly to the Muslims, saying, "If you can free my mother and my younger brother and sister, I am willing to follow you."
translations.idiomatic: She told the Muslims falsely, "Free my mother and siblings and I will go with you."

sentences.zh: 」回遣兩騎使守一舊僕護之行。

translations.literal: " The Muslims sent two horsemen with Shouyi's old servant to escort them on the road.
translations.idiomatic: They sent two riders and an old servant of Shouyi's to escort the family away.

sentences.zh: 春英度去遠，入井死。

translations.literal: When Chunying judged they were far enough away she entered a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Once they were far off she drowned herself in a well.

sentences.zh: 王占元妻楊，皋蘭人。

translations.literal: Yang, the wife of Wang Zhanyuan, was a native of Gaolan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, wife of Wang Zhanyuan, was from Gaolan.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，回亂，楊從家人匿山穴中，為回所得。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi, during the Hui rebellion, Yang hid with her family in a mountain cave and was seized by Muslims.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 4, amid the Muslim revolt, she hid with kin in a cave and was captured.

sentences.zh: 楊曰：「如愛我，幸毋傷我姑。

translations.literal: Yang said, "If you love me, I beg you not to harm my mother-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "If you want me, spare my mother-in-law."

sentences.zh: 」回驅楊去，至一村，回入掠。

translations.literal: " The Muslims drove Yang away; when they reached a village the Muslims entered to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: They marched her off; at a village her captors went in to loot.

sentences.zh: 楊語途人曰：「我王占元妻，將死於此。

translations.literal: Yang said to passersby, "I am the wife of Wang Zhanyuan and will die here."
translations.idiomatic: She told people on the road, "I am Wang Zhanyuan's wife and mean to die here."

sentences.zh: 乞寄語吾夫，速負母遠遁！

translations.literal: Please send word to my husband to carry my mother away quickly and flee far!"
translations.idiomatic: Tell my husband to take my mother and flee at once!"

sentences.zh: 」遂入井死。

translations.literal: She then entered a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then she threw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 王秉堃女翠環，固原人。

translations.literal: Cuihuan, daughter of Wang Bingkun, was a native of Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cuihuan, daughter of Wang Bingkun, was from Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 亦為回得，欲挾之去，翠環曰：「釋我父、兄，可。

translations.literal: She too was seized by Muslims who wished to take her away; Cuihuan said, "Release my father and elder brother and I will consent."
translations.idiomatic: Muslims seized her; she said, "Let my father and brother go and I will come."

sentences.zh: 」回釋其父、兄，曰：「我弱不任騎，原以輿行。

translations.literal: " The Muslims released her father and brother; she said, "I am too weak to ride; I would rather travel in a litter."
translations.idiomatic: They freed her father and brother; she said, "I am frail—carry me in a sedan."

sentences.zh: 」回喜，俾以輿行，女輿中餌毒，未至回所，死輿中。

translations.literal: " The Muslims were pleased and had her carried in a litter; inside the litter the girl took poison, and before they reached the Muslim camp she died in the litter.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, they put her in a palanquin; she had poisoned herself and was dead before they arrived.

sentences.zh: 魏克明女秀蓮，涇州人。

translations.literal: Xiulian, daughter of Wei Keming, was a native of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulian, daughter of Wei Keming, was from Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 同治七年二月，從兩兄行避兵。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year of Tongzhi she traveled with her two elder brothers to flee the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tongzhi 7 she fled the fighting with her two brothers.

sentences.zh: 回至，次兄中矛死。

translations.literal: Muslims came; her second brother was struck by a spear and died.
translations.idiomatic: Muslims overtook them; her second brother died of a spear thrust.

sentences.zh: 秀蓮跪請活長兄，回許之。

translations.literal: Xiulian knelt and begged that her elder brother be spared; the Muslims agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulian knelt and pleaded for her elder brother's life; they consented.

sentences.zh: 長兄脫走至山麓，遙望回迫秀蓮乘馬渡水，至中流，墜水死。

translations.literal: Her elder brother escaped to the foot of the mountain; from afar he saw Muslims forcing Xiulian onto a horse to cross the water; at midstream she fell into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother fled to the hillside and watched them force Xiulian on horseback into the stream; halfway across she fell in and drowned.

sentences.zh: 劉慶耀妻廖，龍南人。

translations.literal: Liao, the wife of Liu Qingyao, was a native of Longnan.
translations.idiomatic: Liao, wife of Liu Qingyao, was from Longnan.

sentences.zh: 慶耀貰酒自給。

translations.literal: Qingyao kept a wine shop for his livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyao made his living selling wine.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，賊至，廖持刃衛姑出。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi bandits came; Liao took a blade and guarded her mother-in-law as she went out.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 3 rebels came; Liao armed herself and escorted her mother-in-law out.

sentences.zh: 賊執姑，廖揮刃斷賊腕，姑得脫。

translations.literal: A bandit seized the mother-in-law; Liao swung her blade and severed the bandit's wrist, and the mother-in-law escaped.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel grabbed the older woman; Liao hacked off his wrist and freed her.

sentences.zh: 賊鬥廖，廖殺二賊，力盡，刳腹斷舌死。

translations.literal: The bandits fought Liao; she killed two bandits; when her strength was spent they cut open her belly and severed her tongue and she died.
translations.idiomatic: They turned on her; she killed two before exhaustion; they disemboweled her and cut out her tongue.

sentences.zh: 歐陽維元妻曹，崇仁人。

translations.literal: Cao, the wife of Ouyang Weiyuan, was a native of Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: Cao, wife of Ouyang Weiyuan, was from Chongren.

sentences.zh: 姑早寡，年九十九矣，賊急，曹奉姑走太浮山，遇賊，姑見殺。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law had been widowed early and was ninety-nine years old; when bandits pressed close Cao led the old woman toward Mount Taifu; they met bandits and the mother-in-law was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband's mother, widowed early, was ninety-nine; Cao fled with her toward Mount Taifu, met rebels, and the old woman was killed.

sentences.zh: 曹與維元擊賊，皆死。

translations.literal: Cao and Weiyuan struck at the bandits and both died.
translations.idiomatic: Cao and Weiyuan fought the rebels and both fell.

sentences.zh: 李盤龍妻鄧，永新人。

translations.literal: Deng, the wife of Li Panlong, was a native of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: Deng, wife of Li Panlong, was from Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 賊攻縣，鄧與族娣、姒走，遇賊仕坪。

translations.literal: When bandits attacked the county Deng fled with a younger sister-in-law and an elder sister-in-law and met bandits at Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels stormed the county Deng fled with two sisters-in-law and met them at Shiping.

sentences.zh: 三婦共鬥賊，皆死。

translations.literal: The three women together fought the bandits and all died.
translations.idiomatic: All three women fought the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 娣、姒失其氏。

translations.literal: The surnames of the younger and elder sisters-in-law are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The sisters-in-law's surnames are lost.

sentences.zh: 黃氏女，名婉梨，江寧人。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Huang clan, named Wanli, was a native of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli, a Huang-clan daughter, was from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，洪秀全破江寧，婉梨方五歲，有母，與兄弟居。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng Hong Xiuquan took Jiangning; Wanli was then five years old; she had a mother and lived with her brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 Hong Xiuquan seized Nanjing; Wanli was five and lived with her mother and brothers.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，師克江寧，有兵入其室，殺其母及其兄弟，縛婉梨置舟中，謂將歸湖南。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi the army recovered Jiangning; soldiers entered her house, killed her mother and brothers, bound Wanli and placed her in a boat, saying they would take her back to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 4 the city was recovered; troops entered, killed her mother and brothers, bound Wanli aboard a boat bound for Hunan.

sentences.zh: 婉梨好語兵：「至汝家，當妻汝，舟中毋相逼。

translations.literal: Wanli spoke pleasantly to the soldiers, saying, "When we reach your home you may take me as wife; on the boat do not press me."
translations.idiomatic: She told the soldiers sweetly, "At your home you may marry me—do not force me on the boat."

sentences.zh: 」時有金眉姑者，亦被掠，自沉於江，婉梨舉以怵兵，兵不敢犯。

translations.literal: " At the time there was one Jin Meigu who had also been seized and drowned herself in the river; Wanli cited her to warn the soldiers, and they did not dare violate her.
translations.idiomatic: She pointed to Jin Meigu, another captive who had drowned herself, and the soldiers dared not touch her.

sentences.zh: 月餘，將至其家，驅就陸，兵遇其侶，與俱投逆旅，二人方共飲，婉梨見牖上有毒鼠藥，潛置食中。

translations.literal: After more than a month, as they were about to reach his home they drove her ashore; the soldier met a companion and they lodged together at an inn; as the two were drinking together Wanli saw rat poison on the window ledge and secretly placed it in the food.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, nearing his home, they put in ashore; he met a comrade at an inn and Wanli slipped rat poison into their meal.

sentences.zh: 夜分，一人毒發死，一人毒淺，未即死，婉梨掣所佩刀剚其腹，題詩壁間，述始末，自經死。

translations.literal: At midnight one man died of the poison; the other was lightly poisoned and did not die at once; Wanli drew the knife at her belt and stabbed his belly, wrote a poem on the wall recounting the whole affair, and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight one died; the other lingered; she knifed his belly, wrote their story on the wall, and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 程氏女，名季玉，歸安人，從父居蘇州。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Cheng clan, named Jiyu, was from Gui'an and lived with her father at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyu, a Cheng-clan daughter from Gui'an, lived with her father in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 蘇州陷，其父以醫卜自活。

translations.literal: When Suzhou fell her father supported himself by medicine and divination.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzhou fell her father lived by medicine and fortune-telling.

sentences.zh: 師克蘇州，季玉與其父相失，就鄰媼匿桃花塢。

translations.literal: When the army recovered Suzhou Jiyu was separated from her father and hid with a neighboring old woman in Taohua Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was retaken she lost her father and hid with a neighbor in Taohua Wu.

sentences.zh: 其女兄為部曲將所得，脅季玉去。

translations.literal: A kinsman of the household was seized by a company commander, who then coerced Jiyu to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: A male relative was taken by a company commander who then forced Jiyu to follow.

sentences.zh: 季玉自經，不死，作絕命詩畀媼，使他日告其父，入井死。

translations.literal: Jiyu hanged herself but did not die; she composed a farewell poem and gave it to the old woman to deliver to her father another day, then entered a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Her hanging failed; she wrote a death poem for the old woman to give her father, then drowned in a well.

sentences.zh: 韓肖朱妻郗，趙州人。

translations.literal: Xi, the wife of Han Xiaozhu, was from Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, wife of Han Xiaozhu, was from Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 姑瞽，張總愚自柏鄉向趙州，郗奉姑走欒城。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law was blind; Zhang Zongyu came from Baixiang toward Zhaozhou; Xi led the old woman in flight toward Luancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law was blind; as Zhang Zongyu marched from Baixiang on Zhaozhou, Xi fled with her toward Luancheng.

sentences.zh: 賊驟至，姑曰：「我瞽不能行，汝可疾逃，無以我累汝！

translations.literal: The old woman said, "I am blind and cannot walk; you should flee quickly—do not let me burden you!"
translations.idiomatic: The old woman said, "I am blind and cannot run—go quickly; do not let me hold you back!"

sentences.zh: 」郗侍姑終不去。

translations.literal: " Xi attended her mother-in-law to the end and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Xi stayed with her and would not go.

sentences.zh: 賊見其少，將縶以去，郗請訣於姑，賊稍緩，郗急趨赴井。

translations.literal: The bandits saw she was young and were about to bind her and take her away; Xi asked leave to bid farewell to her mother-in-law; the bandits relaxed somewhat; Xi hurried to a well.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing she was young, rebels meant to seize her; she asked to farewell her mother-in-law; when they eased off she ran for a well.

sentences.zh: 賊持矛遂之，郗張兩手以拒，回身墮井死。

translations.literal: A bandit took a spear and pursued her; Xi spread both hands to ward it off, turned, and fell into the well and died.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel speared after her; she spread her arms, turned, and dropped into the well dead.

sentences.zh: 賊去，出其屍，矛創七。

translations.literal: When the bandits left they pulled out her corpse; there were seven spear wounds.
translations.idiomatic: After they left her body was recovered with seven spear cuts.

sentences.zh: 張醴仁妻王，武強人。

translations.literal: Wang, the wife of Zhang Liren, was a native of Wuqiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, wife of Zhang Liren, was from Wuqiang.

sentences.zh: 張總愚之徒入縣境，王避亂深州。

translations.literal: When the followers of Zhang Zongyu entered the county borders Wang fled the turmoil to Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zongyu's forces entered the district Wang fled to Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊至，王與婦女數百自沉於滹沱，水淺，不即死。

translations.literal: When bandits came Wang and several hundred women drowned themselves in the Hutuo River; the water was shallow and they did not die at once.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels came; Wang and hundreds of women waded into the Hutuo, but the water was shallow and death was slow.

sentences.zh: 賊據河濱村二日，飢凍顛踣，一婦哭曰：「此不即死，不如死賊刃！

translations.literal: The bandits held villages along the riverbank for two days; hunger, cold, and stumbling laid them low; one woman wept, saying, "If we cannot die at once, better die on the rebels' blades!"
translations.idiomatic: Rebels camped on the bank two days; cold and hunger broke them; one woman cried, "Since we cannot drown quickly, let the rebels kill us!"

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「見殺於賊辱甚，不如水死！

translations.literal: Wang said, "To be killed by bandits is a greater shame than to die in the water!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang said, "Death by the rebels' blades is more shameful than drowning!"

sentences.zh: 」三日僵立死。

translations.literal: " On the third day they stood rigid until they died.
translations.idiomatic: They stood in the water three days until they froze stiff and died.

sentences.zh: 同縣許氏女，從其父避賊。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Xu clan in the same county fled the bandits with her father.
translations.idiomatic: In the same county a Xu-clan daughter fled with her father.

sentences.zh: 行遇賊，女促父速去。

translations.literal: On the road they met bandits; the girl urged her father to flee quickly.
translations.idiomatic: They met rebels on the road; she urged her father to run.

sentences.zh: 父陟岡望之，賊授女鞭令上馬，女持鞭鞭賊，罵曰：「竪子！

translations.literal: The father climbed a hill to watch; the bandits gave the girl a whip and ordered her to mount; she took the whip and struck the bandits, cursing, "Whelp!
translations.idiomatic: Her father climbed a knoll to watch; rebels handed her a whip and told her to mount; she whipped them and cried, "You whelps!

sentences.zh: 安敢爾？

translations.literal: How dare you act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: How dare you!"

sentences.zh: 」賊縶女，挾刃迫之，女罵如故。

translations.literal: " The bandits bound the girl, held a blade to force her, and she cursed as before.
translations.idiomatic: They bound her and threatened her with blades; she cursed on unchanged.

sentences.zh: 刺其腕，刺其肩，罵如故，遂見殺。

translations.literal: They stabbed her wrist and stabbed her shoulder; she cursed as before and was finally killed.
translations.idiomatic: They stabbed her wrist and shoulder; still she cursed, and at last they killed her.

sentences.zh: 李氏女，名蒲，饒陽人。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Li clan, named Pu, was a native of Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, a Li-clan daughter, was from Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 亦從父避賊。

translations.literal: She too fled the bandits with her father.
translations.idiomatic: She also fled with her father.

sentences.zh: 賊至，將劫之去，女抱持父，坐於地不起。

translations.literal: When bandits came and were about to seize her and take her away the girl clung to her father and sat on the ground refusing to rise.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels came to take her she clung to her father and would not stand.

sentences.zh: 父令從賊行，道側有井，父顧曰：「蒲，井也！

translations.literal: The father ordered her to go with the bandits; beside the road there was a well; the father glanced back and said, "Pu, a well!
translations.idiomatic: Her father told her to go with them; a well stood by the road; he looked back and said, "Pu—the well!

sentences.zh: 」蒲疾入井。

translations.literal: " Pu swiftly entered the well.
translations.idiomatic: Pu threw herself into the well at once.

sentences.zh: 賊並擠其父入井，同死。

translations.literal: The bandits also crowded her father into the well and all died together.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shoved her father in after her; both drowned.

sentences.zh: 楊某妻吳，武進人。

translations.literal: Wu, the wife of a man surnamed Yang, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, wife of a Yang, was from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 子傳第，以舉人官知府。

translations.literal: Her son Chuandi, a licentiate, served as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Their son Chuandi, a licentiate, became a prefect.

sentences.zh: 客河道總督幕，迎吳居黑堈。

translations.literal: He was retained on the staff of the Yellow River conservancy governor and brought Wu to live at Heigan.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the Yellow River governor's staff and settled Wu at Heigan.

sentences.zh: 黑堈在開封北，濱河。

translations.literal: Heigan lay north of Kaifeng on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Heigan stood north of Kaifeng along the river.

sentences.zh: 同治三年八月，捻匪攻開封，未下，掠黑堈，吳罵賊死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Tongzhi the Nian bandits attacked Kaifeng but did not take it; they raided Heigan and Wu cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tongzhi 3 Nian rebels besieged Kaifeng, then raided Heigan; Wu cursed them and was killed.

sentences.zh: 傳第從河道總督在開封，聞母死，大戚。

translations.literal: Chuandi was with the Yellow River governor at Kaifeng; hearing of his mother's death he grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Chuandi was at Kaifeng with the governor; when he heard his mother was dead he was stricken.

sentences.zh: 以為不能豫戒，陷母死，為母撰行述，成，抑藥死。

translations.literal: Believing he had failed to warn her in advance and had brought about his mother's death, he composed a narrative of her conduct; when it was finished he restrained himself and died by poison.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed himself for not warning her in time, wrote her life account, then took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 康創業妻，與李鴻業妻，皆邸氏，兄弟也，深澤人。

translations.literal: The wives of Kang Chuangye and Li Hongye were both of the Di clan, brothers from Shenze.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chuangye's and Li Hongye's wives were Di-clan sisters-in-law from Shenze.

sentences.zh: 同治七年，張總愚黨掠縣境，方歸寧，從其父半千登屋避。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi the followers of Zhang Zongyu raided the county borders; they were visiting home and climbed the roof with their father Banqian to escape.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 7 Zhang Zongyu's men raided the county; home on a visit, they fled to the rooftop with their father Banqian.

sentences.zh: 賊登，刺半千死，姊持梃擊賊，妹奪賊刀殪之。

translations.literal: Bandits climbed up, stabbed Banqian to death; the elder sister struck bandits with a staff and the younger seized a bandit's knife and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels mounted the roof and killed Banqian; the elder sister beat them with a pole while the younger wrested a blade and slew one.

sentences.zh: 賊踵登，揮刀墮梯下，斃。

translations.literal: More bandits followed up the ladder; she swung a blade and knocked them off the ladder below, killing them.
translations.idiomatic: Others climbed after; she hacked at the ladder and sent them tumbling to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 賊發槍，妹僕，姊被數十創，亦死。

translations.literal: The bandits fired guns; the younger sister fell; the elder sister suffered several dozen wounds and also died.
translations.idiomatic: They opened fire; the younger sister fell, and the elder took dozens of wounds and died.

sentences.zh: 王書云妻谷，亦縣人。

translations.literal: Gu, the wife of Wang Shuyun, was also from that county.
translations.idiomatic: Gu, wife of Wang Shuyun, was from the same county.

sentences.zh: 書云精針灸，谷傳其術，活婦女無算。

translations.literal: Shuyun was skilled in acupuncture; Gu learned his art and saved countless women.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyun excelled at acupuncture; Gu mastered it and saved innumerable women.

sentences.zh: 賊至，矛刺其子鳳銜僕，谷操杖擊賊酋。

translations.literal: When bandits came a spear stabbed her son Fengxian and he fell; Gu took a staff and struck the bandit chief.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels came; a spear felled her son Fengxian; Gu clubbed their chief.

sentences.zh: 賊縱火，與其子鳳德、鳳桐，女然文，皆死。

translations.literal: The bandits set fire; she died together with her sons Fengde and Fengtong and her daughter Ranwen.
translations.idiomatic: They torched the house; Gu died with sons Fengde and Fengtong and daughter Ranwen.

sentences.zh: 王有周妻楊，玉門人。

translations.literal: Yang, the wife of Wang Youzhou, was a native of Yumen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, wife of Wang Youzhou, was from Yumen.

sentences.zh: 早寡，撫三子漢連、漢元、漢科，皆長。

translations.literal: Widowed early, she raised three sons—Hanlian, Hanyuan, and Hanke—until they were grown.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young, she raised Hanlian, Hanyuan, and Hanke to adulthood.

sentences.zh: 同治三年正月，回攻所居堡，急。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Tongzhi Muslims attacked the fort where they lived; the danger was acute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tongzhi 3 Muslims stormed their fort.

sentences.zh: 楊使漢元間道詣肅州請兵，漢連以其人出禦。

translations.literal: Yang sent Hanyuan by a secret path to Suzhou to ask for troops; Hanlian led the men out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: She sent Hanyuan by a back road to Suzhou for reinforcements while Hanlian led the defense.

sentences.zh: 楊聞砲聲急，意堡破，將二女孫入井死。

translations.literal: Hearing urgent cannon fire Yang thought the fort had fallen and led her two granddaughters into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: At the sound of cannon she feared the fort was lost and drowned herself in a well with two granddaughters.

sentences.zh: 漢連妻張挈次女自經，漢元妻李率次女飲酖，漢科妻李及子三、從女一、女甥一皆自剄。

translations.literal: Hanlian's wife Zhang hanged herself with a younger daughter; Hanyuan's wife Li gave poison to a younger daughter; Hanke's wife Li, three sons, a niece, and a daughter's daughter all cut their throats.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Hanlian's wife, hanged herself with a granddaughter; Li, Hanyuan's wife, poisoned another; Hanke's wife Li and kin slit their throats.

sentences.zh: 逾時回敗去，漢連歸，則家人皆狼藉死矣。

translations.literal: After a time the Muslims were defeated and withdrew; when Hanlian returned, his family lay slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Muslims retreated Hanlian came home to find his household dead.

sentences.zh: 張金鑄妻段，平涼人。

translations.literal: Duan, the wife of Zhang Jinzhu, was a native of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Duan, wife of Zhang Jinzhu, was from Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 同治間，回亂，金鑄跳而逸，段未得從。

translations.literal: During the Tongzhi years, in the Muslim rebellion, Jinzhu leaped and escaped but Duan could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: During the Muslim revolt Jinzhu leaped free while Duan was left behind.

sentences.zh: 回至，脅以刃，不為屈。

translations.literal: When Muslims came they threatened her with blades but she would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Muslims threatened her with blades; she would not bend.

sentences.zh: 砍項折，未殊，猶怒罵。

translations.literal: They hacked her neck until it broke but she was not yet dead and still cursed in anger.
translations.idiomatic: They nearly severed her neck; still alive, she cursed them.

sentences.zh: 复斷其左臂，乃僕，回委之去。

translations.literal: They cut off her left arm as well and she fell; the Muslims cast her aside and left.
translations.idiomatic: They took her left arm too; she collapsed, and the Muslims abandoned her.

sentences.zh: 金鑄歸，段尚能語，曰：「我家長物，盡為寇掠去，惟敝書數帙，我取置懷中，君可將去！

translations.literal: When Jinzhu returned Duan could still speak and said, "Our household's fine things were all plundered by the raiders; only a few worn books remain—I took them and placed them in my bosom; you may carry them away!"
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhu found her still conscious: "The raiders took everything but a few old books in my bosom—take them!"

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「我且死，君當速行！

translations.literal: " She said again, "I am about to die—you must go quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: " She added, "I am dying—flee at once!"

sentences.zh: 勿以我故留，寇復至，君將不免。

translations.literal: Do not stay on my account; if the raiders come again you will not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Do not linger for me; if they return you will perish too.

sentences.zh: 」金鑄取懷中書欲去，返顧，段已絕。

translations.literal: " Jinzhu took the books from her bosom and was about to leave; he looked back and Duan was already gone.
translations.idiomatic: He reached for the books and turned back; she was dead.

sentences.zh: 王氏二女，香蘭、纏娃，秦州人。

translations.literal: Two daughters of the Wang clan, Xianglan and Chanwa, were from Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianglan and Chanwa, sisters of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 同治八年，回亂，掠香蘭。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tongzhi, during the Muslim rebellion, Xianglan was seized.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 8 Muslims seized Xianglan.

sentences.zh: 悅其色，以好言誘，不從；

translations.literal: Pleased with her beauty they coaxed her with fair words; she would not obey;
translations.idiomatic: Taken for her looks, they coaxed her; she refused;

sentences.zh: 刃脅，不屈。

translations.literal: they threatened her with blades; she would not bend.
translations.idiomatic: they threatened her with knives; she would not yield.

sentences.zh: 欲走投崖，為賊追及，支解死。

translations.literal: She tried to flee and throw herself from a cliff but bandits overtook her and dismembered her.
translations.idiomatic: She ran for a cliff to leap; rebels caught her and hacked her apart.

sentences.zh: 纏娃年十六，尤麗。

translations.literal: Chanwa was sixteen and exceptionally beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Chanwa was sixteen and famed for her beauty.

sentences.zh: 賊縶以行，纏娃唾賊面罵，不少怯，亦見殺。

translations.literal: Bandits bound her and marched her off; Chanwa spat in a bandit's face and cursed without the least fear and was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Bound and marched off, Chanwa spat in a rebel's face, cursed without fear, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 馬安娃妻趙，秦州人。

translations.literal: Zhao, the wife of Ma Anwa, was from Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, wife of Ma Anwa, was from Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 莊而有容。

translations.literal: She was dignified and comely in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: She was grave and handsome in bearing.

sentences.zh: 回亂，見執，纏賊，劙口，被數十創而死。

translations.literal: In the Muslim rebellion she was seized; she clung to the bandits, they split her mouth, and she died under several dozen cuts.
translations.idiomatic: Seized in the revolt, she clung to her captors; they slashed her mouth and hacked her to death.

sentences.zh: 安娃母田、兄妻趙皆死。

translations.literal: Anwa's mother Tian and his elder brother's wife Zhao also died.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Tian and his sister-in-law Zhao died as well.

sentences.zh: 王之綱妻李，亦秦州人。

translations.literal: Li, the wife of Wang Zhigang, was also from Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li, wife of Wang Zhigang, was also from Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 扶姑避賊，賊及之，李捍賊刃，乞代姑，姑得間走，李乃罵賊。

translations.literal: She supported her mother-in-law in flight from bandits; when bandits overtook them Li parried the bandits' blades and begged to take her mother-in-law's place; the old woman found an opening and ran; Li then cursed the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing with her mother-in-law, she blocked their blades and offered herself in the old woman's place; when her mother-in-law escaped she cursed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊剜其左目，被十餘刃而死。

translations.literal: The bandits gouged out her left eye and she died under more than ten blade cuts.
translations.idiomatic: They gouged out her left eye and stabbed her more than ten times.

sentences.zh: 穆氏女，名芝，束鹿人。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Mu clan, named Zhi, was from Shulu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, a Mu-clan daughter, was from Shulu.

sentences.zh: 幼慧。

translations.literal: She was clever from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: She had been clever since childhood.

sentences.zh: 同治七年，年十八，捻匪至，欲縶以去。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi, at eighteen, Nian bandits came and were about to bind her and take her away.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 7, aged eighteen, Nian rebels came to seize her.

sentences.zh: 女哀之，不聽，乃呼其父曰：「速去！

translations.literal: The girl pleaded piteously but they would not listen; she then called to her father, "Go quickly!
translations.idiomatic: She begged in vain, then shouted to her father, "Run!

sentences.zh: 勿相顧，兒自有以處之。

translations.literal: Do not look back—your daughter has her own way to deal with this."
translations.idiomatic: Do not look back—I know what to do."

sentences.zh: 」父行稍遠，芝厲聲詬賊，賊鞭之僕。

translations.literal: " When her father had gone a little distance Zhi cursed the bandits in a harsh voice and the bandits whipped her until she fell.
translations.idiomatic: Once her father was far enough she cursed the rebels fiercely; they beat her down.

sentences.zh: 賊曰：「汝陽死，豈拾汝耶？

translations.literal: A bandit said, "You pretend you want to die—do you think we would spare you?"
translations.idiomatic: One rebel sneered, "Playing at death—do you think we'd let you off?"

sentences.zh: 」就曳之，芝驟舉足創賊目，賊連刃刺之死。

translations.literal: " As they dragged her along Zhi suddenly kicked and wounded a bandit's eye; the bandits stabbed her repeatedly until she died.
translations.idiomatic: Dragging her off, she kicked out and gouged a rebel's eye; they stabbed her to death.

sentences.zh: 張某妻蔡，秦安人。

translations.literal: Cai, the wife of a man surnamed Zhang, was from Qin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Cai, wife of a Zhang, was from Qin'an.

sentences.zh: 同治中，回亂，蔡有色，回使執爨，不可；

translations.literal: During the Tongzhi years, in the Muslim rebellion, Cai was fair of face; Muslims made her tend the kitchen and she would not;
translations.idiomatic: In the Muslim revolt of the Tongzhi era, Muslims seized fair-faced Cai for kitchen work; she refused;

sentences.zh: 與語兼嘲謔，蔡奪他賊刀刺之，傷賊手，見殺。

translations.literal: when they spoke to her with mockery and banter Cai seized another bandit's knife and stabbed him, wounding the bandit's hand, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: when they mocked her she snatched another man's blade, wounded a hand, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 同縣程丁兒妻黃，執廚刀擊賊，不中，賊刳其腹，引腸懸樹上。

translations.literal: In the same county Huang, wife of Cheng Dinger, took a kitchen knife and struck at bandits but missed; the bandits cut open her belly and hung her entrails on a tree.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, Cheng Dinger's wife in the same county, struck at rebels with a kitchen knife, missed, and was disemboweled; they hung her guts on a tree.

sentences.zh: 張氏女，小字純秀，年十七，有色。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Zhang clan, pet name Chunxiu, was seventeen and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chunxiu, seventeen, was famed for her beauty.

sentences.zh: 為回得，堅縶之。

translations.literal: Seized by Muslims, she was bound tightly.
translations.idiomatic: Muslims seized and bound her fast.

sentences.zh: 女止哭，求弛縛，度峭岩，聳身自擲岩下死。

translations.literal: The girl stopped weeping and asked that her bonds be loosened; judging a steep cliff she flung herself from the rock and died.
translations.idiomatic: She stopped crying, asked to be unbound, then hurled herself from a cliff.

sentences.zh: 趙貴賜妻任，甘肅安化人。

translations.literal: Ren, the wife of Zhao Guici, was from Anhua in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Ren, wife of Zhao Guici, was from Anhua in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 同治間，回亂，貴賜為團勇，戰死。

translations.literal: During the Tongzhi years, in the Muslim rebellion, Guici was a militiaman and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tongzhi Muslim revolt Guici served in the local militia and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 回入其家，任執廚刀伏戶側，回先入者，出不意，斫之，踣。

translations.literal: Muslims entered their house; Ren took a kitchen knife and lay in wait beside the door; when a Muslim entered first she struck him unexpectedly and he fell.
translations.idiomatic: Muslims entered; Ren hid with a kitchen knife and cut down the first man through the door.

sentences.zh: 餘賊挺矛入，任反刃自殺。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits thrust spears in; Ren turned the blade on herself and died.
translations.idiomatic: More rebels rushed in with spears; she turned the knife on herself.

sentences.zh: 楊貴升妻劉，伏羌人。

translations.literal: Liu, the wife of Yang Guisheng, was from Fuqiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, wife of Yang Guisheng, was from Fuqiang.

sentences.zh: 回執其姑，將捶楚，劉請代，不聽，取廚刀殲一賊，因自殺。

translations.literal: Muslims seized her mother-in-law and were about to beat her; Liu asked to take her place but they would not listen; she took a kitchen knife and killed one bandit, then killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: Muslims seized her mother-in-law to beat her; Liu offered herself in exchange, then killed a rebel with a kitchen knife and took her own life.

sentences.zh: 多寶聘妻，宗室氏，多寶，赫舍里氏，失其所隸旗；

translations.literal: The betrothed wife of Duobao—Duobao was of the Heseri clan and the banner he belonged to is not recorded;
translations.idiomatic: Duobao's betrothed: Duobao was Heseri, his banner unrecorded;

sentences.zh: 宗室氏，正藍旗人，大學士靈桂兄女。

translations.literal: the clanswoman was of the imperial lineage, from the Plain Blue Banner, daughter of the elder brother of Grand Secretary Linggui.
translations.idiomatic: his bride was imperial lineage, Plain Blue Banner, daughter of Grand Secretary Linggui's brother.

sentences.zh: 未行，多寶卒，易衰絰，赴吊，立從子英爚為後。

translations.literal: Before the marriage was completed Duobao died; she changed into mourning garments, went to mourn him, and established his collateral nephew Yingyao as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Duobao died before the wedding; she donned mourning, attended his rites, and set up his nephew Yingyao as heir.

sentences.zh: 靈桂以聞，穆宗書「未吉完貞」四字以賜。

translations.literal: Linggui reported it to the throne and the Muzong Emperor wrote four characters, "Chastity preserved though the wedding was uncompleted," and bestowed them as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Linggui memorialized the throne; Emperor Muzong bestowed the four characters "Chastity preserved though unwed."

sentences.zh: 英爚亦早卒，妻鄂卓爾氏，蒙古正白旗人，大學士榮慶女弟。

translations.literal: Yingyao also died early; his wife was of the Ezhuo'er clan, from the Mongol Plain White Banner, younger sister of Grand Secretary Rongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyao too died young; his wife was Ezhuo'er, Mongol Plain White Banner, Rongqing's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 婚甫踰月，姑、婦食貧守節。

translations.literal: The marriage had barely passed a month; mother-in-law and daughter-in-law lived in poverty keeping chastity.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month wed, mother-in-law and daughter-in-law lived poor and chaste.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十六年，義和拳為亂，各國合軍入京師，城破，多寶弟和寶妻，率傭婦入井；

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu the Boxers made rebellion; the armies of various nations together entered the capital; the city fell; the wife of Duobao's younger brother Hebao, leading servant women, entered a well;
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 26 the Boxers rose; allied armies took Beijing; Hebao's wife led servants into a well;

sentences.zh: 多寶妻起，引藥飲其婦，視既絕，乃自飲，同殉。

translations.literal: Duobao's wife rose, drew out medicine and gave it to her sister-in-law; when she saw she was dead she drank herself and died together as martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: Duobao's widow fed poison to her sister-in-law, waited until she was gone, then drank and died with her.

sentences.zh: 公額布妻，西安駐防，失其所隸旗。

translations.literal: The wife of Gong'eboo was stationed at garrison duty in Xi'an; the banner she belonged to is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Gong'eboo's wife, Xi'an garrison, banner unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 善事姑，三十而寡，教二子奎亮、奎喜，有禮法。

translations.literal: She served her mother-in-law well; widowed at thirty, she taught her two sons Kuiliang and Kuixi with propriety and ritual decorum.
translations.idiomatic: She cared for her mother-in-law, was widowed at thirty, and raised Kuiliang and Kuixi with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年九月，亂作，戒二子曰：「此我完節時，汝曹當努力報朝廷，毋念我！

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Xuantong turmoil broke out; she admonished her two sons, saying, "This is my time to complete my integrity; you must strive to repay the court and do not think of me!"
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Xuantong 3 she told her sons, "This is my hour to die with honor—serve the dynasty and forget me!"

sentences.zh: 」城破，率二子婦及孫定炎、成惠、孫女三入井死。

translations.literal: " When the city fell she led her two daughters-in-law and grandsons Dingyan, Chenghui, and three granddaughters into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell she led her daughters-in-law and grandsons Dingyan and Chenghui and three granddaughters into a well.

sentences.zh: 清中葉後，八旗多從漢姓，公額布妻姓關桑氏，奎亮妻關鄂氏，奎喜妻關白氏。

translations.literal: After the mid-Qing many Banner families took Han surnames; Gong'eboo's wife was surnamed Guansang, Kuiliang's wife Guane, and Kuixi's wife Guanbai.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Qing Banner families often took Han names: she was Guansang; Kuiliang's wife was Guane; Kuixi's was Guanbai.

sentences.zh: 音德布女雪雁，西安駐防，正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Xueyan, daughter of Yindebu, was stationed at garrison duty in Xi'an, Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan, daughter of Yindebu, Xi'an garrison, Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 幼慧，粗解文字。

translations.literal: Clever from childhood, she had a rough knowledge of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Bright as a child, she knew some writing.

sentences.zh: 亂作，從家人出避。

translations.literal: When turmoil broke out she fled with her family.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began she fled with kin.

sentences.zh: 行遇兵，有誘之者，雪雁引刀斷其指，血沾衣，誘者驚卻。

translations.literal: On the road they met soldiers; when one tried to entice her Xueyan drew a knife and severed his finger; blood stained her clothes and the tempter fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers accosted her; she cut off a molester's finger and bloodied her clothes until he fled.

sentences.zh: 又遇兵，強脅之，女大詬曰：「吾頭可斷，志不可奪！

translations.literal: She met soldiers again who tried to seize her by force; the girl cursed loudly, "My head may be cut off but my resolve cannot be taken!"
translations.idiomatic: More soldiers seized her; she cried, "You may take my head but not my will!"

sentences.zh: 」兵群起抶之，無完膚，女罵不絕，刃洞胸死之。

translations.literal: " The soldiers together rose and beat her until no patch of skin was whole; the girl cursed without cease and they ran a blade through her breast until she died.
translations.idiomatic: They beat her until no skin was whole; still cursing, they ran a blade through her chest.

sentences.zh: 良奎妻，從漢姓曰石甘氏，荊州駐防，滿洲鑲黃旗人，為駐藏大臣鳳全女兄。

translations.literal: The wife of Liangkui—using the Han surname Shi, Gan—was stationed at garrison duty in Jingzhou, Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner, elder sister of the Tibet resident commissioner Feng Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Liangkui's wife, known in Han as Shi Gan, Jingzhou garrison, Bordered Yellow Banner, was elder sister to Tibet commissioner Feng Quan.

sentences.zh: 鳳全自有傳。

translations.literal: Feng Quan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 貧，躬織紉供朝夕，諸子佐軍，迎母居武昌。

translations.literal: Poor, she wove and sewed with her own hands to supply daily needs; her sons aided the army and brought their mother to live at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In poverty she wove for their bread; her sons served the army and brought her to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年八月，武昌兵起，諸子將奉母出避，力拒曰：「吾七十老婦，死何憾！

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Xuantong soldiers rose at Wuchang; her sons were about to escort their mother away but she forcefully refused, saying, "I am an old woman of seventy—what regret is there in death!"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Xuantong 3 the Wuchang mutiny broke out; her sons tried to move her, but she refused: "I am seventy—why fear death?"

sentences.zh: 」諸子哭，麾之出，遽闔戶。

translations.literal: " Her sons wept; she waved them out and hastily barred the door.
translations.idiomatic: They wept; she drove them out and barred the door.

sentences.zh: 翌日，兵大掠，與子婦二、女子一、孫及女孫三，皆死之。

translations.literal: The next day soldiers looted on a great scale; with two daughters-in-law, one daughter, a grandson, and three granddaughters, all died.
translations.idiomatic: Next day soldiers looted the city; she died with two daughters-in-law, a daughter, a grandson, and three granddaughters.

sentences.zh: 連惠妻，從漢姓曰趙那氏，京口駐防，失其所隸旗。

translations.literal: The wife of Lianhui—using the Han surname Zhao, Na—was stationed at garrison duty in Jingkou; the banner she belonged to is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Lianhui's wife, Han name Zhao Na, Jingkou garrison, banner unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 連惠咸豐間以前鋒從攻鎮江，戰死。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng years Lianhui served as vanguard in the attack on Zhenjiang and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianfeng era Lianhui led the vanguard at Zhenjiang and fell.

sentences.zh: 連惠妻以節旌。

translations.literal: Lianhui's wife received an official commendation for chastity.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended her chastity.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，年已逾八十。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong she was already more than eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: By Xuantong 3 she was past eighty.

sentences.zh: 九月兵起，出走，兵抽刃擊之，未殊，罵不絕，被數刃，乃絕。

translations.literal: In the ninth month soldiers rose; she went out to flee; soldiers drew blades and struck her; she was not yet dead and cursed without cease; after several blade cuts she expired.
translations.idiomatic: When the September rising came she fled; soldiers slashed her; still cursing, she died under many cuts.

sentences.zh: 血肉狼藉，白髮為之赤。

translations.literal: Flesh and blood lay in disorder; her white hair was turned red.
translations.idiomatic: Her flesh was torn and her white hair ran red with blood.

sentences.zh: 根瑞妻，從漢姓曰王劉氏，京口駐防，鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: The wife of Genrui—using the Han surname Wang, Liu—was stationed at garrison duty in Jingkou, a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Genrui's wife, Han name Wang Liu, Jingkou garrison, Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父德永，有文譽，客授學子。

translations.literal: Her father Deyong enjoyed a literary reputation and taught students as a guest instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Deyong was a noted scholar who tutored pupils.

sentences.zh: 根瑞妻服父訓，早寡，以節旌。

translations.literal: Genrui's wife followed her father's instruction; widowed early, she received an official commendation for chastity.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young, she heeded her father's teaching and was commended for chastity.

sentences.zh: 無子，有女已嫁，依以居。

translations.literal: She had no son; she had a daughter already married and lived depending on her.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, she lived with her married daughter.

sentences.zh: 聞兵起，語女及女夫曰：「吾年六十二，被旌，當殉變。

translations.literal: Hearing that soldiers had risen, she said to her daughter and son-in-law, "I am sixty-two, have received an official banner, and should die with the upheaval."
translations.idiomatic: When the rising began she told daughter and son-in-law, "I am sixty-two and was officially commended—I should die with the times."

sentences.zh: 爾曹將子女村居，得田十畝，耕且食，毋更求仕。

translations.literal: You should take your children to live in a village; you can get ten mu of fields, farm and eat, and seek office no more."
translations.idiomatic: Take your children to the country, farm ten mu, and never seek office again."

sentences.zh: 」俄聞副都統載穆死官，即求死，輒救免；

translations.literal: " Soon she heard that Vice Governor-General Zai Mu had died in office; she immediately sought death but was repeatedly saved;
translations.idiomatic: Soon she heard Vice Governor-General Zai Mu had died in office; she tried to kill herself but was saved;

sentences.zh: 號泣不食，女及女夫跪進食，終不食，七日乃絕。

translations.literal: she wailed and refused food; her daughter and son-in-law knelt offering food but she never ate, and after seven days she expired.
translations.idiomatic: she wailed and fasted; kin begged her to eat; after seven days she died.

sentences.zh: 松文母吳，松文，荊州駐防，鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Wu, the mother of Songwen—Songwen was stationed at garrison duty in Jingzhou, Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, mother of Songwen: Jingzhou garrison, Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 同治初，徙江寧，從漢姓為馮氏。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi years they moved to Jiangning and took the Han surname Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi they moved to Jiangning and adopted the Han surname Feng.

sentences.zh: 吳，荊州士人女也。

translations.literal: Wu was the daughter of a Jingzhou scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was a Jingzhou scholar's daughter.

sentences.zh: 事姑孝，早寡，無子，松文​​，其族子也，立為後。

translations.literal: She served her mother-in-law with filial piety, was widowed early and had no son; Songwen was a clansman and was established as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and widowed without sons, she adopted clansman Songwen as heir.

sentences.zh: 松文子富倫渾，才而早卒，松文哭子慟，亦卒。

translations.literal: Songwen's son Fulunhun was talented and died early; Songwen grieved for his son and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Songwen's gifted son Fulunhun died young; Songwen mourned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 松文妻康，富倫渾妻石，仍世守節。

translations.literal: Songwen's wife Kang and Fulunhun's wife Shi both kept chastity through successive generations.
translations.idiomatic: Wives Kang and Shi kept chastity across generations.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，兵起，江寧駐防軍潰，松文母年九十三矣，慟哭，以仍世守節，義不辱，首觸牆死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong soldiers rose; the Jiangning garrison army collapsed; Songwen's mother was ninety-three; she wailed bitterly; because the family had kept chastity for generations, in righteousness she would not suffer disgrace and dashed her head against the wall and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 the garrison broke; aged ninety-three, Songwen's mother wailed, then killed herself against the wall rather than be shamed.

sentences.zh: 康與婦石將諸孫自沉於水。

translations.literal: Kang and her daughter-in-law Shi led the grandchildren to drown themselves in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Kang and Shi drowned themselves in the water with the grandchildren.

sentences.zh: 康死，石與子、女遇救免，康與石不詳其族系。

translations.literal: Kang died; Shi, with her son and daughter, was rescued and spared; the clan affiliations of Kang and Shi are not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Kang died; Shi and her children were saved; their lineages are unclear.

sentences.zh: 姚叶敏妻耿，襄城人。

translations.literal: Geng, the wife of Yao Yemin, was from Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Geng, wife of Yao Yemin, was from Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 葉敏早卒，事舅姑盡禮。

translations.literal: Yemin died early; she served her parents-in-law with full ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed early, she served her in-laws with full propriety.

sentences.zh: 立兄子為後。

translations.literal: She established her husband's brother's son as heir.
translations.idiomatic: She adopted her husband's brother's son as heir.

sentences.zh: 武漢兵起，耿方病，襄城土豪為暴，掠婦子為質，耿懼辱，飲藥死。

translations.literal: When soldiers rose at Wuhan Geng was ill; a local bully in Xiangcheng ran riot, seized women and children as hostages; fearing disgrace Geng took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuhan rising she was ill; a Xiangcheng bully seized hostages; fearing shame she poisoned herself.

sentences.zh: 陳某妻殷，秀水人。

translations.literal: Yin, the wife of a man surnamed Chen, was from Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, wife of a Chen, was from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，殷從夫在郴州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong Yin followed her husband at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 Yin was with her husband at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，長沙兵起，湘南諸府州應之，郴屬縣宜章、永興皆變，殷告夫誓相守以死。

translations.literal: In the ninth month soldiers rose at Changsha and the prefectures and departments of southern Hunan responded; Yizhang and Yongxing, counties under Chen, also rebelled; Yin told her husband they had sworn to keep faith unto death together.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Changsha rose and southern Hunan followed; Yin swore to die with her husband.

sentences.zh: 夫趣殷將子女徙湘鄉，依戚屬避兵，殷不可；

translations.literal: Her husband urged Yin to move the children to Xiangxiang and rely on kin to flee the fighting; Yin would not;
translations.idiomatic: He urged her to flee with the children to Xiangxiang; she refused;

sentences.zh: 強之，乃行。

translations.literal: when he forced her she finally went.
translations.idiomatic: forced, she at last departed.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，部署瑣雜事井井，入舟，抑鬱，語子女：「若曹免矣，若父奈何？

translations.literal: On the verge of leaving she arranged trifling matters in perfect order, boarded the boat, grew depressed, and said to her children, "You are spared—but what of your father?
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving she set every detail in order, then told her children on the boat, "You are safe—what of your father?

sentences.zh: 」湘鄉距郴千餘裡，俄傳郴破，殷憂悸不食，面深墨，戚屬相慰藉，陽為酬答。

translations.literal: " Xiangxiang was more than a thousand li from Chen; soon word came that Chen had fallen; Yin grew anxious and fearful and would not eat; her face turned deep black; kin comforted her and she answered them as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li from Chen, news came the city had fallen; she stopped eating, her face went black, yet she pretended calm for kin.

sentences.zh: 十月壬子夕，戚屬同居者，聞啟戶聲，旋聞其季女驚呼阿母起，燭之，就堂後門衡自罄死矣。

translations.literal: On the evening of the renzi day of the tenth month, kin living together heard the sound of a door opening; then they heard her youngest daughter cry out for her mother to rise; when they lit a lamp they found she had hanged herself on the crossbeam behind the rear hall door.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi evening in the tenth month kin heard a door, then a daughter's cry; they found Yin hanged behind the hall.

sentences.zh: 黃晞妻周，江陰人。

translations.literal: Zhou, the wife of Huang Xi, was from Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou, wife of Huang Xi, was from Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 晞父毓祺，明諸生，能文，明亡，發狂亡命。

translations.literal: Xi's father Yuqi was a Ming licentiate, able in letters; when the Ming fell he went mad and fled as a fugitive.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's father Yuqi, a Ming scholar, went mad and fled when the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 有司得晞系諸獄，週聞自經，婢救之，不死；

translations.literal: The authorities seized Xi and imprisoned him; when Zhou heard she hanged herself; a maid saved her and she did not die;
translations.idiomatic: Xi was jailed; Zhou tried to hang herself; a maid saved her;

sentences.zh: 乃日餽獄饘粥，夏不施帷，恣蚊囓，曰：「我遙與獄中共辛苦也！

translations.literal: she then daily sent gruel to the prison; in summer she hung no curtains and let mosquitoes bite, saying, "I share his hardship in the prison from afar!"
translations.idiomatic: She sent him prison gruel daily, went without mosquito nets in summer, and said she shared his torment from afar.

sentences.zh: 」晞入獄十閱月，事小解，得出。

translations.literal: " Xi had been in prison ten months when the matter eased somewhat and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: After ten months in prison he was released.

sentences.zh: 居無何，怨家告毓祺所在，死江寧按察使獄中。

translations.literal: Not long after they had lived together, an enemy informed on where Yuqi was hiding; he died in the Jiangning provincial judge's prison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an enemy exposed Yuqi; he died in the Jiangning provincial prison.

sentences.zh: 有司籍其家，捕晞兄弟，兼收週，週夜投水，不死；

translations.literal: The authorities registered their household property, seized Xi's brothers, and also took Zhou; Zhou threw herself into the water at night but did not die;
translations.idiomatic: Officials seized the family; Zhou drowned herself but survived;

sentences.zh: 茹金屑，亦不死；

translations.literal: she ate gold filings and also did not die;
translations.idiomatic: she ate gold dust and still lived;

sentences.zh: 乃詣府，藏刃刺喉，血衝溢僕地。

translations.literal: she then went to the prefectural yamen, hid a blade, and stabbed her throat; blood gushed forth and she fell.
translations.idiomatic: she went to the prefecture, stabbed her throat, and collapsed in blood.

sentences.zh: 知府驚其烈，問晞有女兄為女僧，命舁置所居庵，上按察使請釋週，按察使不許，下縣令再收週。

translations.literal: The prefect was startled by her fierceness; learning that Xi had an elder sister who had become a Buddhist nun, he ordered Zhou carried to the nunnery where she lived and memorialized the provincial judge to release Zhou; the judge would not permit it and ordered the county magistrate to seize Zhou again.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect sent her to a nunnery and asked the judge to release her; the judge refused and ordered her rearrested.

sentences.zh: 週創漸合，乃自歸，語縣役曰：「我不累若輩，第徐之，俟我死，持片紙去公家，事易了也。

translations.literal: Zhou's wound gradually closed; she then returned of her own accord and told the county runners, "I will not burden you—just take your time; wait until I am dead, take a slip of paper to the authorities, and the matter will be easily settled."
translations.idiomatic: When her wound healed she returned and told the runners to wait until she died, then take a note to the yamen.

sentences.zh: 」手檢晞單衣一，付老僕曰：「主人行久，無衷衣備澣濯，汝以此寄之！

translations.literal: " With her hand she sorted out one of Xi's unlined garments and gave it to an old servant, saying, "The master has been away long and has no undergarments ready for washing—you may send this to him!"
translations.idiomatic: She gave an old servant one of Xi's undergarments for him in prison.

sentences.zh: 」徐入室，闔戶自經乃死。

translations.literal: " She slowly entered the room, closed the door, hanged herself, and died.
translations.idiomatic: She went inside, barred the door, and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 時順治七年十月丁巳，年二十八。

translations.literal: It was the dingsi day of the tenth month of the seventh year of Shunzhi; she was twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the tenth month of Shunzhi 7 she was twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 晞尚係按察使獄，聞周死，為文述其事，略言：「古成仁取義之士，所以趨死之道不一，由其一，皆可得死。

translations.literal: Xi was still bound in the provincial judge's prison; hearing of Zhou's death he wrote an essay recounting the affair, saying in brief, "Ancient men who fulfilled humanity and righteousness had many roads to death; by any one of them all could obtain death."
translations.idiomatic: Still imprisoned, Xi wrote that ancient martyrs had many paths to death, any one sufficient.

sentences.zh: 婦獨多途遍歷，靡苦不嚐，而顛跌頓撼，卒死於家。

translations.literal: A wife alone travels many roads, tastes every bitterness, and after stumbling and being thrown about finally dies at home.
translations.idiomatic: A wife alone tries every path of suffering and dies at last in her own house.

sentences.zh: 一以顯百折不回之苦節，一以遂正命內寢之初心，天不可謂無意云。

translations.literal: In one way she displays a will unbent through a hundred setbacks; in another she fulfills the original resolve of a proper death in the inner quarters—Heaven cannot be said to be without purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Thus she showed unbroken resolve and died the death she first intended—Heaven had its design.

sentences.zh: 」晞輸八旗為官奴，鄉人贖出之，得歸，為童子師，至七十餘乃卒。

translations.literal: " Xi was consigned to the Eight Banners as a government slave; countrymen ransomed him and he returned, became a village schoolteacher, and lived to more than seventy before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xi became a banner slave; kin ransomed him; he taught school until past seventy.

sentences.zh: 鄒延玠妻吳，武進人。

translations.literal: Wu, the wife of Zou Yanjue, was from Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, wife of Zou Yanjue, was from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 延玠，明諸生，順治八年，逮系江寧獄。

translations.literal: Yanjue was a Ming licentiate; in the eighth year of Shunzhi he was seized and imprisoned at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjue, a Ming licentiate, was jailed at Jiangning in Shunzhi 8.

sentences.zh: 十年，見法。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10 he was executed.

sentences.zh: 吳自經，救不死。

translations.literal: Wu hanged herself but was saved and did not die.
translations.idiomatic: She tried to hang herself but survived.

sentences.zh: 十二年，延玠喪還葬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Yanjue's coffin was returned for burial.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 12 his body came home for burial.

sentences.zh: 十三年，有司复議收延玠家北徙。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the authorities again deliberated confiscating Yanjue's family and moving them north.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 officials again planned to exile the family north.

sentences.zh: 吳乃迎母至，夜將半，起，請母所曰：「兒今固必死，安能俯首求旦夕活，作長安累囚婦耶？

translations.literal: Wu then brought her mother there; near midnight she rose and, going to her mother's place, said, "Your daughter must die today—how can I bow my head to beg a few days' life and become a convict's wife in Chang'an?"
translations.idiomatic: Near midnight she told her mother, "I must die today—I will not live as a convict's wife in Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 原母稍忍，成兒死。

translations.literal: I beg Mother to bear it a little and let your daughter die.
translations.idiomatic: Bear it a little and let me die.

sentences.zh: 」母泣不能言。

translations.literal: " Her mother wept and could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother wept speechless.

sentences.zh: 吳更衣拜佛，復向母曰：「兒欲為母拜，恐傷母心，兒不敢。

translations.literal: Wu changed clothes and bowed before the Buddha, then said again to her mother, "Your daughter wishes to bow to Mother but fears it would wound Mother's heart—your daughter dare not."
translations.idiomatic: She dressed, bowed to Buddha, and said she dared not bow to her mother lest it break her heart.

sentences.zh: 母老矣，勿以兒故過哀！

translations.literal: Mother is old—do not grieve too deeply on your daughter's account!
translations.idiomatic: Mother is old—do not grieve too much for me!

sentences.zh: 」因出一扇，曰：「此夫子南京寄我者。

translations.literal: " She then brought out a fan and said, "This is what my husband sent me from Nanjing."
translations.idiomatic: She brought out a fan: "My husband sent this from Nanjing."

sentences.zh: 」出一囊，曰：「有醫方，夫子所手校。

translations.literal: " She brought out a pouch and said, "Inside are medical formulas my husband collated by hand."
translations.idiomatic: From a pouch: "His hand-corrected medical formulas."

sentences.zh: 有書，夫子生平所習。

translations.literal: There are books he studied throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: His lifelong books are here too.

sentences.zh: 有發，夫子獄中所留也，仍乞以殉。

translations.literal: There is hair he left in prison—I still beg that these be buried with him."
translations.idiomatic: And hair he left in prison—bury these with him."

sentences.zh: 」复呼婢戒毋號。

translations.literal: " She again called the maid and admonished her not to cry out.
translations.idiomatic: She told the maid to stay silent.

sentences.zh: 乃自燃燭，持囊及扇還入室。

translations.literal: She then lit a candle herself and, holding the pouch and fan, returned to her room.
translations.idiomatic: She lit a candle and took the pouch and fan inside.

sentences.zh: 時雞甫鳴，母及婢傍徨哭，不敢出聲。

translations.literal: The cock had just crowed; her mother and the maid paced about weeping but dared not make a sound.
translations.idiomatic: At cockcrow mother and maid wept softly outside.

sentences.zh: 少頃，視吳，自經已絕。

translations.literal: After a little while they looked at Wu—she had hanged herself and was dead.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they found her hanged dead.

sentences.zh: 死前一日，苦熱，吳祝曰：「安所得甘雨乎？

translations.literal: The day before her death it was bitterly hot; Wu prayed, "Where can sweet rain be found?"
translations.idiomatic: The day before she died in heat she prayed for rain.

sentences.zh: 」遂雨竟日，人謂「節婦雨」。

translations.literal: " Rain then fell all day; people called it "the chaste widow's rain."
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell all day; people called it the Chaste Widow's Rain.

sentences.zh: 陳生輝妻侯，單縣人。

translations.literal: Hou, the wife of Chen Shenghui, was from Shan County.
translations.idiomatic: Hou, wife of Chen Shenghui, was from Shan County.

sentences.zh: 順治初，盜掠生輝使牧馬。

translations.literal: In the early Shunzhi years bandits seized Shenghui and made him tend horses.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi bandits seized him to tend horses.

sentences.zh: 縣北郭秦氏有馬，為盜掠，生輝乘以歸。

translations.literal: North of the county seat the Qin family had a horse that bandits seized; Shenghui rode it home.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits stole the Qin family's horse north of town; Shenghui rode it home.

sentences.zh: 秦氏見馬訟生輝，生輝坐通寇死。

translations.literal: The Qin family saw the horse and sued Shenghui; Shenghui was convicted of communicating with bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Qins sued; he was convicted of colluding with bandits and executed.

sentences.zh: 侯事姑，喪葬畢，並葬生輝，設祭自剄。

translations.literal: Hou served her mother-in-law; when the funeral rites were complete she buried Shenghui together with him, set out offerings, and cut her own throat.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites she buried him, made offerings, and cut her throat.

sentences.zh: 田一朋妻劉，通江人。

translations.literal: Liu, the wife of Tian Yipeng, was from Tongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, wife of Tian Yipeng, was from Tongjiang.

sentences.zh: 國初，一朋不從薙發令，坐當死，吏並縶劉去。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty Yipeng would not obey the tonsure order and was sentenced to death; the clerk also seized Liu and took her away.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding Yipeng refused the tonsure edict and was condemned; Liu was seized with him.

sentences.zh: 劉挾毒自隨，聞一朋將就刑，先服毒死。

translations.literal: Liu carried poison with her; hearing Yipeng was about to be executed she took the poison first and died.
translations.idiomatic: She carried poison and took it before he was executed.

sentences.zh: 蔣世珍妻劉，揚州人，失其縣。

translations.literal: Liu, the wife of Jiang Shizhen, was from Yangzhou; the county is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, wife of Jiang Shizhen, was from Yangzhou; her county is lost.

sentences.zh: 世珍，順治中為廣東連平知州，有惠於民。

translations.literal: Shizhen, in the Shunzhi years, was magistrate of Lianping in Guangdong and showed kindness to the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi he was magistrate of Lianping in Guangdong and was kind to the people.

sentences.zh: 嶺海初定，土寇數發，諜報旁縣賊數千人鄉連平，行至。

translations.literal: When the Lingnan coast was first pacified local bandits rose repeatedly; spies reported that several thousand bandits from a neighboring county were heading toward Lianping and had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits repeatedly rose; spies said thousands from a neighboring county were marching on Lianping.

sentences.zh: 世珍曰：「賊至，驚吾民，吾且往，權順逆強弱而為之所。

translations.literal: Shizhen said, "When bandits come they will alarm our people; I shall go and, weighing submission or resistance, strong or weak, do what is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I will go alone and judge whether to coax or fight them."

sentences.zh: 」單騎入賊中，諭其渠降，其渠為引退。

translations.literal: " He entered the bandit host alone on horseback, persuaded their chief to submit, and the chief withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He rode in alone, persuaded their chief to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 世珍宿賊營，翌旦乃還。

translations.literal: Shizhen lodged in the bandit camp and returned only the next morning.
translations.idiomatic: He spent the night in their camp and returned next day.

sentences.zh: 守備吳章者，故與世珍有隙，誣世珍通寇，告總兵黃應傑，應傑啟平南王尚可喜，捕世珍赴惠州獄，劉系置守備廨旁舍。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Wu Zhang had an old grudge against Shizhen; he slandered Shizhen as communicating with bandits, reported to Regional Commander Huang Yingjie; Yingjie informed Prince Pingnan Shang Kexi; Shizhen was seized and sent to prison at Huizhou; Liu was detained in a side building beside the commander's yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wu Zhang slandered him to Huang Yingjie and Prince Pingnan; Shizhen was jailed at Huizhou; Liu was held near Wu's yamen.

sentences.zh: 章將無禮於劉，劉怒叱去。

translations.literal: Zhang was about to behave improperly toward Liu; Liu rebuked him angrily and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhang meant to violate her; she drove him off with a shout.

sentences.zh: 又遣婢說劉，劉曰：「死不可緩矣！

translations.literal: He again sent a maid to persuade Liu; Liu said, "Death cannot be delayed!"
translations.idiomatic: He sent a maid; she said, "Death cannot wait!"

sentences.zh: 」遂縊而死。

translations.literal: " She then hanged herself and died.
translations.idiomatic: She hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 世珍入獄病，亦死。

translations.literal: Shizhen fell ill in prison and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen sickened in prison and died.

sentences.zh: 連平民葬劉州南烏石坳，為之碣，曰「正烈劉宜人之墓」。

translations.literal: The people of Lianping buried Liu south of the prefecture at Wushi'ao and set up a stele reading, "Tomb of the Upright and Fierce Lady Liu."
translations.idiomatic: Lianping buried her at Wushi'ao with a stele: "Tomb of the Upright and Fierce Lady Liu."
