sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十三年，知州陳鵬來上其事，乃得旌。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiaqing Magistrate Chen Penglai reported the affair to the throne and she then received an official commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 23 Magistrate Chen Penglai memorialized and she was officially commended.

sentences.zh: 王有章妻羅，益陽人。

translations.literal: Luo, the wife of Wang Youzhang, was from Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo, wife of Wang Youzhang, was from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 順治七年，盜殺有章父賡及家人男婦二十餘輩。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shunzhi bandits killed Youzhang's father Geng and more than twenty men and women of the household.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 7 bandits killed his father Geng and over twenty kin.

sentences.zh: 越三年，又殺有章，惟餘羅及有章妹頭貞，皆斷發剺面，號於有司。

translations.literal: Three years later they killed Youzhang as well; only Luo and Youzhang's sister Touzhen remained; both cut their hair and scarred their faces and cried out to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later they killed Youzhang; only Luo and sister Touzhen remained, hair cut and faces scarred, petitioning officials.

sentences.zh: 曆八年，乃論殺盜渠。

translations.literal: After eight years the bandit chiefs were finally sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years the bandit leaders were executed.

sentences.zh: 羅謂頭貞曰：「我當報汝兄地下！

translations.literal: Luo said to Touzhen, "I shall repay your brother in the world below!"
translations.idiomatic: Luo told Touzhen, "I will answer to your brother underground!"

sentences.zh: 」因不食死。

translations.literal: " She then starved herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: She starved herself to death.

sentences.zh: 頭貞初字曹氏子，曹氏子以其毀容也，遂罷婚。

translations.literal: Touzhen had first been betrothed to a son of the Cao clan; the Cao son, because her appearance was ruined, then broke off the engagement.
translations.idiomatic: Touzhen had been betrothed to a Cao; he broke the engagement when her face was ruined.

sentences.zh: 頭貞徙長沙，仇家有子赴​​試，誘至家，殪之。

translations.literal: Touzhen moved to Changsha; a son of an enemy family went to take the examinations; she lured him to her house and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In Changsha she lured an enemy's son who came for the exams and killed him.

sentences.zh: 樓文貴妻盧，東陽人。

translations.literal: Lu, the wife of Lou Wengui, was from Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, wife of Lou Wengui, was from Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 文貴，農也，有鵝啄其麥，文貴驅鵝，傷鄰兒。

translations.literal: Wengui was a farmer; a goose pecked his wheat; Wengui drove off the goose and injured a neighbor's child.
translations.idiomatic: Farmer Wengui's goose damaged a neighbor's child while he chased it from his wheat.

sentences.zh: 鄰兒呼，遂毆之，投水死。

translations.literal: The neighbor's child cried out; he then beat the child, who fell into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: The child cried; he beat him; the boy drowned.

sentences.zh: 裡豪喝文貴，使鬻妻以為解。

translations.literal: A local bully threatened Wengui and made him sell his wife to settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: A bully forced Wengui to sell his wife to settle the case.

sentences.zh: 盧曰：「吾不忍生離！

translations.literal: Lu said, "I cannot bear to part while living!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu said, "I cannot bear to part in life!"

sentences.zh: 」文貴怵得罪，因求死，盧曰：「吾與汝同死！

translations.literal: " Wengui, fearing punishment, then sought death; Lu said, "I die with you!"
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the law, he sought death; Lu said, "We die together!"

sentences.zh: 」遂入林偕縊。

translations.literal: " They then entered the woods and hanged themselves together.
translations.idiomatic: They hanged themselves together in the woods.

sentences.zh: 沙木哈妻哈里克，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Harike, the wife of Shamha, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Harike, wife of Shamha, Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 沙木哈，兵也，為弟三太所擊，垂斃，沙木哈妻誓身殉。

translations.literal: Shamha was a soldier; he was struck by his younger brother Santai and was near death; Shamha's wife vowed to die with her body.
translations.idiomatic: Soldier Shamha was beaten near death by his brother Santai; his wife vowed to die with him.

sentences.zh: 沙木哈言曰：「我止一弟，我死，弟抵罪。

translations.literal: Shamha said, "I have only one younger brother; if I die my brother will pay with his life."
translations.idiomatic: Shamha said, "I have only one brother—if I die he pays with his life."

sentences.zh: 守先墓，撫諸孤，復何人？

translations.literal: Guard the ancestral graves, raise the orphans—who else is there?
translations.idiomatic: Guard our graves and raise the orphans—who else remains?

sentences.zh: 汝當言於官，曲貰三太死。

translations.literal: You should speak to the authorities and beg them to spare Santai's life."
translations.idiomatic: Tell the authorities to spare Santai."

sentences.zh: 」沙木哈遂死。

translations.literal: Shamha then died.
translations.idiomatic: Shamha died.

sentences.zh: 沙木哈妻叩閽，述沙木哈遺言，乞貰三太，聖祖命許之。

translations.literal: Shamha's wife knocked at the palace gate, recounted Shamha's last words, and begged pardon for Santai; the Kangxi Emperor ordered it granted.
translations.idiomatic: His wife petitioned the throne with his last wish; Kangxi pardoned Santai.

sentences.zh: 沙木哈妻得請，即自裁。

translations.literal: When Shamha's wife obtained the grant she immediately killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: Once pardon was granted she killed herself.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年正月壬午，禮部疏請旌表，聖祖令立石塚上，書其事始未。

translations.literal: On the renwu day of the first month of the third year of Kangxi the Ministry of Rites memorialized requesting an official commendation; the Kangxi Emperor ordered a stone set on the mound recording the affair from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kangxi 3 the Ministry of Rites sought commendation; Kangxi ordered a stone on the tomb recounting the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 鄭榮組妻徐，西安人。

translations.literal: Xu, the wife of Zheng Rongzu, was from Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, wife of Zheng Rongzu, was from Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 榮組有族叔，無狀，毆其父，赴救，為所殺。

translations.literal: Rongzu had a clansman uncle who was dissolute; he beat Rongzu's father; Rongzu ran to the rescue and was killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: A dissolute clansman uncle beat Rongzu's father; Rongzu was killed trying to save him.

sentences.zh: 其子五元、七元遇仇於途，囓其鼻。

translations.literal: His sons Wuyuan and Qiyuan met the enemy on the road and bit off his nose.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Wuyuan and Qiyuan met the killer and bit off his nose.

sentences.zh: 仇愬於縣，縣吏逮五元、七元，徐以冤白吏，吏不省，撞縣門碑死，時康熙二十七年六月事也。

translations.literal: The enemy complained to the county; the county clerk seized Wuyuan and Qiyuan; Xu stated the injustice to the clerk but the clerk paid no heed; she dashed herself against the county gate stele and died—it was the sixth month of the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The killer sued; clerks seized the sons; Xu protested, then killed herself on the county stele in the sixth month of Kangxi 27.

sentences.zh: 典史某為具槥，露置城西鐵塔。

translations.literal: A certain jail clerk prepared a coffin and set it exposed west of the city at the iron pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: A jail clerk coffined her and set her west of the iron pagoda.

sentences.zh: 越七年，知縣陳鵬年為營葬，立祠於墓側。

translations.literal: Seven years later Magistrate Chen Pengnian arranged burial and built a shrine beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later Magistrate Chen Pengnian buried her and built a shrine.

sentences.zh: 張翼妻戴，名禮，烏程人。

translations.literal: Dai, the wife of Zhang Yi, named Li, was from Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Li, wife of Zhang Yi, was from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 翼父韜，嘗知休寧縣，託翼於其友王毅，毅以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Yi's father Tao had once been magistrate of Xiuning County; he entrusted Yi to his friend Wang Yi, and Wang Yi gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's father Tao, once Xiuning magistrate, entrusted him to Wang Yi, who married him to his daughter.

sentences.zh: 韜卒，毅女亦死，繼室於戴。

translations.literal: When Tao died Wang Yi's daughter also died; he remarried into the Dai family.
translations.idiomatic: After Tao died Wang's daughter died too; Yi remarried a Dai.

sentences.zh: 毅子覬翼產，康熙六十年五月，誘至其家，迫作券，毆之垂斃，擠墮水。

translations.literal: Wang Yi's son coveted Yi's property; in the fifth month of the sixtieth year of Kangxi he lured him to his house, forced him to write a bond, beat him nearly to death, and pushed him into the water.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kangxi 60 Wang's son lured Yi, forced a bond, beat him, and pushed him into the water.

sentences.zh: 舁歸，不能語，瞠視戴。

translations.literal: When they carried him home he could not speak and stared wide-eyed at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Carried home, he could not speak and stared at Dai.

sentences.zh: 戴泣曰：「我一弱女子，不能為君復仇，當以死從君。

translations.literal: Dai wept and said, "I am but a weak woman and cannot avenge my lord for you—I shall follow you in death."
translations.idiomatic: Dai wept, "I cannot avenge you—I will die with you."

sentences.zh: 」齧指以誓。

translations.literal: She bit her finger to swear.
translations.idiomatic: She bit her finger in oath.

sentences.zh: 越七日，翼死；

translations.literal: After seven days Yi died;
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later Yi died;

sentences.zh: 又十七日，戴自經，衣帶間得絕命詩三章。

translations.literal: seventeen days later Dai hanged herself; among her garments were found three death poems.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen days later Dai hanged herself, leaving three death poems.

sentences.zh: 詹允迪妻吳，東陽人。

translations.literal: Wu, the wife of Zhan Yundi, was from Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, wife of Zhan Yundi, was from Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 允迪不嗛於族人，為所中，坐危法下獄，吳期與俱死。

translations.literal: Yundi was at odds with his clansmen; they framed him and he fell under a severe statute and was imprisoned; Wu pledged to die with him.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen framed Yundi; imprisoned under a harsh statute, Wu vowed to die with him.

sentences.zh: 至其日，盡出金珠畀所識貧乏者，散諸婢僕，詣獄與允迪訣，瞠視不語者久之，歸自剄。

translations.literal: When the day came she gave out all her gold and jewels to poor acquaintances she knew, distributed gifts among maids and servants, went to the prison to bid Yundi farewell, stared without speaking for a long while, returned home, and cut her throat.
translations.idiomatic: On the day she gave her jewels to the poor, dismissed servants, bade him farewell in prison, then cut her throat at home.

sentences.zh: 蔡以位妻孫，侯官人。

translations.literal: Sun, the wife of Cai Yiwei, was from Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, wife of Cai Yiwei, was from Houguan.

sentences.zh: 以位佐鹺商與私販者鬥而死，孫迎喪河干，自擲入水，以救免。

translations.literal: Yiwei died fighting salt merchants who dealt with private traders; Sun met the coffin at the riverbank and threw herself into the water but was saved.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwei died fighting salt smugglers; Sun threw herself into the river at his coffin but was saved.

sentences.zh: 其娣，即其姊也，責以撫孤，乃不復言死。

translations.literal: Her younger sister-in-law—that is, her elder sister—rebuked her to raise the orphans, and she spoke of death no more.
translations.idiomatic: Her sister urged her to raise the orphans, and she ceased speaking of death.

sentences.zh: 官捕得私販者，法當檢驗，讞乃定，孫曰：「是重僇吾夫也！

translations.literal: When the authorities captured the private trader the law required an inquest before the case could be settled; Sun said, "That would double the punishment on my husband!"
translations.idiomatic: When the smuggler was caught the law required an inquest; Sun cried that would shame her husband twice.

sentences.zh: 」乃大戚。

translations.literal: She then grieved greatly.
translations.idiomatic: She grieved bitterly.

sentences.zh: 官悲其意，為杖殺私販者。

translations.literal: The magistrate pitied her intent and had the private trader beaten to death with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate, moved, had the smuggler beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 喪再期，從容語其姊曰：「兒稍長，履可取諸市，不煩手自製矣。

translations.literal: When the mourning period had passed twice she said calmly to her sister, "The boy is somewhat grown; shoes can be bought in the market and need not trouble your hand to make them."
translations.idiomatic: After two mourning cycles she told her sister the boy could buy shoes in the market now.

sentences.zh: 兒昔病瘍，今愈矣。

translations.literal: The boy was once ill with sores but is healed now.
translations.idiomatic: His sores are healed.

sentences.zh: 不累我姊矣！

translations.literal: He no longer burdens my sister!
translations.idiomatic: I no longer burden you!

sentences.zh: 」或曰：「姑在，既祥，當更淺色履。

translations.literal: Someone said, "Your mother-in-law is still alive; after the auspicious rites you should wear lighter-colored shoes."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said after the rites she should wear lighter mourning shoes.

sentences.zh: 」孫曰：「然，姑徐之！

translations.literal: Sun said, "So it is—Mother-in-law, take your time!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun said, "Yes—take your time, Mother-in-law!"

sentences.zh: 」至大祥，奠竟，入戶自經死。

translations.literal: At the great auspicious rites, when the offering was finished, she entered her room and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the great mourning she hanged herself in her room.

sentences.zh: 楊春芳妻王，銅梁人。

translations.literal: Wang, the wife of Yang Chunfang, was from Tongliang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, wife of Yang Chunfang, was from Tongliang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，其家火，春芳臥病，王入戶，負以行。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong fire broke out at their home; Chunfang lay ill; Wang entered the room and carried him on her back as she went out.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 17 their house burned; she carried the ailing Chunfang out.

sentences.zh: 火逼不能出，子女奔赴，皆死。

translations.literal: The fire pressed close and they could not get out; sons and daughters rushed to help and all died.
translations.idiomatic: Flames blocked the way; children rushed in and all perished.

sentences.zh: 王尊德妾唐，臨桂人。

translations.literal: Tang, concubine of Wang Zunde, was from Lingui.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was Zunde's concubine, a native of Lingui.

sentences.zh: 尊德年八十，病劇，鄰家火，唐欲負以避，力不勝。

translations.literal: Zunde was eighty and gravely ill; a neighbor's house caught fire; Tang wished to carry him on her back to escape but lacked the strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zunde was eighty and dying; when a neighbor's house burned she tried to carry him but could not.

sentences.zh: 火迫，尊德揮使出，唐身翼蔽尊德，皆死。

translations.literal: The fire pressed close; Zunde waved her out; Tang shielded Zunde with her body and both died.
translations.idiomatic: He sent her out; she shielded him with her body; both died.

sentences.zh: 竇鴻妾郝，字湘娥，保定人。

translations.literal: Hao, concubine of Dou Hong, style Xiang'e, was from Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Xiang'e, concubine of Dou Hong, was from Baoding.

sentences.zh: 十六為鴻妾，能詩善弈，畫兼工花草、士女。

translations.literal: At sixteen she became Hong's concubine; she could compose poetry and was skilled at chess; her painting excelled at flowers and grasses and figures.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen she entered his household, wrote poetry, played chess, and painted flowers and figures.

sentences.zh: 有繩其才者，豪家謀奪之，不能。

translations.literal: Some envied her talent; a powerful family plotted to seize her but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Envious of her gifts, a powerful house tried to take her and failed.

sentences.zh: 嗾盜誣鴻死，湘娥因自經。

translations.literal: They incited bandits to frame Hong for death; Xiang'e therefore hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: They set bandits to frame Hong; Xiang'e hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 將死，為絕命詞，矢為厲以報。

translations.literal: About to die she composed a death poem and vowed to become a vengeful ghost.
translations.idiomatic: She wrote a death poem and swore to haunt them as a ghost.

sentences.zh: 章學閔妻董，名合珠，連江人。

translations.literal: Dong, the wife of Zhang Xueyin, named Hezhu, was from Lianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hezhu, wife of Zhang Xueyin, was from Lianjiang.

sentences.zh: 故為婢，嫁學閔。

translations.literal: She had formerly been a maidservant and married Xueyin.
translations.idiomatic: Once a maidservant, she married Xueyin.

sentences.zh: 學閔貧不自聊，走死深山中。

translations.literal: Xueyin, poor and unable to support himself, went off and died in the deep mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Destitute, Xueyin wandered into the mountains and died.

sentences.zh: 董號泣求之，不知其存亡。

translations.literal: Dong wailed and sought him, not knowing whether he was alive or dead.
translations.idiomatic: Dong searched wailing, not knowing if he lived.

sentences.zh: 逾年，有樵入山，若有聲䰰䰰，行見遺骼委於地，只履在側。

translations.literal: After more than a year a woodcutter entered the mountains; if there was a sound rustling, he went and saw scattered bones on the ground with a single shoe at the side.
translations.idiomatic: A year later a woodcutter heard rustling in the hills and found bones and one shoe.

sentences.zh: 出以語人，董聞曰：「得非吾夫乎？

translations.literal: He came out and told people; when Dong heard she said, "Could this be my husband?"
translations.idiomatic: He told others; Dong said, "Could that be my husband?"

sentences.zh: 」亟往視履，其手製也，拾餘骨瘞焉，即夕自經死。

translations.literal: " She hastened to look at the shoe—it was of her own making; she gathered the remaining bones and buried them, and that very night hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: The shoe was her handiwork; she buried the bones and hanged herself that night.

sentences.zh: 杜聶齊妻何，聶齊，泰宁人；

translations.literal: He, the wife of Du Nieqi—Nieqi was from Taining;
translations.idiomatic: He, wife of Du Nieqi: Nieqi was from Taining;

sentences.zh: 何，將樂人。

translations.literal: He was from Jiangle.
translations.idiomatic: She was a native of Jiangle.

sentences.zh: 聶齊死於虎，何求得屍，解衣拭其血。

translations.literal: Nieqi died from a tiger; He obtained the corpse and removed her garment to wipe away its blood.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger killed Nieqi; He found the body and wiped the blood with her own clothes.

sentences.zh: 斂畢，斥家財以葬，悉以其餘分戚族，遂自經。

translations.literal: When the encoffining was finished she spent the family wealth on burial, distributed all that remained among kin, and then hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: She buried him at her expense, gave the rest to kin, and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 張氏婦，宿州人。

translations.literal: A woman of the Zhang clan, from Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhang-clan wife, from Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 夫樵於野，遇狼，為所噬。

translations.literal: Her husband gathered firewood in the wild and met a wolf that devoured him.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband was gathering firewood when a wolf killed him.

sentences.zh: 婦求得夫屍，以鐮絕脰死。

translations.literal: The wife obtained her husband's corpse and cut her throat with a sickle.
translations.idiomatic: She found his body and cut her throat with a sickle.

sentences.zh: 寧化二婦，不知其氏。

translations.literal: Two women of Ninghua—their surnames are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Two women of Ninghua, surnames unknown.

sentences.zh: 其一，夫嗜博，母閉諸室中，不與飲食，婦導使出亡。

translations.literal: Of the first, the husband was addicted to gambling; the mother shut him in a room and gave him no food or drink; the wife guided him out to escape.
translations.idiomatic: One husband gambled; his mother starved him in a room; his wife helped him escape.

sentences.zh: 既，夫死於途，婦聞，自殺。

translations.literal: Afterward the husband died on the road; when the wife heard she killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the road; hearing of it, she killed herself.

sentences.zh: 其一，夫行竊，父將殺之，婦泣為請免。

translations.literal: Of the other, the husband stole; the father was about to kill him and the wife wept begging that he be spared.
translations.idiomatic: The other husband stole; his father meant to kill him; his wife begged for his life.

sentences.zh: 生二子，婦攜就母家，父卒殺其夫，婦聞，亦自殺。

translations.literal: She bore two sons; the wife took them to her mother's home; the father still killed her husband; when the wife heard she also killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two sons and fled to her mother's house; her father-in-law still killed him; she killed herself on hearing it.
